reports.lens: Exact money, precision and currency across `sal.*` and `wty.*` (P1-11 protected schema, migrations `20260724090000`–`20260724095000`), read at `d9a2c1dc8d09e8fe2b3cf9ca8a2d4a6c905756de` with 119 migrations and no migration 120.
reports.summary: Money in `sal.*` is `numeric(18,4)` on exactly eleven columns and nowhere else; `wty.*` contains ZERO monetary columns of any kind. The enforced bounds are therefore 14 integer digits and exactly 4 decimal places — anything wider raises `22003 numeric_value_out_of_range`, which is not a `check_violation` and will surface as a 500 unless the API rejects it first. Zero is legal on the invoice totals, the line amounts and the event ledger (`>= 0`), and illegal on receipts, allocations, credit notes and reversals (`> 0`); negatives are legal NOWHERE, so there is no signed amount anywhere in the domain and `sal.financial_events` has no debit/credit/direction column at all — direction is implied only by `event_type`. Currency is `currency_code text NOT NULL` with an `ON DELETE RESTRICT` FK to `shared.currencies (code)` on seven tables, with NO default anywhere in `sal`/`wty` (the only hard-coded currency default in the whole database is `qms.rework_link_details.cost_currency DEFAULT 'JOD'`, deliberately outside this domain). The two restricted money detail tables carry no currency column of their own, so every amount they hold is currency-less until joined to its parent. Crucially, the P1-11 handoff prose claims currency coherence "is enforced (M-fin-4)" — the DDL says otherwise: credit-note↔invoice and reversal↔receipt currency equality is enforced by NOTHING, and allocation↔receipt↔invoice equality lives only inside `sal.allocate_receipt` while `app_runtime` holds raw INSERT on `sal.payment_allocations`. Two currencies can therefore meet in one aggregate, and `sal.partner_outstanding_balance(uuid)` actively does it: it loops every issued invoice for a partner with no currency filter and returns one unlabelled scalar. There is no `GENERATED` money column anywhere in `sal`/`wty` (only `seq bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY`), so unlike P1-21's inventory nothing is derived by PostgreSQL — every total is application-written and only reconciled after the fact by CHECKs and one deferred constraint trigger. `pg@^8.22.0` returns `numeric` (OID 1700) as a string and no `setTypeParser` call exists in the repository, so exact decimal strings cross the driver boundary intact.

findings.fact: Money is numeric(18,4) on exactly eleven columns across four tables, and on no other column in sal or wty. The enforced bound is 14 integer digits and exactly 4 decimal places: magnitude ceiling 99999999999999.9999.
findings.evidence: `net_total numeric(18, 4) NOT NULL`, `tax_total numeric(18, 4) NOT NULL`, `gross_total numeric(18, 4) NOT NULL` (20260724091000 L167-169); `unit_price numeric(18, 4) NOT NULL … warranty_pay_amount numeric(18, 4) NOT NULL` (L331-336); `amount numeric(18, 4) NOT NULL` (20260724092000 L84, L191, L279, L340; 20260724093000 L31).
findings.consequence: The API boundary must reject any amount with more than 4 decimal places or more than 14 integer digits BEFORE it reaches SQL. Exceeding precision raises SQLSTATE `22003` (`numeric field overflow`), a driver-level error that is NOT `23514` and does not map to a validation failure; exceeding scale is NOT an error at all — PostgreSQL silently rounds to 4 dp (half away from zero) on the cast to typmod. Use `Decimal.parse(value, MONEY)` from `src/modules/pricing/domain/decimal.ts` (precision 18, scale 4), which already refuses both.

findings.fact: Quantity is numeric(12,3) and must be strictly positive; zero quantity is illegal. Bounds: 0.001 .. 999999999.999.
findings.evidence: `quantity numeric(12, 3) NOT NULL,` and `CONSTRAINT ck_invoice_lines_quantity CHECK (quantity > 0)` (20260724091000 L243, L267).
findings.consequence: Reuse the existing `QUANTITY` spec (`{precision:12, scale:3}`) and `parsePositive()` from `src/modules/pricing/domain/decimal.ts`. This matches `quo.quotation_items.captured_quantity` exactly, so a quotation quantity transcribes to an invoice line without rescaling.

findings.fact: Zero is legal on the invoice header totals, the line amounts and the event ledger, and ILLEGAL on every payment instrument. Negatives are legal on no monetary column anywhere in sal or wty.
findings.identifier: ck_invoice_amounts_nonneg; ck_invoice_line_amounts_nonneg; ck_financial_events_amount; ck_receipts_amount; ck_payment_allocations_amount; ck_credit_notes_amount; ck_receipt_reversals_amount
findings.evidence: `CONSTRAINT ck_invoice_amounts_nonneg CHECK (net_total >= 0 AND tax_total >= 0 AND gross_total >= 0)`; `CONSTRAINT ck_invoice_line_amounts_nonneg CHECK (unit_price >= 0 AND net_amount >= 0 AND tax_amount >= 0 AND gross_amount >= 0 AND customer_pay_amount >= 0 AND warranty_pay_amount >= 0)`; `CONSTRAINT ck_financial_events_amount CHECK (amount >= 0)`; against `CONSTRAINT ck_receipts_amount CHECK (amount > 0)`, `CONSTRAINT ck_payment_allocations_amount CHECK (amount > 0)`, `CONSTRAINT ck_credit_notes_amount CHECK (amount > 0)`, `CONSTRAINT ck_receipt_reversals_amount CHECK (amount > 0)`.
findings.consequence: Two distinct API validators are required, not one: `>= 0` for invoice/line/event amounts, `> 0` for receipt, allocation, credit-note and reversal amounts. A zero-value issued invoice IS legal (`sal.issue_invoice` only requires `v_lines = 0` to fail), and it can never be allocated against because `sal.allocate_receipt` rejects `p_amount <= 0` and also rejects `p_amount > v_open` where `v_open` is 0. There is no negative-amount representation: a credit is a separate positive-amount `sal.credit_notes` row, never a negative invoice line.

findings.fact: sal.financial_events has NO debit/credit, sign, direction or account column. Amount is unsigned and direction is implied solely by event_type.
findings.evidence: Column list is `event_type, source_type, source_id, currency_code, amount, occurred_at, actor_id, correlation_id, idempotency_key, seq` with `CHECK (amount >= 0)`. Table comment: 'The future accounting integration point (Figure 4.29) — NOT a general ledger: no debit/credit/account columns.'
findings.consequence: Any P1-22 read model or report that sums `sal.financial_events.amount` across event types produces a meaningless number. Every aggregate must partition by `event_type` first, and the sign convention (issuance increases receivable; receipt/allocation/credit/reversal reduce it) is application knowledge that exists nowhere in the schema.

findings.fact: The full event vocabulary is six values and the source vocabulary is five; both are closed CHECKs, and the ledger is single-use per (source, event_type).
findings.evidence: `CHECK (event_type IN ('invoice_issued', 'receipt_recorded', 'payment_allocated', 'credit_note_issued', 'receipt_reversed', 'warranty_split_recorded'))`; `CHECK (source_type IN ('invoice', 'receipt', 'payment_allocation', 'credit_note', 'receipt_reversal'))`; `CONSTRAINT uq_financial_events_source UNIQUE (tenant_id, source_type, source_id, event_type)`.
findings.consequence: These six strings are the complete legal event vocabulary — the backend transcribes them and invents none. A replayed command hits `23505` on `uq_financial_events_source`. Note `invoice_issued` and `warranty_split_recorded` share `source_type = 'invoice'` and are distinguished only by `event_type`.

findings.fact: Every event's amount and currency are hard-bound to its source row by a BEFORE INSERT provenance guard, with exact numeric inequality.
findings.evidence: `IF NEW.amount <> v_amount THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'sal.financial_events: amount % does not bind the source amount %' … USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation'; END IF; IF NEW.currency_code <> v_currency THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'sal.financial_events: currency % does not bind the source currency %' …`
findings.consequence: The backend never chooses an event amount or currency — it is the source row's own value, and any drift fails with `23514`. For `warranty_split_recorded` the bound amount is `COALESCE(sum(la.warranty_pay_amount), 0)` over the invoice's non-deleted line amounts, and the currency is `i.currency_code` (the invoice header), NOT any column on the amount tables.

findings.fact: currency_code is text NOT NULL with an ON DELETE RESTRICT FK to shared.currencies(code) on seven tables, and has NO DEFAULT anywhere in sal or wty.
findings.identifier: fk_invoices_currency; fk_invoice_lines_currency; fk_receipts_currency; fk_payment_allocations_currency; fk_credit_notes_currency; fk_receipt_reversals_currency; fk_financial_events_currency
findings.evidence: Seven identical clauses of the form `CONSTRAINT fk_invoices_currency FOREIGN KEY (currency_code) REFERENCES shared.currencies (code) ON DELETE RESTRICT` (20260724091000 L64, L265; 20260724092000 L108, L205, L298, L361; 20260724093000 L44).
findings.consequence: Currency is mandatory on every currency-bearing write and must be an existing `shared.currencies.code`; an unseeded code fails with `23503`, not `23514`. There is no application, tenant, company or jurisdiction default currency to fall back on — the caller must state it. `org.legal_companies.base_currency_code` exists but NOTHING in sal/wty reads or checks against it.

findings.fact: The two restricted money detail tables carry no currency column of their own. Their amounts are currency-less until joined to the parent.
findings.evidence: `sal.invoice_amounts` column list is `id, tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, invoice_id, net_total, tax_total, gross_total, classification, record_version, …` — no `currency_code`. `sal.invoice_line_amounts` is `… invoice_line_id, invoice_id, unit_price, net_amount, tax_amount, gross_amount, customer_pay_amount, warranty_pay_amount, classification, …` — no `currency_code`.
findings.consequence: Every money projection must join `sal.invoices.currency_code` (header) or `sal.invoice_lines.currency_code` (line) to render `{ amount, currency }`. Rendering a `sal.invoice_amounts` row alone would emit an amount with no currency — exactly the class of bug `src/modules/pricing/domain/money.ts` was written to make unexpressible.

findings.fact: Line currency must equal the header currency, enforced by a trigger, and the header currency freezes at issue.
findings.evidence: `IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sal.invoices i WHERE … AND i.currency_code = NEW.currency_code) THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'sal.invoice_lines: line currency must match the invoice header currency' USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation';` and, post-draft, `OR NEW.currency_code <> OLD.currency_code THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'sal.invoices: an issued invoice''s number/issue/source/currency are frozen'`.
findings.consequence: A single invoice can never be multi-currency: one header currency governs all its lines. The backend sets the currency once at draft creation and never sends it on a line-create command — it is redundant and any mismatch fails with `23514`.

findings.fact: There is exactly ONE arithmetic identity on money in the whole domain — gross = round(net + tax, 4) — applied at three layers, plus one payer-split identity.
findings.evidence: `CONSTRAINT ck_invoice_amounts_gross CHECK (gross_total = round(net_total + tax_total, 4))`; `CONSTRAINT ck_invoice_line_amounts_gross CHECK (gross_amount = round(net_amount + tax_amount, 4))`; `CONSTRAINT ck_invoice_line_amounts_payer_split CHECK (customer_pay_amount + warranty_pay_amount = gross_amount)`.
findings.consequence: These are the only money identities the database will enforce on a write. Note the payer split is exact equality with NO `round()` — correct, because the sum of two scale-4 numerics is already exactly scale 4. `customer_pay_amount + warranty_pay_amount = gross_amount` means the warranty share is per-line and total, never a percentage; the API must accept both components and reject any pair that does not sum exactly.

findings.fact: The rounding convention enforced by the schema is PostgreSQL round(numeric, 4), i.e. half away from zero at scale 4. Because every amount is non-negative this is unconditionally half-up.
findings.identifier: round(net_total + tax_total, 4) in ck_invoice_amounts_gross; round(v_net + v_tax, 4) in sal.issue_invoice; round(v_gross - v_alloc - v_credit, 4) in sal.invoice_open_receivable; round(v_amount - v_alloc, 4) in sal.receipt_unallocated; round(v_total, 4) in sal.partner_outstanding_balance
findings.evidence: `UPDATE sal.invoice_amounts SET net_total = v_net, tax_total = v_tax, gross_total = round(v_net + v_tax, 4)`; `RETURN round(v_gross - v_alloc - v_credit, 4);`.
findings.consequence: Any TypeScript rounding P1-22 introduces must be half-away-from-zero at scale 4 — NOT banker's rounding, NOT `toFixed` (which is IEEE-754 and can round 1.005 down). Since all amounts are `>= 0`, half-up is the exact equivalent.

findings.fact: Header totals are recomputed from the lines by the issue primitive itself, so the backend does not have to compute them — and cannot make them stick if it computes them wrongly.
findings.identifier: sal.issue_invoice(p_invoice_id uuid, p_correlation_id uuid DEFAULT NULL) RETURNS text
findings.evidence: `SELECT count(*)::int, COALESCE(sum(la.net_amount), 0), COALESCE(sum(la.tax_amount), 0), COALESCE(sum(la.gross_amount), 0), COALESCE(sum(la.warranty_pay_amount), 0) INTO v_lines, v_net, v_tax, v_gross, v_wty …` then `UPDATE sal.invoice_amounts SET net_total = v_net, tax_total = v_tax, gross_total = round(v_net + v_tax, 4) …; IF NOT FOUND THEN INSERT INTO sal.invoice_amounts (…) VALUES (…, v_net, v_tax, round(v_net + v_tax, 4), v_actor); END IF;`
findings.consequence: P1-22 may skip creating `sal.invoice_amounts` on the draft entirely — `sal.issue_invoice` inserts it if absent, while the invoice is still `draft` (before the status flip), so `tg_invoice_amounts_frozen` permits it. Any header total the backend wrote beforehand is overwritten. It is a sum over line amounts joined on `invoice_line_id` with `l.deleted_at IS NULL AND la.deleted_at IS NULL`, so a soft-deleted line silently leaves the total.

findings.fact: Header↔line reconciliation is a DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED constraint trigger that fires only for a non-draft invoice, and it compares with plain numeric inequality.
findings.evidence: `CREATE CONSTRAINT TRIGGER tg_invoice_line_amounts_reconcile AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON sal.invoice_line_amounts DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED FOR EACH ROW …`; inside: `IF v_status IS NULL OR v_status = 'draft' THEN RETURN NULL; -- draft assembly or teardown` and `IF v_hnet <> v_net OR v_htax <> v_tax OR v_hgross <> v_gross THEN RAISE EXCEPTION … USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation';`
findings.consequence: The reconciliation failure surfaces at COMMIT, not at statement time — the backend's transaction wrapper must map a commit-time `23514` to a domain failure, not to a generic 500. Tests that need it early must `SET CONSTRAINTS ALL IMMEDIATE` (as `tests/db/p1-11-precision.test.ts` does). Numeric `<>` ignores trailing-zero dscale differences, so `1.5` and `1.5000` reconcile.

findings.fact: There is NO GENERATED money column anywhere in sal or wty. The only GENERATED columns are identity sequences.
findings.identifier: seq bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY on sal.invoice_status_history, sal.payment_allocations, sal.financial_events, sal.delivery_status_history, wty.warranty_status_history
findings.evidence: Grepping `GENERATED` across all six P1-11 migrations returns only `seq bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY` (five occurrences) — no `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (...) STORED` exists in sal or wty.
findings.consequence: Unlike P1-21's inventory (`signed_qty`, `available_qty` both `GENERATED`), NOTHING monetary is derived by PostgreSQL here. Every amount is application-written and only checked after the fact. The nearest GENERATED column P1-22 touches is `veh.odometer_readings.value_km numeric(14,4) GENERATED ALWAYS AS (CASE unit WHEN 'km' THEN value WHEN 'mi' THEN round(value * 1.609344, 4) END) STORED`, reached through `sal.complete_delivery`.

findings.fact: Balances are derived by three SECURITY INVOKER functions with a bare `numeric` return type; the value carries dscale 4 from the final round().
findings.identifier: sal.invoice_open_receivable(p_invoice_id uuid) RETURNS numeric; sal.receipt_unallocated(p_receipt_id uuid) RETURNS numeric; sal.partner_outstanding_balance(p_partner_id uuid) RETURNS numeric
findings.evidence: `GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION sal.invoice_open_receivable(uuid) TO app_runtime, app_readonly;` — likewise for the other two. Body: `RETURN round(v_gross - v_alloc - v_credit, 4);`
findings.consequence: All three are granted to `app_readonly` as well as `app_runtime`, so a reporting path can call them. `pg` returns the result as a string with four decimal places; read it with `::text` for explicitness (the house pattern in `src/modules/pricing/data/pricing-repository.ts`) and wrap with `Decimal.fromDatabase(value, MONEY)`.

findings.fact: The reversed-receipt exclusion is real and asymmetric: invoice open receivable drops allocations of reversed receipts, receipt-unallocated does not filter them but short-circuits on a reversed receipt.
findings.evidence: open receivable: `… FROM sal.payment_allocations pa JOIN sal.receipts r ON … WHERE pa.tenant_id = v_tenant AND pa.invoice_id = p_invoice_id AND r.status <> 'reversed';` — unallocated: `IF v_amount IS NULL OR v_status = 'reversed' THEN RETURN 0; END IF;` then an unfiltered `sum(amount)`.
findings.consequence: Reversing a receipt automatically re-opens the receivable on every invoice it paid, with no allocation row deleted (append-only). A reversed receipt reports zero unallocated. P1-22 must never cache or store either value without invalidating on `receipt_reversed`.

findings.fact: Receipt allocation is the ONE place currency coherence is checked, and it is checked inside the function only.
findings.identifier: sal.allocate_receipt(p_receipt_id uuid, p_invoice_id uuid, p_amount numeric, p_correlation_id uuid DEFAULT NULL)
findings.evidence: `IF v_inv.currency_code <> v_rcpt.currency_code THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'sal.allocate_receipt: invoice currency % <> receipt currency %', v_inv.currency_code, v_rcpt.currency_code USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation'; END IF;` and the insert uses `v_rcpt.currency_code`, never a caller-supplied code.
findings.consequence: P1-22 must call `sal.allocate_receipt` and must NEVER raw-INSERT into `sal.payment_allocations` — the grant permits it (`GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON sal.payment_allocations TO app_runtime`) but no constraint or trigger reproduces the currency check. The function also takes locks in the fixed order receipt → invoice; the backend must not invert it.

findings.fact: The primitives accept bare `numeric` parameters with no typmod, so a caller can hand them a sub-scale amount that is silently rounded on storage.
findings.identifier: sal.record_receipt(uuid, uuid, uuid, uuid, text, numeric, uuid, text, uuid); sal.allocate_receipt(uuid, uuid, numeric, uuid); sal.complete_delivery(uuid, numeric, text, uuid)
findings.evidence: `p_currency_code text, p_amount numeric, p_evidence_document_version_id uuid DEFAULT NULL` (record_receipt); `p_amount numeric` (allocate_receipt); `p_final_odometer_value numeric, p_odometer_unit text DEFAULT 'km'` (complete_delivery).
findings.consequence: An amount of `10.00004` is stored as `10.0000` with no error. The API boundary is the ONLY place sub-scale precision loss can be refused, so `Decimal.parse(value, MONEY)` must run on every inbound amount. Over-allocation cannot be produced by rounding — `allocate_receipt` compares the UNROUNDED `p_amount` against `v_unalloc`/`v_open` before the cast — but a legitimate amount can still be quietly truncated.

findings.fact: Receipt money freezes on the row the moment it is recorded; only status may advance, and only through an approved reversal.
findings.evidence: `IF NEW.amount <> OLD.amount OR NEW.currency_code <> OLD.currency_code OR NEW.payment_method_id <> OLD.payment_method_id OR NEW.payer_partner_id <> OLD.payer_partner_id OR NEW.received_at IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.received_at OR NEW.receipt_number <> OLD.receipt_number THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'sal.receipts: a recorded receipt''s amount/method/payer/currency/received_at/number are frozen (corrections via reversal only)'`; `CHECK (status IN ('recorded', 'partially_allocated', 'allocated', 'reversed'))`.
findings.consequence: There is no receipt-edit operation to build. A wrong amount is corrected by a full-receipt reversal (`uq_receipt_reversals_receipt UNIQUE (tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, original_receipt_id)` — at most one per receipt, always the full amount) plus a new receipt. Partial reversal is unrepresentable.

findings.fact: Invoice and line money freeze the moment the invoice leaves draft, via three separate guards; the generic immutable-column guard does NOT cover the amount columns.
findings.evidence: `IF v_status <> 'draft' THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'sal.invoice_amounts: parent invoice is % (not draft); header totals are frozen', v_status USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation';` — while `tg_invoice_amounts_immutable … org.guard_immutable_columns('tenant_id', 'company_id', 'branch_id', 'invoice_id', 'classification', 'created_at', 'created_by')` names no amount column.
findings.consequence: All money editing must happen while `sal.invoices.status = 'draft'`. After issue the only monetary movement is a credit note or an allocation. `sal.guard_invoice_line_amount_frozen` additionally enforces `l.invoice_id = NEW.invoice_id` (L-fin-4), so the denormalized `invoice_id` on a line amount must equal its parent line's — mismatch is `23503`.

findings.fact: Every INSERT of a money-bearing row is gated by iam.has_permission('sal.finance.view') inside the RLS policy, including the financial_events insert that every primitive performs.
findings.identifier: ins_invoice_amounts_gated; ins_invoice_line_amounts_gated; ins_receipts_gated; ins_payment_allocations_gated; ins_credit_notes_gated; ins_receipt_reversals_gated; ins_financial_events_gated
findings.evidence: `CREATE POLICY ins_financial_events_gated ON sal.financial_events FOR INSERT TO app_runtime WITH CHECK (tenant_id = iam.current_tenant_id() AND iam.has_permission('sal.finance.view') AND …)` — the same predicate on all seven.
findings.consequence: Because every primitive is `SECURITY INVOKER` and RLS is `FORCE` on all seven tables, the ACTING USER must hold `sal.finance.view` to record a receipt, allocate, credit, reverse, or issue an invoice — `sal.payment.record` / `sal.invoice.issue` alone are NOT sufficient. P1-22's role composition must pair each write permission with `sal.finance.view` or every write fails on the RLS WITH CHECK (which surfaces as `42501`-flavoured 'new row violates row-level security policy', not a permission error the API generated).

findings.fact: Reading a money row is likewise gated, but the structural rows around it are not — quantity is visible without finance permission while unit price is not.
findings.evidence: `CREATE POLICY sel_invoice_lines_scope ON sal.invoice_lines FOR SELECT TO app_runtime, app_readonly USING (tenant_id = iam.current_tenant_id() AND …)` — no permission predicate; against `CREATE POLICY sel_invoice_line_amounts_gated … USING (tenant_id = iam.current_tenant_id() AND iam.has_permission('sal.finance.view') AND …)`.
findings.consequence: A non-finance caller legitimately sees invoice structure (line number, type, quantity, currency, tax class, source refs) and sees NO amounts at all — not a masked zero, but zero rows from the join. The invoice-read API must render two distinct shapes rather than nulling fields, and must not infer 'unpaid' from an empty amounts join.

findings.fact: The full permission catalog for this domain is eleven codes, already seeded; nothing monetary is missing but nothing extra exists either.
findings.identifier: sal.invoice.manage, sal.invoice.issue, sal.payment.record, sal.payment.allocate, sal.credit.manage, sal.reversal.approve, sal.finance.view, sal.delivery.manage, sal.delivery.complete, sal.delivery.view, wty.policy.manage, wty.warranty.issue
findings.evidence: `('sal.finance.view', 'sal', 'View financial amounts (invoices/receipts/events)', 'high', …)`, `('sal.credit.manage', 'sal', 'Request and manage credit notes', 'high', …)`, `('sal.reversal.approve', 'sal', 'Approve receipt reversals (dual control)', 'high', …)` in supabase/seeds/04_iam_permission_catalog.sql L60-73.
findings.consequence: There is NO `sal.credit.approve` — `sal.credit.manage` covers both request and approval, with the maker≠approver separation enforced by `sal.guard_dual_control_approval()` at the row level rather than by two permissions. New codes should be added only where none of these eleven carries the meaning.

findings.fact: Dual-control approval freezes the amount as part of the decision, and rejects self-approval at two layers.
findings.evidence: `ELSIF OLD.approval_state <> 'pending' THEN IF NEW.approval_state <> OLD.approval_state OR NEW.requested_by <> OLD.requested_by OR NEW.approved_by IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.approved_by OR NEW.amount <> OLD.amount THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'dual control: a % decision is frozen'` plus `CHECK (approved_by IS NULL OR approved_by <> requested_by)`.
findings.consequence: The credit-note amount is settable only while `approval_state = 'pending'`; approval is a state transition, never an amount edit. `sal.stamp_dual_control_maker()` overwrites any client-supplied `requested_by` with `iam.current_user_id()` and nulls `approved_by`/`approved_at`, so the API must not accept those three fields at all.

findings.fact: Credit is bounded by the derived open receivable under the invoice lock, and the bound is checked in the same numeric scale.
findings.identifier: sal.approve_credit_note(p_credit_id uuid, p_correlation_id uuid DEFAULT NULL)
findings.evidence: `PERFORM 1 FROM sal.invoices WHERE id = v_cn.invoice_id … FOR UPDATE; v_open := sal.invoice_open_receivable(v_cn.invoice_id); IF v_cn.amount > v_open THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'sal.approve_credit_note: credit % exceeds invoice open receivable %', v_cn.amount, v_open USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation'; END IF;`
findings.consequence: Open receivable can never be driven negative by a credit. The backend must never pre-check the bound itself and then approve — it calls the primitive, which locks first. The function is idempotent on an already-approved credit (`IF v_cn.approval_state = 'approved' THEN RETURN;`).

findings.fact: wty.* contains ZERO monetary and ZERO rate columns. The only numbers in warranty are integers: duration in months and an unlabelled odometer.
findings.identifier: wty.warranty_coverage.{duration_months integer, odometer_limit integer}; wty.warranty_records.{odometer_at_issue integer, odometer_limit integer}
findings.evidence: `duration_months integer NOT NULL, odometer_limit integer NULL` with `CONSTRAINT ck_warranty_coverage_duration CHECK (duration_months > 0)` and `CONSTRAINT ck_warranty_coverage_odometer CHECK (odometer_limit IS NULL OR odometer_limit > 0)`; `odometer_at_issue integer NOT NULL, odometer_limit integer NULL` with `CONSTRAINT ck_warranty_records_odometer CHECK (odometer_at_issue >= 0 AND (odometer_limit IS NULL OR odometer_limit >= odometer_at_issue))`.
findings.consequence: Warranty carries no money. The ONLY monetary expression of warranty in the entire database is `sal.invoice_line_amounts.warranty_pay_amount numeric(18,4)` and the `warranty_split_recorded` financial event derived from its sum. Any P1-22 warranty API that returns an amount must source it from the invoice side; a warranty record itself has no value, no reserve, and no claim amount.

findings.fact: Warranty duration and expiry are computed by interval arithmetic on a date, with no duration column on the record.
findings.identifier: wty.issue_warranty(p_delivery_id uuid, p_policy_id uuid, p_correlation_id uuid DEFAULT NULL, p_idempotency_key text DEFAULT NULL) RETURNS uuid
findings.evidence: `(v_start + (v_cov.duration_months || ' months')::interval)::date` for `expiry_date`, and `CASE WHEN v_cov.odometer_limit IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE v_odo + v_cov.odometer_limit END` for the record's `odometer_limit`, with `CONSTRAINT ck_warranty_records_dates CHECK (expiry_date > start_date)`.
findings.consequence: The record's `odometer_limit` is ABSOLUTE (issue reading + coverage allowance), while the coverage's `odometer_limit` is a DELTA. Two identically-named columns with different meanings — the API must not conflate them. `start_date` is `v_del.delivered_at::date`, a timestamptz cast to date in the SESSION time zone, so the effective-date coverage lookup is time-zone sensitive.

findings.fact: pg returns numeric as a string and the repository never overrides that; the existing decimal helpers already encode the exact protected scales.
findings.identifier: pg ^8.22.0; src/modules/pricing/domain/decimal.ts MONEY/QUANTITY/TAX_RATE specs; src/modules/pricing/domain/money.ts Money/MoneyView
findings.evidence: `"pg": "^8.22.0"` in package.json; no `setTypeParser` call exists anywhere in src/, scripts/ or tests/ (only comments referencing it). `export const MONEY: DecimalSpec = Object.freeze({ precision: 18, scale: 4, label: 'money' });`
findings.consequence: P1-22 reuses `Decimal`/`Money`/`moneyView` unchanged and reads every money column with an explicit `::text` cast (the pattern in `src/modules/pricing/data/pricing-repository.ts`), so a future `setTypeParser(1700, parseFloat)` cannot silently turn a P1-22 amount into a float. Never use `parseFloat`, `Number`, `toFixed` or `Math.round` on an authoritative money path.

findings.fact: A structural CI invariant pins the precision contract across sal/wty/rpt and will fail if it is ever widened.
findings.evidence: `SELECT … FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = ANY($1) AND data_type IN ('real','double precision')` asserted `toEqual([])`, and `WHERE … data_type='numeric' AND numeric_scale=4` asserted `numeric_precision` `toBe(18)` — with `const SCHEMAS = ['sal', 'wty', 'rpt']`.
findings.consequence: Any scale-4 numeric added to sal/wty/rpt must be precision 18 or this test fails. P1-22 adds no migration so it cannot break this, but the test is the mechanical statement of the money-type contract and should be cited as the evidence, not re-asserted in prose.

gaps.assumed: `sal.payment_allocations` rows are always currency-coherent because `sal.allocate_receipt` checks.
gaps.reality: `GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON sal.payment_allocations TO app_runtime` — the runtime role holds raw INSERT, and the table has NO trigger at all except the deferred `tg_payment_allocations_event_completeness`, which only demands that a `payment_allocated` event exist. `sal.guard_financial_event_provenance` binds the event's currency to the ALLOCATION's own `currency_code` (`SELECT amount, currency_code INTO v_amount, v_currency FROM sal.payment_allocations`), not to the receipt's or the invoice's — so a raw INSERT with a mismatched currency plus a matching event passes every check.
gaps.mitigation: P1-22 routes 100% of allocation writes through `sal.allocate_receipt(uuid, uuid, numeric, uuid)` and never raw-INSERTs `sal.payment_allocations`. Enforce this with a repository-layer rule (single code path) and a structural test asserting no `INSERT INTO sal.payment_allocations` string exists outside the primitive call.

gaps.assumed: `receipt_reversal.currency = receipt.currency` is guaranteed.
gaps.reality: `sal.approve_receipt_reversal` checks the AMOUNT only: `IF v_rev.amount <> v_rcpt.amount THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'sal.approve_receipt_reversal: full-receipt reversal amount % must equal receipt amount %'`. There is no currency comparison in the function, and no trigger or CHECK on `sal.receipt_reversals` references `sal.receipts.currency_code`.
gaps.mitigation: P1-22 sets `receipt_reversals.currency_code` from the receipt row it just read, never from client input, and asserts equality before INSERT. Practically the blast radius is small (amount equality plus one-reversal-per-receipt), but the field is client-writable and must not be trusted.

gaps.assumed: A line's money is arithmetically tied to its unit price and quantity, the way `quo.quotation_items` is.
gaps.reality: There is NO such identity. `quo.quotation_items` carries `CONSTRAINT ck_quotation_items_line_total CHECK (captured_line_total = round(captured_unit_price * captured_quantity - captured_discount + captured_tax_amount, 4))`. `sal.invoice_line_amounts` has only `ck_invoice_line_amounts_nonneg`, `ck_invoice_line_amounts_gross`, `ck_invoice_line_amounts_payer_split`, `ck_invoice_line_amounts_classification` — nothing relating `net_amount` to `unit_price`. It could not: `quantity` lives on `sal.invoice_lines` and `unit_price` on `sal.invoice_line_amounts`, two different tables. The database will accept `unit_price = 1.0000`, `quantity = 100.000`, `net_amount = 999999.0000`.
gaps.mitigation: P1-22 owns the per-line identity entirely in the application: compute `net_amount` and validate `net_amount = round(unit_price * quantity - discount, 4)` before writing both rows in one transaction. Because both writes must succeed together and `tg_invoice_line_amounts_frozen` demands the parent be draft, the line and its amount detail must be inserted in the same transaction under the same draft invoice.

gaps.assumed: An invoice line's tax can be recomputed or audited from what the schema stores.
gaps.reality: `sal.invoice_lines.tax_class_id uuid NULL` is the ONLY tax reference, it is NULLABLE, and its FK is `fk_invoice_lines_tax_class → org.tax_classes (tenant_id, company_id, id)`. There is NO rate column anywhere in `sal.*` — no `captured_tax_rate`, no `tax_rate`, no reference to `org.tax_rates`. Nothing validates `tax_amount` against any rate. Contrast `quo.quotation_items.captured_tax_rate numeric(9,6) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` with `ck_quotation_items_tax_amount CHECK (captured_tax_amount = round((captured_unit_price * captured_quantity - captured_discount) * captured_tax_rate, 4))`. Additionally `org.tax_rates` is seeded with ZERO rows by policy ("ZERO rows are seeded: every rate is tenant configuration … OIR-04 (jurisdiction policy) remains OPEN").
gaps.mitigation: P1-22 resolves the effective rate from `org.tax_rates` (`rate numeric(9,6)`, `CHECK (rate >= 0 AND rate <= 1)`, no-overlap `ex_tax_rates_no_active_overlap` over `daterange(effective_from, effective_to, '[)')`) at invoice-line creation time and computes `tax_amount` itself. It CANNOT be re-derived later from the invoice — the rate is not captured. NEVER invent a default rate: with zero seeded rates the correct behaviour for a company with no active rate is an explicit refusal, not an assumed 0.

gaps.assumed: Amounts are stored at the precision the currency actually uses.
gaps.reality: `shared.currencies.minor_unit smallint NOT NULL CHECK (minor_unit BETWEEN 0 AND 4)` exists and is seeded (`JOD 3`, `USD 2`, `EUR 2`), and its column comment says it is "Used by later phases to format and round monetary amounts" — but a repository-wide grep shows `minor_unit` is read by NO migration, NO function, NO constraint and NO TypeScript module. Every money column is `numeric(18,4)` regardless, so `100.1234 USD` (4 dp for a 2-dp currency) is accepted with no error.
gaps.mitigation: P1-22 must load `shared.currencies.minor_unit` for the invoice's currency and reject any inbound amount whose non-zero decimal places exceed it, at the API boundary. Storage stays scale 4 (padded), and the rendered `MoneyView.amount` stays the canonical scale-4 string from `Decimal.toString()` — do NOT reformat to minor_unit on output, or a stored value stops round-tripping byte-identically.

gaps.assumed: `schemas.money` from `src/server/http/validation.ts` is a sufficient boundary for P1-22 amounts.
gaps.reality: It is strictly WIDER than every protected column: `amount: z.string().regex(/^-?\d{1,15}(\.\d{1,6})?$/, 'must be a decimal string with at most 6 decimal places')` permits a leading minus (illegal on every sal/wty money column), 15 integer digits (the column holds 14), and 6 decimal places (the column holds 4, and silently rounds the extra two away). `currency: z.string().regex(/^[A-Z]{3}$/)` validates shape only and does not check membership of `shared.currencies`.
gaps.mitigation: Do not change `schemas.money` (it is shared across eleven phases). Add a P1-22-local refinement that composes `schemas.money` with `Decimal.parse(value, MONEY)` plus the appropriate `parseNonNegative` / `parsePositive`, and resolve the currency against `shared.currencies` (status `active`) before any write — otherwise an unseeded code surfaces as a raw `23503` from the FK.

gaps.assumed: The existing decimal helper can perform the arithmetic P1-22 needs.
gaps.reality: `src/modules/pricing/domain/decimal.ts` exposes ONLY `parse`, `fromDatabase`, `zero`, `scale`, `scaledUnits`, `isZero`, `isNegative`, `compare`, `equals`, `lessThan`, `greaterThan`, `toString`, `toJSON` — plus `parseNonNegative`/`parsePositive`. There is deliberately no `add`, `subtract`, `multiply`, or `round`, and its own header says so: "This type is therefore deliberately NOT a calculation engine." `Money` likewise states "There is no `add` or `multiply`." But P1-22 genuinely must compute `net = unit_price × quantity` and `tax = net × rate` — arithmetic that P1-20 delegated to PostgreSQL CHECKs that do not exist on the invoice side.
gaps.mitigation: Two options, and the choice must be deliberate. (a) Compute the line arithmetic in SQL inside the insert statement (`round($1::numeric * $2::numeric, 4)`), keeping PostgreSQL as the single arithmetic engine and matching its half-away-from-zero rounding exactly. (b) Extend `Decimal` with exact `bigint` multiply-and-round-half-up. Option (a) preserves the P1-20 principle that the database is the only calculator and requires no change to a shared module; prefer it unless a pure-domain computation is needed for a pre-write policy check.

gaps.assumed: `src/modules/pricing/domain/money.ts` describes the platform's currency posture accurately.
gaps.reality: Its `CURRENCY_CODE` doc comment reads: "The platform deliberately ships no currency table and no jurisdiction defaults". That is FALSE at this SHA. `shared.currencies` exists (`20260717100000_org_reference_tables.sql` L73), is seeded with JOD/USD/EUR, and every `currency_code` in `sal`/`wty`/`svc`/`quo`/`inv`/`crm` is FK-RESTRICTed to it. `assertCurrencyCode()` therefore accepts codes the database will reject.
gaps.mitigation: Do not weaken `assertCurrencyCode` (shape validation is still correct as the innermost guard), but P1-22 must add a currency-existence check against `shared.currencies` at the boundary so an unknown code produces a domain validation failure rather than a `23503`. Flag the stale comment as a divergence in the P1-22 record; correcting a comment in a shared module is a judgment call for the implementation wave, not archaeology.

gaps.assumed: An invoice's currency is constrained to the company's or the source quotation's currency.
gaps.reality: Neither. `sal.invoices` has `fk_invoices_quotation_revision → quo.quotation_revisions (tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, id)` and `fk_invoices_currency → shared.currencies (code)`, but NO constraint or trigger compares `sal.invoices.currency_code` with `quo.quotation_revisions.currency_code` or with `org.legal_companies.base_currency_code`. `sal.guard_invoice_freeze()` only freezes the currency AFTER the draft→issued transition.
gaps.mitigation: When an invoice is created from a quotation revision, P1-22 must copy `currency_code` from the revision and refuse a client-supplied override. When created without a revision, the currency must be explicitly supplied and validated against `shared.currencies` — never defaulted from the company, because doing so would invent a policy the schema deliberately leaves open (OIR-04).

gaps.assumed: The warranty odometer is a consistent, comparable number.
gaps.reality: `wty.issue_warranty` reads `SELECT o.value::integer … FROM veh.odometer_readings o` — the RAW captured `value numeric(12,1)`, NOT the normalized `value_km numeric(14,4) GENERATED ALWAYS AS (CASE unit WHEN 'km' THEN value WHEN 'mi' THEN round(value * 1.609344, 4) END) STORED`. `sal.complete_delivery(…, p_odometer_unit text DEFAULT 'km', …)` legally accepts `'mi'` (`ck_odometer_readings_unit CHECK (unit IN ('km','mi'))`). So a mile-captured delivery stores MILES in `wty.warranty_records.odometer_at_issue integer`, and `odometer_limit = v_odo + v_cov.odometer_limit` then adds a unitless coverage allowance to a mile reading. Separately, `numeric(12,1)::integer` rounds half away from zero, so `120000.5` becomes `120001` — the tenth of a unit is lost with no record.
gaps.mitigation: P1-22 must pin `p_odometer_unit` to a single unit per company (or refuse `'mi'` outright) before calling `sal.complete_delivery`, and must document that `wty.warranty_records.odometer_at_issue` and `odometer_limit` are UNITLESS integers whose unit is whatever the delivery captured. Any warranty-expiry-by-mileage check the backend performs must resolve the unit from `veh.odometer_readings.unit` via `sal.delivery_records.final_odometer_reading_id` — never assume km. Closing this structurally would need a migration, which this phase is not authorized to add.

gaps.assumed: An issued invoice's totals are derived and cannot drift from its lines.
gaps.reality: Nothing is derived — there is no GENERATED money column in the entire domain. The only cross-row guarantee is the DEFERRED `tg_invoice_line_amounts_reconcile`, and it fires ONLY on `sal.invoice_line_amounts` DML. `sal.guard_invoice_totals_reconcile()` opens with `IF v_status IS NULL OR v_status = 'draft' THEN RETURN NULL;`. So while the invoice is draft — which is the entire window in which the backend assembles it — no reconciliation runs at all, and a header written by the backend can be arbitrarily wrong right up until `sal.issue_invoice` silently overwrites it.
gaps.mitigation: Treat `sal.invoice_amounts` on a draft as advisory: either do not write it (let `sal.issue_invoice` create it) or write it and accept it will be recomputed. Never present a draft header total to a user as authoritative without recomputing from the line amounts in the same read.

gaps.assumed: The invoice-issue path can be audited for a rounding artefact after the fact.
gaps.reality: `sal.issue_invoice` performs round-then-sum: it SUMS the already-scale-4 line amounts (`sum(la.net_amount)`, `sum(la.tax_amount)`) and only then applies `round(v_net + v_tax, 4)` to the gross. Because each line is already exactly scale 4, the sum is exact and the round is a no-op — the convention is safe, but it means any per-line rounding error introduced by the APPLICATION when it computed `net_amount` is baked in permanently and is invisible to every database check.
gaps.mitigation: P1-22 rounds each line to scale 4 at the moment it computes it (never accumulating an unrounded intermediate across lines), matching the round-then-sum convention exactly. `tests/db/p1-11-precision.test.ts` already pins the reference case (33.3333 × 3 = 99.9999); mirror it as a backend-level test over the real line-creation path.

gaps.assumed: P1-11's own financial-precision contract states, verbatim: "Coherence is enforced (M-fin-4): credit_note.currency = invoice.currency, receipt_reversal.currency = receipt.currency, and an allocation matches both the receipt and the invoice currency."
gaps.reality: For credit notes this is enforced by NOTHING. `sal.credit_notes` has `fk_credit_notes_currency` to `shared.currencies` and four CHECKs (`ck_credit_notes_amount`, `ck_credit_notes_approval_state`, `ck_credit_notes_approved_distinct`, `ck_credit_notes_approved_shape`) — none mentions the invoice. Its five triggers are `tg_credit_notes_stamp_maker`, `tg_credit_notes_approval`, `tg_credit_notes_touch_metadata`, `tg_credit_notes_immutable`, `tg_credit_notes_event_completeness`; none reads `sal.invoices.currency_code`. `sal.approve_credit_note` locks the invoice and checks `v_cn.amount > v_open` but never compares currency. A JOD credit note against a USD invoice is accepted, approved, and subtracted from the USD gross by `sal.invoice_open_receivable` (`SELECT COALESCE(sum(amount), 0) INTO v_credit FROM sal.credit_notes WHERE tenant_id = v_tenant AND invoice_id = p_invoice_id AND approval_state = 'approved'` — no currency predicate).
gaps.mitigation: P1-22 must validate `creditNote.currencyCode === invoice.currencyCode` in the application before INSERT, and must treat this as a hard invariant of its own, not a re-check of a database rule. Because no migration is authorized, this cannot be closed structurally in this phase — record it as a named accepted residual with the exact identifier, and cover it with an abuse-case test that proves the database still accepts the mismatch.

verdict.reasoning:
VERDICT: NOT REFUTED. The gap is genuine, and the archaeologist actually UNDERSTATED it (one leg they credited is enforced, one leg they did not examine is equally broken).

=== 1. THE TABLE DDL CONFIRMS THE CLAIM EXACTLY ===
supabase/migrations/20260724092000_sal_payments.sql:272-304 — `CREATE TABLE sal.credit_notes` carries `invoice_id uuid NOT NULL`, `currency_code text NOT NULL`, `amount numeric(18, 4) NOT NULL`. Its full constraint set is: `pk_credit_notes`, `uq_credit_notes_scope_id UNIQUE (tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, id)`, `fk_credit_notes_tenant`, `fk_credit_notes_invoice FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, invoice_id) REFERENCES sal.invoices (tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, id) ON DELETE RESTRICT`, `fk_credit_notes_currency FOREIGN KEY (currency_code) REFERENCES shared.currencies (code) ON DELETE RESTRICT`, `ck_credit_notes_amount CHECK (amount > 0)`, `ck_credit_notes_approval_state`, `ck_credit_notes_approved_distinct`, `ck_credit_notes_approved_shape`. The invoice FK does NOT carry `currency_code`, and no CHECK names the invoice. Trigger list (lines 309-313) is exactly the five named: `tg_credit_notes_stamp_maker`, `tg_credit_notes_approval`, `tg_credit_notes_touch_metadata`, `tg_credit_notes_immutable`, `tg_credit_notes_event_completeness` (the last created at 20260724093000_sal_financial_events.sql:388). I read all five bodies — `sal.stamp_dual_control_maker`, `sal.guard_dual_control_approval`, `shared.touch_row_metadata`, `org.guard_immutable_columns('tenant_id','company_id','branch_id','invoice_id','currency_code','created_at','created_by')`, `sal.guard_event_completeness` — none reads `sal.invoices.currency_code`. `sal.approve_credit_note(uuid, uuid)` (20260724093000:307-324) locks the invoice with `PERFORM 1 FROM sal.invoices ... FOR UPDATE`, tests `IF v_cn.amount > v_open`, and never compares currency. Confirmed verbatim.

=== 2. THE "COMPOSITE FK" THE DOCS CLAIM IS NOT EVEN CONSTRUCTIBLE ===
docs/phase-1/phase-1-11/phase-1-11-design.md:381 says "[M-fin-4] `credit_note.currency = invoice.currency` ... (CHECK/composite FK)" and phase-1-11-review-response.md:94 says "(CHECK + composite FK)". Neither exists. More importantly, `sal.invoices` has only `pk_invoices PRIMARY KEY (id)` and `uq_invoices_scope_id UNIQUE (tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, id)` (20260724091000_sal_invoices.sql:53-54) — there is NO unique key that includes `currency_code`, so a currency-carrying composite FK cannot be declared without first adding a new UNIQUE index to a protected table. That is what makes this structurally unclosable in a backend-only phase: BOTH candidate fixes (a BEFORE INSERT trigger, or the FK the docs claim) require a new migration. This is the decisive point against refutation.

=== 3. THE CORRECT PATTERN EXISTS IN THE SAME PHASE — IT WAS SIMPLY NOT APPLIED HERE ===
`sal.guard_invoice_line_frozen` (20260724091000_sal_invoices.sql:288-292) contains: `IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sal.invoices i WHERE ... AND i.currency_code = NEW.currency_code) THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'sal.invoice_lines: line currency must match the invoice header currency' USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation';` — bound by `tg_invoice_lines_frozen BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE`. P1-11 knew how to write this guard and wrote it for `sal.invoice_lines`. It wrote no equivalent for `sal.credit_notes`.

=== 4. CORRECTION TO THE CLAIM (in P1-11's favour): the ALLOCATION leg IS enforced ===
The archaeologist quoted the M-fin-4 sentence including "an allocation matches both the receipt and the invoice currency" without noting that this third leg IS real: `sal.allocate_receipt` (20260724093000:281-283) does `IF v_inv.currency_code <> v_rcpt.currency_code THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'sal.allocate_receipt: invoice currency % <> receipt currency %' ... ERRCODE = 'check_violation'`, and it is covered by a live test — tests/db/sal-payments.test.ts:102 "rejects allocation when receipt and invoice currencies differ (23514)" (USD invoice + `seedReceipt(..., currency: 'JOD')`). So M-fin-4 is 1-of-3 enforced, not 0-of-3. Any P1-22 write-up must say this or it misrepresents the protected schema.

=== 5. ESCALATION THE ARCHAEOLOGIST MISSED: the RECEIPT-REVERSAL leg is ALSO unenforced ===
`sal.approve_receipt_reversal(uuid, uuid)` (20260724093000:329-350) locks the receipt and asserts `IF v_rev.amount <> v_rcpt.amount THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'sal.approve_receipt_reversal: full-receipt reversal amount % must equal receipt amount %'` — but it NEVER compares `v_rev.currency_code` to `v_rcpt.currency_code`. `sal.receipt_reversals`' constraints are `pk_receipt_reversals`, `uq_receipt_reversals_scope_id`, `uq_receipt_reversals_receipt UNIQUE (tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, original_receipt_id)`, `fk_receipt_reversals_tenant`, `fk_receipt_reversals_receipt FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, original_receipt_id) REFERENCES sal.receipts (tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, id)`, `fk_receipt_reversals_currency`, `ck_receipt_reversals_amount`, `ck_receipt_reversals_approval_state`, `ck_receipt_reversals_approved_distinct`, `ck_receipt_reversals_approved_shape` — none names the receipt's currency. So `receipt_reversal.currency = receipt.currency` (M-fin-4, second leg) is enforced by NOTHING either, and it emits a `receipt_reversed` financial event in the wrong currency. P1-22 must carry TWO named residuals, not one.

=== 6. WHY THE LEDGER DOES NOT CATCH IT ===
`sal.guard_financial_event_provenance` (20260724093000:64-107, bound by `tg_financial_events_provenance BEFORE INSERT`) binds the event to its OWN source: for `credit_note_issued` it does `SELECT amount, currency_code INTO v_amount, v_currency FROM sal.credit_notes WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND id = NEW.source_id AND approval_state = 'approved'` then `IF NEW.currency_code <> v_currency THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'sal.financial_events: currency % does not bind the source currency %'`. It compares event↔credit-note, never credit-note↔invoice. So the mismatched credit note produces a *perfectly provenance-valid* JOD `credit_note_issued` event against a USD invoice, into the ledger P1-11 designates as "the future accounting integration point (Figure 4.29)". And `sal.invoice_open_receivable` (20260724093000:145-146) subtracts it with no currency predicate — exactly as quoted: `SELECT COALESCE(sum(amount), 0) INTO v_credit FROM sal.credit_notes WHERE tenant_id = v_tenant AND invoice_id = p_invoice_id AND approval_state = 'approved'`. `ck_financial_events_event_type` / `ck_financial_events_source_type` vocabularies ('invoice_issued','receipt_recorded','payment_allocated','credit_note_issued','receipt_reversed','warranty_split_recorded' / 'invoice','receipt','payment_allocation','credit_note','receipt_reversal') offer no additional filter.

=== 7. REACHABILITY IS PROVEN, NOT THEORETICAL ===
supabase/seeds/01_reference_data.sql:19-24 seeds THREE currencies: `('JOD','Jordanian Dinar',3)`, `('USD','United States Dollar',2)`, `('EUR','Euro',2)`. `fk_credit_notes_currency` therefore admits all three. There is NO `INSERT INTO sal.credit_notes` anywhere under supabase/ — no SECURITY DEFINER creation primitive exists (only `sal.approve_credit_note`), and the grant is `GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON sal.credit_notes TO app_runtime`, with `ins_credit_notes_gated` checking only tenant + `iam.has_permission('sal.finance.view')` + company/branch scope. So the application inserts the row directly with a fully client-chosen `currency_code`. P1-11's own test helper `seedCreditNote` (tests/db/p1-11-helpers.ts:395-405) even exposes `opts: { currency?: string }` defaulting to 'USD' — the knob is already wired, no test ever turns it. Worse: `tg_credit_notes_immutable` freezes `currency_code`, so a wrong currency is PERMANENT; the row can only be abandoned via `approval_state='rejected'`.

=== 8. TWO DOCUMENTATION DEFECTS TO RAISE ALONGSIDE ===
(a) docs/phase-1/phase-1-11/phase-1-11-abuse-case-ledger.md:37 row 22 "Cross-currency / cross-branch financial mix" records mitigation "`credit.currency=invoice.currency`, `reversal.currency=receipt.currency`; currency-match on allocation" and residual risk **"none"**. Two of those three mitigations do not exist; the residual is not none.
(b) docs/phase-1/phase-1-11/phase-1-11-test-catalog.md:21 credits suite `sal-credit-reversal` with "currency coherence". No file `tests/db/sal-credit-reversal.test.ts` exists; the credit/reversal tests live in tests/db/sal-payments.test.ts, and the ONLY currency-coherence assertion in the whole P1-11 DB suite is the allocation one at line 102. Per the DDL-is-authoritative rule, prose loses.

=== 9. DISPOSITION ===
The proposed mitigation is right and is the only thing available: P1-22 validates `creditNote.currencyCode === invoice.currencyCode` (and `reversal.currencyCode === receipt.currencyCode`) in application code before INSERT, treats both as first-class P1-22 invariants rather than re-checks, and proves the residual with abuse-case tests that assert the DATABASE still accepts the mismatch (insert a JOD credit note against a USD invoice, call `sal.approve_credit_note`, assert it succeeds and that `sal.invoice_open_receivable` has dropped by the raw amount). Application-level validation is NOT "clearly sufficient" in the refutation sense: `app_runtime` holds direct INSERT on the table, so any current or future code path holding `sal.finance.view` bypasses a route-level check — closing it structurally requires a migration (new trigger, or new UNIQUE on `sal.invoices` + widened FK), and no migration is authorized in P1-22. Severity BLOCKER-for-P1-22's-invariant-list is fair, with the honest framing that it is a P1-11 residual carried forward, not a P1-22 regression.

verdict.reasoning:
REFUTED AS A BLOCKER — but the underlying observation is factually correct and should be kept as a Medium advisory. The archaeologist's own MITIGATION is the proof it is not a blocker: it is 100% application-level and requires no migration, so this cannot be a contract gap.

## 1. The DDL quote is verbatim accurate

`supabase/migrations/20260724093000_sal_financial_events.sql:164-176`:

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION sal.partner_outstanding_balance(p_partner_id uuid)
RETURNS numeric LANGUAGE plpgsql STABLE SECURITY INVOKER SET search_path = '' AS $$
DECLARE v_total numeric(18, 4) := 0; r RECORD;
BEGIN
  FOR r IN SELECT id FROM sal.invoices
    WHERE tenant_id = iam.current_tenant_id() AND payer_partner_id = p_partner_id AND status = 'issued' AND deleted_at IS NULL
  LOOP
    v_total := v_total + sal.invoice_open_receivable(r.id);
  END LOOP;
  RETURN round(v_total, 4);
END; $$;
```

No currency predicate, no grouping, scalar `numeric` return. Confirmed.

## 2. Multi-currency really is reachable (I tried to refute this and could not)

- `sal.invoices.currency_code text NOT NULL`, `CONSTRAINT fk_invoices_currency FOREIGN KEY (currency_code) REFERENCES shared.currencies (code) ON DELETE RESTRICT` (`…091000:40,64`). Any `active` row in `shared.currencies` is admissible.
- `org.legal_companies.base_currency_code text NOT NULL` exists (`20260717103000_org_companies_branches.sql:60,79`) but NOTHING ties `sal.invoices.currency_code` to it — no check constraint, no trigger, no FK. I grepped all 9 `base_currency_code` occurrences; it is referenced only by its own table, its index `ix_legal_companies_base_currency_code`, and `org.provisioning`. The `shared.currencies` COMMENT states outright: "No default/application currency exists: a company states its own base_currency_code."
- `sal.partner_outstanding_balance` has NO company predicate at all, so it spans every company the caller can see. Even if invoice currency were pinned per company, a partner billed by two companies with different `base_currency_code` would still mix.
- The only currency coherence in the module is intra-invoice and intra-allocation: `sal.invoice_lines` line-vs-header (`…091000:288-291`) and `sal.allocate_receipt`'s `IF v_inv.currency_code <> v_rcpt.currency_code THEN RAISE ... 'invoice currency % <> receipt currency %'` (`…093000:281-283`). Neither constrains a partner to one currency.

So the 100 JOD + 100 USD = 200.0000 scenario is genuinely reachable.

## 3. Why it is NOT a blocker: every ingredient for the app-level fix is already granted

- `sal.invoices` — `GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON sal.invoices TO app_runtime; GRANT SELECT ON sal.invoices TO app_readonly;` with `sel_invoices_scope` RLS. `currency_code`, `payer_partner_id`, `status`, `deleted_at` are all directly selectable.
- `sal.invoice_open_receivable(uuid)` — `GRANT EXECUTE ... TO app_runtime, app_readonly` (`…093000:150`).

The proposed mitigation (group invoices by `currency_code` in the application, call `sal.invoice_open_receivable` per invoice, return an array of `{amount, currency}`) uses only these two already-granted objects. It needs no new DDL, no new grant, no new permission. Per the stated test — "refuted=true if ... an application-level composition is clearly sufficient" — this is refuted. The correct classification is: **do not expose `sal.partner_outstanding_balance` as an API result**, plus a documentation divergence. Nothing is missing from the schema.

## 4. The divergence finding stands, and is broader than currency

`docs/phase-1/phase-1-11/phase-1-11-outstanding-balance-derivation-contract.md:15` says only: "`sal.partner_outstanding_balance(p_partner_id uuid)` — the same, aggregated per payer partner." Silent on currency. Per the DDL-is-authoritative rule this should be corrected. It also propagates unqualified into three downstream contracts: `phase-1-11-p1-22-backend-contract.md:24`, `phase-1-11-p1-23-reporting-backend-contract.md:19`, `phase-1-11-p1-30-31-frontend-data-contract.md:17`.

## 5. TWO further defects in the same function that the archaeologist MISSED — and the proposed mitigation would inherit both

**(a) `status = 'issued'` silently drops collectable 'credited' invoices — an internal DDL-vs-DDL contradiction, stronger than the currency point.**
`ck_invoices_status CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'issued', 'credited', 'void_before_issue'))` (`…091000:65`), and the freeze guard permits `issued → credited` (`…091000:122`). `sal.invoice_open_receivable` zeroes ONLY `'draft'` and `'void_before_issue'` (`…093000:137-139`) — so a `'credited'` invoice can still carry a positive open receivable. Decisively, `sal.allocate_receipt` explicitly allows collecting against one: `IF v_inv.status NOT IN ('issued', 'credited') THEN RAISE ...` (`…093000:278`). So the schema considers `'credited'` invoices collectable while `partner_outstanding_balance` drops them from the partner total. If P1-22 copies the `status = 'issued'` filter into the application composition (as the mitigation text literally proposes: "grouping `sal.invoices` on `currency_code`"), it reproduces this bug. The application predicate must be `status IN ('issued','credited')`.

**(b) The derivation does NOT fail closed on a missing finance permission — it silently returns 0.**
`sal.invoices.sel_invoices_scope` carries NO permission predicate (`…091000:140-143`), but `sal.invoice_amounts` (`sel_invoice_amounts_gated`), `sal.payment_allocations` (`sel_payment_allocations_gated`) and `sal.credit_notes` (`sel_credit_notes_gated`) are every one gated by `iam.has_permission('sal.finance.view')`. `sal.invoice_open_receivable` is `SECURITY INVOKER` and LEFT JOINs `sal.invoice_amounts`, then does `v_gross := COALESCE(v_gross, 0)`. A caller who can see the invoice but lacks `sal.finance.view` therefore gets gross 0, alloc 0, credit 0 → **`0.0000` with no error raised**. P1-22 routes MUST enforce `sal.finance.view` at the route layer; the function will not do it for them. This hazard is inherited identically by the app-level composition.

## 6. Minor archaeology corrections
- `phase-1-11-change-log.md:31` and `phase-1-11-traceability.md:21` both place `invoice_open_receivable` / `partner_outstanding_balance` / `receipt_unallocated` in `…092000_sal_payments`. They are in `…093000_sal_financial_events.sql`. Wrong file cited in two contract documents.
- `partner_outstanding_balance` filters `deleted_at IS NULL`; `invoice_open_receivable` does not. Harmless here, but the app composition must keep the `deleted_at IS NULL` filter itself.
- `crm.customer_credit_profiles` carries ONE `credit_limit` with ONE nullable `currency_code` under `uq_customer_credit_profiles_partner UNIQUE (tenant_id, partner_id)` — i.e. the credit model is also single-currency-per-partner and cannot consume an array balance without an app-side currency match. Its COMMENT is explicit: "No enforcement/billing." Do not wire a credit check to it in P1-22 without raising that separately.

## Bottom line
Observation accurate, classification wrong. No migration is required, nothing is absent from the schema, and the fix is entirely within P1-22's application layer using already-granted objects — so this is not a BLOCKER contract gap. Record it as: (i) a Medium "do not expose" advisory on `sal.partner_outstanding_balance`, (ii) a documentation divergence against `phase-1-11-outstanding-balance-derivation-contract.md:15` and its three downstream contracts, and (iii) escalate the two missed defects in §5, of which 5(a) is a genuine internal contradiction in the deployed DDL and 5(b) is a silent-authorization-failure hazard that the proposed mitigation does not address.
