reports.lens: Payments, receipts, allocations — protected `sal` payment contract as deployed at `d9a2c1d` (migrations `20260724092000_sal_payments.sql` + `20260724093000_sal_financial_events.sql`, 119 migrations, no 120)
reports.summary: The payment side of `sal` is a five-table, function-mediated ledger: `sal.payment_methods` (dual-scope reference), `sal.receipts` (branch-scoped, whole-row gated by `sal.finance.view`), `sal.payment_allocations` (append-only, SELECT+INSERT only), `sal.credit_notes` and `sal.receipt_reversals` (both dual-control). Every money column is `numeric(18, 4)` with a `> 0` CHECK; `sal.financial_events.amount` is the only one that allows `>= 0`. Nothing anywhere stores a balance: `sal.invoice_open_receivable`, `sal.receipt_unallocated` and `sal.partner_outstanding_balance` derive it on every call from `sal.invoice_amounts.gross_total` minus non-reversed allocations minus approved credit notes. One receipt CAN allocate to many invoices and one invoice CAN receive many receipts — but only within the SAME `(tenant, company, branch)`, because `fk_payment_allocations_receipt` and `fk_payment_allocations_invoice` are four-column composite scoped FKs. Over-allocation is prevented ONLY inside `sal.allocate_receipt` (two `IF … RAISE check_violation` bounds evaluated under a receipt→invoice `FOR UPDATE` lock order); there is NO constraint, trigger, or exclusion that bounds `Σ payment_allocations.amount` against the receipt or invoice, and `app_runtime` holds raw `INSERT` on `sal.payment_allocations`, so the DB does not defend BR-SAL-002 against any path except the primitive. Corrections are extremely coarse: allocations have no UPDATE/DELETE grant and no reversal record, and `sal.receipt_reversals` is full-receipt-only and terminal, so a single misallocated line can be corrected only by reversing the entire receipt under dual control and recording a new one with a new number. Several things the P1-11 prose promises are simply not in the DDL — the reversal-amount "CHECK", the credit/reversal currency equality (M-fin-4), the conditional receipt freeze, and a function named `reverse_receipt` — and two hard blockers exist before a single receipt can be recorded at all: the `receipt` number sequence is never seeded and `app_runtime` cannot provision it, and the three seeded PLATFORM payment methods are structurally unreachable from `sal.receipts`.

findings.fact: Every payment-side money column is numeric(18, 4) with a strictly-positive CHECK. Only the financial event allows zero.
findings.identifier: sal.receipts.amount, sal.payment_allocations.amount, sal.credit_notes.amount, sal.receipt_reversals.amount, sal.financial_events.amount; ck_receipts_amount, ck_payment_allocations_amount, ck_credit_notes_amount, ck_receipt_reversals_amount, ck_financial_events_amount
findings.evidence: `amount numeric(18, 4) NOT NULL` on all five; `CONSTRAINT ck_receipts_amount CHECK (amount > 0)`, `CONSTRAINT ck_payment_allocations_amount CHECK (amount > 0)`, `CONSTRAINT ck_credit_notes_amount CHECK (amount > 0)`, `CONSTRAINT ck_receipt_reversals_amount CHECK (amount > 0)`, vs `CONSTRAINT ck_financial_events_amount CHECK (amount >= 0)`
findings.consequence: Money crosses the `pg` driver as a string. P1-22 carries amounts as exact decimal strings end to end — no parseFloat/Number/toFixed/float aggregation on any authoritative path — and rejects a zero-amount receipt/allocation/credit/reversal in validation, because the DB will reject it with 23514. Bounds are 0.0001 .. 99999999999999.9999.

findings.fact: The payment-method vocabulary is exactly three kinds, closed by CHECK, and the three platform rows are seeded. There is no online gateway/settlement/wallet kind.
findings.evidence: `CONSTRAINT ck_payment_methods_kind CHECK (kind IN ('cash', 'card_terminal', 'bank_transfer'))`; `ck_payment_methods_scope CHECK (scope IN ('platform', 'tenant'))`; `ck_payment_methods_status CHECK (status IN ('active', 'inactive'))`; `ck_payment_methods_code CHECK (method_code ~ '^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,62}$')`. Seed: `('platform', NULL, 'cash','cash','Cash',…), ('platform', NULL, 'card_terminal','card_terminal','Card terminal',…), ('platform', NULL, 'bank_transfer','bank_transfer','Bank transfer',…)`
findings.consequence: P1-22 transcribes exactly `cash | card_terminal | bank_transfer` as the kind vocabulary and `active | inactive` as the status vocabulary. It NEVER invents a gateway, wallet, cheque, or settlement kind (ASM-14 / CON-04). Tenant method_code must match the regex before it reaches SQL.

findings.fact: sal.receipts is branch-scoped and its WHOLE ROW is gated by sal.finance.view on SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE — not just the amount column.
findings.evidence: `CREATE POLICY sel_receipts_gated ON sal.receipts FOR SELECT TO app_runtime, app_readonly USING (tenant_id = iam.current_tenant_id() AND iam.has_permission('sal.finance.view') AND (iam.allowed_company_ids() IS NULL OR company_id = ANY (iam.allowed_company_ids())) AND (iam.allowed_branch_ids() IS NULL OR branch_id = ANY (iam.allowed_branch_ids())))`
findings.consequence: A caller without `sal.finance.view` sees ZERO receipts — not a redacted receipt. P1-22 must not build a "receipt list without amounts" view for non-finance roles; the row simply does not exist for them. Same whole-row gate applies to `sal.payment_allocations`, `sal.credit_notes`, `sal.receipt_reversals` and `sal.financial_events`.

findings.fact: Receipt status is a four-value closed vocabulary, and 'reversed' is terminal and reachable only through an approved reversal.
findings.evidence: `CONSTRAINT ck_receipts_status CHECK (status IN ('recorded', 'partially_allocated', 'allocated', 'reversed'))`; guard: `IF OLD.status = 'reversed' THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'sal.receipts: reversed is terminal'`; and `IF NEW.status = 'reversed' THEN IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sal.receipt_reversals rr WHERE … rr.approval_state = 'approved') THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'sal.receipts: a receipt may be reversed only via an approved receipt reversal (sal.approve_receipt_reversal)'`
findings.consequence: P1-22 transcribes exactly `recorded | partially_allocated | allocated | reversed`. It never writes `status='reversed'` directly (23514), and never offers a transition out of `reversed`.

findings.fact: The deployed receipt freeze is UNCONDITIONAL on every UPDATE and also freezes receipt_number — it is not conditioned on the event existing or on status, as the handoff prose claims.
findings.identifier: sal.guard_receipt_freeze(), trigger tg_receipts_freeze BEFORE UPDATE ON sal.receipts
findings.evidence: `IF NEW.amount <> OLD.amount OR NEW.currency_code <> OLD.currency_code OR NEW.payment_method_id <> OLD.payment_method_id OR NEW.payer_partner_id <> OLD.payer_partner_id OR NEW.received_at IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.received_at OR NEW.receipt_number <> OLD.receipt_number THEN RAISE EXCEPTION … USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation'` — no status/event precondition anywhere in the function.
findings.consequence: DDL is authoritative over `phase-1-11-receipt-contract.md` ("once the `receipt_recorded` event exists or `status ≠ 'recorded'`") and over the immutability matrix. Six columns are frozen from the very first UPDATE, receipt_number included. The columns the guard does NOT freeze are `evidence_document_version_id`, `received_by`, `idempotency_key`, `deleted_at`, `deleted_by` and `status` — so attaching evidence after the fact is legal, and P1-22 may expose exactly that.

findings.fact: Receipt numbering is allocated inside the primitive from the shared allocator with the fixed literal sequence code 'receipt', scoped to (company, branch), and is unique per branch.
findings.evidence: `SELECT display_number INTO v_number FROM shared.next_display_number('receipt', p_company_id, p_branch_id);` and `CONSTRAINT uq_receipts_number UNIQUE (tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, receipt_number)`
findings.consequence: P1-22 NEVER supplies or validates a receipt number, and never calls `NumberAllocationService` for receipts — the primitive owns it. The number format (prefix, pad width, reset rule) is operator configuration on the `shared.number_sequences` row, so P1-22 must not document or assert any format. `receipt` is already a registered code in `src/modules/shared-services/domain/sequence-registry.ts` (targetTable `sal.receipts`, targetColumn `receipt_number`).

findings.fact: sal.record_receipt server-stamps the cashier and the tenant; neither is a client input.
findings.identifier: sal.record_receipt(uuid, uuid, uuid, uuid, text, numeric, uuid, text, uuid) RETURNS uuid
findings.evidence: `DECLARE v_tenant uuid := iam.current_tenant_id(); v_actor uuid := iam.current_user_id();` … `VALUES (v_tenant, p_company_id, p_branch_id, v_number, p_method_id, p_payer_partner_id, p_currency_code, p_amount, v_actor, …)` — `received_by` is `v_actor`.
findings.consequence: P1-22 exposes no `receivedBy` or `tenantId` field on the record-receipt request. The full granted signature is `sal.record_receipt(p_company_id uuid, p_branch_id uuid, p_method_id uuid, p_payer_partner_id uuid, p_currency_code text, p_amount numeric, p_evidence_document_version_id uuid DEFAULT NULL, p_idempotency_key text DEFAULT NULL, p_correlation_id uuid DEFAULT NULL)`.

findings.fact: YES — one payment can allocate to MULTIPLE invoices, and one invoice can receive multiple receipts. The only structural restriction is that receipt and invoice must be in the same (tenant, company, branch).
findings.evidence: `CONSTRAINT fk_payment_allocations_receipt FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, receipt_id) REFERENCES sal.receipts (tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, id) ON DELETE RESTRICT` and the matching `fk_payment_allocations_invoice … REFERENCES sal.invoices (tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, id)`. There is NO unique constraint on `(receipt_id)`, on `(invoice_id)`, or on `(receipt_id, invoice_id)` — the only UNIQUE on the table is `pk_payment_allocations PRIMARY KEY (id)`.
findings.consequence: P1-22's allocate endpoint is many-to-many by contract. It may also allocate the SAME receipt to the SAME invoice twice (no uniqueness stops it) as long as the bounds hold — so partial top-ups are legal and the backend must not assume one allocation row per (receipt, invoice) pair when rendering.

findings.fact: Over-allocation is prevented by the FUNCTION, not by the database. No constraint bounds Σ allocations against the receipt amount or the invoice open receivable.
findings.identifier: sal.allocate_receipt(uuid, uuid, numeric, uuid); absence of any CHECK/EXCLUDE/trigger on sal.payment_allocations other than ck_payment_allocations_amount
findings.evidence: Inside the function only: `v_unalloc := sal.receipt_unallocated(p_receipt_id); IF p_amount > v_unalloc THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'sal.allocate_receipt: amount % exceeds receipt unallocated %' … USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation';` and `v_open := sal.invoice_open_receivable(p_invoice_id); IF p_amount > v_open THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'sal.allocate_receipt: amount % exceeds invoice open receivable %' …`. The table's only constraints are `pk_payment_allocations`, four FKs and `ck_payment_allocations_amount CHECK (amount > 0)`. Grant: `GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON sal.payment_allocations TO app_runtime;`
findings.consequence: BLOCKING RULE for P1-22: allocation MUST go through `sal.allocate_receipt` on every path. A direct `INSERT INTO sal.payment_allocations` is granted and would over-allocate silently (the only thing that would stop it is the DEFERRED completeness trigger demanding a matching `payment_allocated` event, which a determined direct writer could also satisfy). The backend's own guard is the structural guarantee, so the repository layer must expose no raw insert for this table.

findings.fact: The allocation lock order is receipt → invoice, both FOR UPDATE, and the bounds are re-derived AFTER the locks are held.
findings.evidence: `SELECT * INTO v_rcpt FROM sal.receipts WHERE id = p_receipt_id AND tenant_id = iam.current_tenant_id() FOR UPDATE;` … `SELECT * INTO v_inv FROM sal.invoices WHERE id = p_invoice_id AND tenant_id = v_rcpt.tenant_id AND company_id = v_rcpt.company_id AND branch_id = v_rcpt.branch_id FOR UPDATE;` … then `v_unalloc := sal.receipt_unallocated(...)`, `v_open := sal.invoice_open_receivable(...)`
findings.consequence: P1-22 must never read a balance and then write based on the read; it calls the primitive, which locks first. Any new P1-22-owned transaction that touches both a receipt and an invoice must take them in the same receipt→invoice order or it introduces a deadlock the DB cannot save it from.

findings.fact: sal.allocate_receipt enforces five gates in order, each with a distinct message; two raise no_data_found (P0002) and three raise check_violation (23514).
findings.identifier: sal.allocate_receipt(p_receipt_id uuid, p_invoice_id uuid, p_amount numeric, p_correlation_id uuid DEFAULT NULL) RETURNS uuid
findings.evidence: (1) `'sal.allocate_receipt: receipt % not found in scope'` USING ERRCODE = 'no_data_found'; (2) `'sal.allocate_receipt: receipt is reversed'` 23514; (3) `'sal.allocate_receipt: invoice % not found in the receipt scope'` P0002; (4) `IF v_inv.status NOT IN ('issued', 'credited') THEN RAISE … 'sal.allocate_receipt: invoice is % (must be issued)'` 23514; (5) `IF v_inv.currency_code <> v_rcpt.currency_code THEN RAISE … 'invoice currency % <> receipt currency %'` 23514; plus `IF p_amount <= 0`, then the two bound checks.
findings.consequence: P1-22 maps P0002 → ERR-RES-001 and 23514 → a domain conflict/validation failure, and must pre-validate invoice status ∈ {issued, credited} and currency equality so the caller gets a typed error rather than a raw SQLSTATE. Note a `credited` invoice is still allocatable.

findings.fact: After a successful allocation the primitive recomputes and writes the receipt status; the backend never sets it.
findings.evidence: `SELECT COALESCE(sum(amount), 0) INTO v_alloc_total FROM sal.payment_allocations WHERE tenant_id = v_rcpt.tenant_id AND receipt_id = p_receipt_id; UPDATE sal.receipts SET status = CASE WHEN v_alloc_total >= v_rcpt.amount THEN 'allocated' ELSE 'partially_allocated' END WHERE id = p_receipt_id;`
findings.consequence: P1-22 never writes `sal.receipts.status`. Note the sum is NOT filtered by receipt status, and `v_rcpt.amount` is the frozen amount, so the transition is deterministic.

findings.fact: Outstanding balance is DERIVED, never stored. There is no balance column on any sal table. Three STABLE SECURITY INVOKER functions are the only authority.
findings.identifier: sal.invoice_open_receivable(p_invoice_id uuid) RETURNS numeric; sal.receipt_unallocated(p_receipt_id uuid) RETURNS numeric; sal.partner_outstanding_balance(p_partner_id uuid) RETURNS numeric — all three GRANT EXECUTE TO app_runtime, app_readonly
findings.evidence: invoice_open_receivable: `IF v_status IS NULL OR v_status IN ('draft', 'void_before_issue') THEN RETURN 0; END IF;` then `SELECT COALESCE(sum(pa.amount), 0) INTO v_alloc FROM sal.payment_allocations pa JOIN sal.receipts r ON … WHERE pa.tenant_id = v_tenant AND pa.invoice_id = p_invoice_id AND r.status <> 'reversed';` then `SELECT COALESCE(sum(amount), 0) INTO v_credit FROM sal.credit_notes WHERE tenant_id = v_tenant AND invoice_id = p_invoice_id AND approval_state = 'approved';` then `RETURN round(v_gross - v_alloc - v_credit, 4);`. receipt_unallocated: `IF v_amount IS NULL OR v_status = 'reversed' THEN RETURN 0; END IF;` … `RETURN round(v_amount - v_alloc, 4);`
findings.consequence: The exact derivation P1-22 must reproduce or (better) delegate to: open = `sal.invoice_amounts.gross_total` − Σ allocations whose receipt.status <> 'reversed' − Σ credit_notes with approval_state='approved', rounded to 4; unallocated = receipt.amount − Σ ALL its allocations (no status filter needed, since a reversed receipt short-circuits to 0). P1-22 must NOT invent a cached balance column — and if it builds the deferred incremental cache, the derivation above is the reference oracle.

findings.fact: There is no 'paid' or 'partially_paid' invoice status. Payment state is purely derived. But the append-only status-history table accepts both values.
findings.evidence: `CONSTRAINT ck_invoices_status CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'issued', 'credited', 'void_before_issue'))` vs `CONSTRAINT ck_invoice_status_history_to_status CHECK (to_status IN ('draft', 'issued', 'partially_paid', 'paid', 'credited', 'void_before_issue'))`. Table comment: 'Records lifecycle and derived payment milestones (partially_paid/paid may be recorded by the backend from the derived balance).'
findings.consequence: P1-22 must NEVER attempt `UPDATE sal.invoices SET status='paid'` — the CHECK forbids it and `guard_invoice_freeze` allows only issued→credited. "Paid" is `sal.invoice_open_receivable(id) = 0`. P1-22 MAY (and is explicitly invited to) append `partially_paid` / `paid` rows to `sal.invoice_status_history` after an allocation; nothing does so today, so this is a deliberate P1-22 decision, not an inherited behaviour.

findings.fact: sal.invoice_status_history is NOT finance-gated, unlike every amount-bearing table.
findings.evidence: `USING (tenant_id = iam.current_tenant_id() AND (iam.allowed_company_ids() IS NULL OR company_id = ANY (iam.allowed_company_ids())) AND (iam.allowed_branch_ids() IS NULL OR branch_id = ANY (iam.allowed_branch_ids())))` — no `iam.has_permission('sal.finance.view')` clause.
findings.consequence: If P1-22 writes `paid` / `partially_paid` milestones, a non-finance role can read WHEN an invoice was paid while being unable to read any amount. That is intentional and safe, but P1-22 must not put an amount in the `reason` free-text column of that ledger.

findings.fact: Dual control is server-stamped by triggers shared between credit notes and receipt reversals; the client cannot choose the maker, and self-approval is blocked twice over.
findings.identifier: sal.stamp_dual_control_maker(), sal.guard_dual_control_approval(); triggers tg_credit_notes_stamp_maker, tg_credit_notes_approval, tg_receipt_reversals_stamp_maker, tg_receipt_reversals_approval; CHECKs ck_credit_notes_approved_distinct, ck_receipt_reversals_approved_distinct
findings.evidence: maker: `NEW.requested_by := iam.current_user_id(); … NEW.approved_by := NULL; NEW.approved_at := NULL;` with `RAISE EXCEPTION 'dual control: no user context (requested_by cannot be stamped)' USING ERRCODE = 'insufficient_privilege'`. approval: `IF OLD.approval_state = 'pending' AND NEW.approval_state = 'approved' THEN NEW.approved_by := iam.current_user_id(); NEW.approved_at := now(); … IF NEW.approved_by = NEW.requested_by THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'dual control: the approver must differ from the requester (maker<>approver)' USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation'`. Plus `CHECK (approved_by IS NULL OR approved_by <> requested_by)`.
findings.consequence: P1-22 exposes no `requestedBy`/`approvedBy` input. Errors: 42501 when no user context, 23514 on self-approval. Rejection (`pending → rejected`) also stamps `approved_by`, and self-rejection is caught by the table CHECK (23514), not by the trigger. An approved or rejected decision is frozen: `IF OLD.approval_state <> 'pending' THEN … RAISE EXCEPTION 'dual control: a % decision is frozen'`.

findings.fact: Exactly one financial event per financial command is a COMMIT-TIME constraint, not a best-effort convention.
findings.identifier: sal.guard_event_completeness(); tg_receipts_event_completeness, tg_payment_allocations_event_completeness, tg_credit_notes_event_completeness, tg_receipt_reversals_event_completeness, tg_invoices_event_completeness — all DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED
findings.evidence: `CREATE CONSTRAINT TRIGGER tg_payment_allocations_event_completeness AFTER INSERT ON sal.payment_allocations DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION sal.guard_event_completeness();` and `RAISE EXCEPTION 'sal.%: financial command produced no % event (completeness)', TG_TABLE_NAME, v_type USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation'`
findings.consequence: P1-22 must expect 23514 at COMMIT, not at statement time, for any transaction that touches these tables outside the primitives. Because the check is DEFERRED, a failing transaction rolls back everything including the receipt number allocation — which is correct and is the reason numbering is gap-tolerant.

findings.fact: The financial event vocabularies are closed and each event is single-use per source.
findings.evidence: `CHECK (event_type IN ('invoice_issued', 'receipt_recorded', 'payment_allocated', 'credit_note_issued', 'receipt_reversed', 'warranty_split_recorded'))`; `CHECK (source_type IN ('invoice', 'receipt', 'payment_allocation', 'credit_note', 'receipt_reversal'))`; `CONSTRAINT uq_financial_events_source UNIQUE (tenant_id, source_type, source_id, event_type)`
findings.consequence: P1-22's outbox projection reads exactly these six event types and five source types and invents none. The payment-lens pairs are `receipt_recorded`/`receipt`, `payment_allocated`/`payment_allocation`, `credit_note_issued`/`credit_note`, `receipt_reversed`/`receipt_reversal`.

findings.fact: Full-receipt reversal only, at most one per receipt, and it does not touch the allocation rows.
findings.identifier: uq_receipt_reversals_receipt; sal.approve_receipt_reversal(p_reversal_id uuid, p_correlation_id uuid DEFAULT NULL) RETURNS void
findings.evidence: `CONSTRAINT uq_receipt_reversals_receipt UNIQUE (tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, original_receipt_id)`; in the function: `IF v_rev.amount <> v_rcpt.amount THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'sal.approve_receipt_reversal: full-receipt reversal amount % must equal receipt amount %' … USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation';` then `UPDATE sal.receipt_reversals SET approval_state = 'approved', reversed_at = now() … ; UPDATE sal.receipts SET status = 'reversed' WHERE id = v_rcpt.id;` — no statement touches sal.payment_allocations.
findings.consequence: P1-22 offers no partial reversal and no un-allocate. The reversal order (approve reversal, THEN flip the receipt) is mandatory because `guard_receipt_freeze` requires the approved reversal to already exist — a backend that re-implemented this in the other order would deadlock itself against its own guard.

findings.fact: The four sal payment permission codes that already exist, and their risk levels.
findings.evidence: `('sal.payment.record','sal','Record receipts','medium',…)`, `('sal.payment.allocate','sal','Allocate receipts to invoices','medium',…)`, `('sal.credit.manage','sal','Request and manage credit notes','high',…)`, `('sal.reversal.approve','sal','Approve receipt reversals (dual control)','high',…)`, `('sal.finance.view','sal','View financial amounts (invoices/receipts/events)','high',…)`
findings.consequence: P1-22 reuses these exact codes. Because RLS demands `sal.finance.view` for the whole row, EVERY payment operation additionally requires `sal.finance.view` — `sal.payment.record` alone is not sufficient to insert a receipt. P1-22 must therefore require the pair on every payment route.

findings.fact: RLS uses the scope-blind iam.has_permission(), with company/branch narrowing via the union-of-grants arrays — it is defence in depth only.
findings.identifier: iam.has_permission(text), iam.has_permission_in_scope(text, uuid, uuid, uuid), iam.allowed_company_ids(), iam.allowed_branch_ids()
findings.evidence: Every sal payment policy reads `iam.has_permission('sal.finance.view') AND (iam.allowed_company_ids() IS NULL OR company_id = ANY (iam.allowed_company_ids())) AND (iam.allowed_branch_ids() IS NULL OR branch_id = ANY (iam.allowed_branch_ids()))` — `iam.has_permission_in_scope` appears in no sal policy.
findings.consequence: Per P1-18-A-01 the allowed_* arrays are the union of every active grant regardless of which permission it carries. Every branch-scoped P1-22 payment operation must still pass a concrete `authorizationTarget` so application-level evaluation uses `iam.has_permission_in_scope`, exactly as P1-21 §11 required for inventory.

findings.fact: No application role holds DELETE on any payment table, and sal.payment_allocations has no soft-delete column at all.
findings.evidence: `GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON sal.receipts TO app_runtime;` / `GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON sal.payment_allocations TO app_runtime;` / `GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON sal.financial_events TO app_runtime;` / `GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON sal.credit_notes TO app_runtime;` / `GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON sal.receipt_reversals TO app_runtime;` — no DELETE anywhere. `sal.payment_allocations` declares no `deleted_at`/`deleted_by` columns.
findings.consequence: Write feasibility for the payment lens is proven with no new migration. P1-22's allocation repository exposes only read and insert; there is nothing to soft-delete and no correction path other than full receipt reversal.

findings.fact: Idempotency is available on receipts, credit notes and reversals via a tenant-wide partial unique index — but not on allocations.
findings.evidence: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_receipts_idempotency ON sal.receipts (tenant_id, idempotency_key) WHERE idempotency_key IS NOT NULL;` (same shape for the other two). `sal.payment_allocations` has no `idempotency_key` column.
findings.consequence: P1-22 layers the Phase 1-4 Idempotency-Key store over these business keys for record/credit/reversal, and owns idempotency ENTIRELY at the application layer for allocation. Note the key is unique per TENANT, not per branch — two branches cannot reuse a key.

findings.fact: sal.financial_events.correlation_id and idempotency_key are carried through by the primitives, giving P1-22 a ready join key for the outbox.
findings.evidence: `CREATE INDEX ix_financial_events_correlation ON sal.financial_events (tenant_id, correlation_id);` and `sal.record_receipt` passes `p_correlation_id, p_idempotency_key` into the event insert; `sal.allocate_receipt` passes `p_correlation_id` into both the allocation row and the event.
findings.consequence: P1-22 passes its request correlation id as `p_correlation_id` on every primitive call, so the emitted event, the allocation row and the HTTP request are joinable for the future `payment.recorded.v1` / `payment.allocated.v1` outbox projections.

gaps.assumed: That an allocation links a receipt to the payer's own invoice.
gaps.reality: There is NO payer coherence check. `sal.allocate_receipt` never compares `v_rcpt.payer_partner_id` with `v_inv.payer_partner_id`; `sal.payment_allocations` has no partner column and no constraint tying the two. The composite scoped FKs constrain (tenant, company, branch) ONLY. So customer A's receipt can legally pay customer B's invoice inside the same branch, and `sal.partner_outstanding_balance` would then show B's balance reduced by A's money.
gaps.mitigation: Composable: P1-22 loads both `sal.receipts.payer_partner_id` and `sal.invoices.payer_partner_id` before calling the primitive and rejects a mismatch with a typed conflict — with an explicit, documented decision about whether a third-party payer (insurer, fleet owner, warranty provider) is ever permitted, and if so, gated by its own permission rather than allowed by default. The DB will not catch this.

gaps.assumed: That a misallocated payment can be corrected.
gaps.reality: It can only be corrected by destroying the whole receipt. `sal.payment_allocations` is `GRANT SELECT, INSERT` only, has no `deleted_at`, and there is no allocation-reversal table or function. The only correction instrument is `sal.receipt_reversals`, which is FULL-receipt (`uq_receipt_reversals_receipt UNIQUE (tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, original_receipt_id)`, amount must equal the receipt amount) and terminal (`IF OLD.status = 'reversed' THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'sal.receipts: reversed is terminal'`).
gaps.mitigation: No application mitigation restores the allocation. P1-22 must state the operational consequence plainly in its contract: correcting one wrong allocation line requires a dual-control reversal of the ENTIRE receipt (new maker, different approver) and re-recording the money as a NEW receipt with a NEW receipt number, then re-allocating every line. The UI/API must warn before allocation because allocation is effectively irreversible at line granularity.

gaps.assumed: That `sal.record_receipt`'s idempotency key makes a replay safe.
gaps.reality: Two holes. (1) The in-function pre-check `SELECT id INTO v_existing FROM sal.receipts WHERE tenant_id = v_tenant AND idempotency_key = p_idempotency_key; IF FOUND THEN RETURN v_existing; END IF;` returns the ORIGINAL receipt id without comparing amount, currency, method, payer or branch — a replay with different parameters silently succeeds and returns the wrong receipt. (2) That pre-check runs under `sel_receipts_gated`, which narrows by `iam.allowed_branch_ids()`; a replay from a session that cannot see the original branch will miss the pre-check and hit `uq_receipts_idempotency` instead, producing 23505 rather than an idempotent return. There is no lock or advisory lock around the pre-check, so two concurrent same-key calls also race to 23505.
gaps.mitigation: Composable: P1-22 must own idempotency at the application layer (the Phase 1-4 store, per the P1-11 handoff), fingerprinting the full request so a replay with different parameters is rejected as a conflict rather than absorbed, and must map SQLSTATE 23505 on `uq_receipts_idempotency` to the same idempotent-replay outcome instead of a 500.

gaps.assumed: That approving a credit note has a permission of its own, mirroring `sal.reversal.approve`.
gaps.reality: There is NO `sal.credit.approve` in `supabase/seeds/04_iam_permission_catalog.sql` (100 permissions total). Only `sal.credit.manage` ('Request and manage credit notes', high) exists, covering request and approve alike. At database level the only barrier between requesting and approving a credit note is `maker<>approver` — a second holder of `sal.credit.manage` can approve, and there is no separate high-risk approval right the way there is for reversals.
gaps.mitigation: Composable without a migration: the permission catalog is a SEED file, not a migration, and P1-21 already added four codes to it (`inv.item.read`, `inv.custody.manage`, `inv.external_purchase.record`, `inv.audit.read`) — the same path is available. Either add `sal.credit.approve` (risk `high`) and gate `sal.approve_credit_note` on it, or explicitly document reusing `sal.credit.manage` for both sides. Whichever is chosen must be a recorded decision, because the DDL does not decide it.

gaps.assumed: That there are primitives for the whole payment workflow, as the P1-11 handoff table suggests.
gaps.reality: There is no primitive to REQUEST a credit note, no primitive to REQUEST a receipt reversal, and no primitive to REJECT either. The granted `sal.*` functions are exactly `issue_invoice`, `record_receipt`, `allocate_receipt`, `approve_credit_note`, `approve_receipt_reversal`, `complete_delivery`, plus the three read-only derivations. Requesting is a raw `INSERT INTO sal.credit_notes` / `sal.receipt_reversals` (the maker trigger stamps `requested_by` and nulls `approved_by`/`approved_at`), and rejecting is a raw `UPDATE … SET approval_state='rejected'`. The migration header and the `sal.receipt_reversals` table COMMENT both name a function `reverse_receipt` — `grep -rn "reverse_receipt"` proves NO SUCH FUNCTION EXISTS anywhere in the 119 migrations.
gaps.mitigation: Composable: P1-22 writes the request and reject paths itself against the granted table DML, relying on `sal.stamp_dual_control_maker` / `sal.guard_dual_control_approval` / `ck_*_approved_distinct` / `ck_*_approved_shape` for correctness. It must NOT search for or reference `sal.reverse_receipt`, and should record the ghost name as a documentation divergence.

gaps.assumed: That `sal.receipt_reversals.amount = original receipt amount` is a CHECK constraint, as `phase-1-11-data-dictionary-sal.md` states ('CHECK `= original receipt amount`') and as abuse-case 8 claims ('`amount=original` CHECK').
gaps.reality: No such CHECK exists. The table carries only `CONSTRAINT ck_receipt_reversals_amount CHECK (amount > 0)`. The equality lives solely inside `sal.approve_receipt_reversal` as `IF v_rev.amount <> v_rcpt.amount THEN RAISE EXCEPTION … USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation'`. A pending reversal may therefore be created with ANY positive amount and will sit in the queue looking legitimate until approval fails.
gaps.mitigation: Composable: P1-22 reads the receipt amount server-side and sets the reversal amount from it on insert — never accepting it from the client — so a wrong-amount reversal can never be created and queued. DDL is authoritative over the data dictionary here.

gaps.assumed: That `sal.invoice_open_receivable` / `sal.receipt_unallocated` are safe to call for any authenticated user and will error or refuse if the caller is not entitled.
gaps.reality: They return 0 instead. `sel_invoices_scope` is NOT finance-gated but `sel_invoice_amounts_gated` IS (`iam.has_permission('sal.finance.view')`), and the derivation joins amounts with `LEFT JOIN … a.deleted_at IS NULL` then does `v_gross := COALESCE(v_gross, 0)`. So a caller without `sal.finance.view` sees the invoice, gets `gross_total` as NULL, and receives `0` — indistinguishable from a fully paid invoice. `sal.receipt_unallocated` behaves the same way: the receipt row is invisible, `v_amount IS NULL`, `RETURN 0`.
gaps.mitigation: Composable and mandatory: P1-22 must authorize `sal.finance.view` (with a concrete `authorizationTarget`) at the application layer BEFORE calling any derivation, and must never treat a returned 0 as evidence of payment. A silent zero here would be a falsification risk, not a bug.

gaps.assumed: That the UPDATE policies on the finance tables are branch-narrowed like their SELECT/INSERT counterparts.
gaps.reality: They are not. `upd_receipts_gated`, `upd_credit_notes_gated` and `upd_receipt_reversals_gated` each read only `USING (tenant_id = iam.current_tenant_id() AND iam.has_permission('sal.finance.view')) WITH CHECK (tenant_id = iam.current_tenant_id() AND iam.has_permission('sal.finance.view'))` — no `iam.allowed_company_ids()` / `iam.allowed_branch_ids()` clause at all, unlike the SELECT and INSERT policies on the same tables.
gaps.mitigation: Composable: RLS will let a finance user in branch X update a receipt, credit note or reversal row in branch Y of the same tenant (the freeze guards limit WHAT can change, not WHERE). P1-22 must resolve company/branch from the target row and pass a concrete `authorizationTarget` on every mutation route, and must never rely on RLS for branch containment on an UPDATE. Note the practical reach is bounded — `guard_receipt_freeze` blocks the money columns and `guard_dual_control_approval` freezes decided rows — but a cross-branch approval or status write is reachable.

gaps.assumed: That `sal.receipts.deleted_at` means a receipt can be soft-deleted, consistent with the platform-wide 'hard delete is never an application capability' rule.
gaps.reality: The column exists (`deleted_at timestamptz NULL, deleted_by uuid NULL`) and `app_runtime` holds UPDATE, and `sal.guard_receipt_freeze` does NOT protect it — yet NOTHING honours it. `sel_receipts_gated` has no `deleted_at IS NULL` predicate; `sal.receipt_unallocated` does not filter it; `sal.invoice_open_receivable`'s allocation join `JOIN sal.receipts r … WHERE … r.status <> 'reversed'` does not filter it. (By contrast `sal.partner_outstanding_balance` DOES filter `sal.invoices.deleted_at IS NULL`, so the codebase is internally inconsistent.)
gaps.mitigation: Composable by prohibition: P1-22 must never soft-delete a receipt, and must never add `deleted_at IS NULL` to a money query — doing so would make the backend's numbers disagree with `sal.invoice_open_receivable`, the authoritative derivation. Recommend documenting `sal.receipts.deleted_at` as a vestigial column the payment module treats as always NULL.

gaps.assumed: That `sal.financial_events.source_type` is bound to `event_type`, so the event ledger is self-consistent.
gaps.reality: It is not. `sal.guard_financial_event_provenance()` branches exclusively on `NEW.event_type` and looks up the corresponding table; it never validates `NEW.source_type`. `source_type` is constrained only by its own vocabulary CHECK. An event with `event_type='receipt_recorded'` and `source_type='invoice'` pointing at a real receipt id passes the guard, binds the amount, and — because `uq_financial_events_source` is `(tenant_id, source_type, source_id, event_type)` — even escapes the single-use constraint. `app_runtime` holds `GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON sal.financial_events`, so this path is reachable.
gaps.mitigation: Composable by prohibition: P1-22 must NEVER insert into `sal.financial_events` directly; every event is emitted by the primitive, which always passes the correct pair. The repository layer must expose no insert for this table, and the outbox projector must read the pairing from `phase-1-11-financial-event-catalogue.md` rather than trusting `source_type` on an arbitrary row.

gaps.assumed: That `sal.partner_outstanding_balance` is a usable partner-balance read model.
gaps.reality: It is an N+1 loop, not a set query: `FOR r IN SELECT id FROM sal.invoices WHERE tenant_id = iam.current_tenant_id() AND payer_partner_id = p_partner_id AND status = 'issued' AND deleted_at IS NULL LOOP v_total := v_total + sal.invoice_open_receivable(r.id); END LOOP;`. Each iteration re-runs two aggregates. It also EXCLUDES `status = 'credited'` invoices, even though `sal.allocate_receipt` explicitly permits allocating to a `credited` invoice — so money owed on a credited invoice is invisible in the partner balance. And it sums across currencies with no currency predicate. `phase-1-11-outstanding-balance-derivation-contract.md` concedes the O(n) residual and assigns incremental caching to P1-22.
gaps.mitigation: Partly composable. The cross-currency summation and the missing `credited` invoices are real correctness defects that P1-22 must not paper over: if a partner-balance endpoint is offered, P1-22 should compute it in the application from `sal.invoice_open_receivable` per invoice with an explicit currency grouping and an explicit, documented decision about `credited` invoices, rather than surfacing `sal.partner_outstanding_balance` as-is. Any incremental cache P1-22 builds must be validated against the per-invoice derivation, never against this function.

gaps.assumed: That a receipt can be recorded out of the box — `sal.record_receipt` will allocate a receipt number.
gaps.reality: The `receipt` number sequence is NEVER seeded and `app_runtime` CANNOT create it. `grep -rn "'receipt'" supabase/` finds the sequence code only at the call site. `shared.number_sequences` has `-- INSERT / DELETE: deliberately NO policy and NO grant for runtime roles` and only `GRANT SELECT ON shared.number_sequences TO app_runtime, app_readonly; GRANT UPDATE (next_value, current_period) ON shared.number_sequences TO app_runtime;`. `shared.next_display_number` raises `'next_display_number: no sequence is configured for code % in this scope' USING ERRCODE = 'no_data_found'` (P0002). The lookup is `ns.company_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM p_company_id AND ns.branch_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM p_branch_id`, so a tenant-wide row does NOT satisfy a branch-scoped call — the row must exist at exactly (tenant, company, branch). No later migration (20260725…20260730) adds an INSERT grant or policy.
gaps.mitigation: Application-level composition only, and it cannot create the row. P1-22 must (a) call `sharedServices().numbers.isProvisioned(db, { sequenceCode: 'receipt', companyId, branchId })` as a pre-flight so the caller gets a typed failure before work is done, and (b) translate SQLSTATE P0002 raised from inside `sal.record_receipt` to `ERR-RES-001` with the same message shape `NumberAllocationService.translate` already uses (`ALLOCATION_SQLSTATE.noSequenceInScope = 'P0002'` in `src/modules/shared-services/data/number-sequence-repository.ts`). Provisioning stays an operator/onboarding action and must be called out as an accepted limitation — P1-22 is not authorized to add the migration that would grant it.

verdict.searched: git rev-parse HEAD (0a53e540d72329e9aef6b196b68627aeb40b4c79, 119 migrations, no 120, working tree clean except untracked docs/phase-1/phase-1-22/). Read in full: supabase/migrations/0003_number_sequences.sql; supabase/migrations/20260729090000_shared_number_sequence_period_hardening.sql (the CURRENTLY deployed allocator body, lines 92-198); supabase/migrations/20260717107000_org_provisioning.sql (lines 1-320, incl. the sequences loop at 239-250); supabase/migrations/20260717106000_shared_number_sequences_org_fks.sql; supabase/migrations/20260718111000_shared_services_hardening.sql; supabase/migrations/20260724092000_sal_payments.sql lines 70-180 (sal.receipts DDL/triggers/policies/grants); supabase/migrations/20260724093000_sal_financial_events.sql lines 195-320 (sal.issue_invoice, sal.record_receipt, sal.allocate_receipt); supabase/migrations/20260724091000_sal_invoices.sql lines 32-120 and 449-475. verdict.reasoning:
Every FACT in the claim is confirmed; the CONCLUSION ("BLOCKER", framed as a gap a migration would close) is refuted. Confirmed facts: (1) No 'receipt' sequence row exists anywhere. `grep -rn "receipt" supabase/ --include=*.sql` finds the code only at the call site `supabase/migrations/20260724093000_sal_financial_events.sql:251` — `SELECT display_number INTO v_number FROM shared.next_display_number('receipt', p_company_id, p_branch_id);`. All six files in supabase/seeds/ contain ZERO occurrences of "sequence", and supabase/seed.sql is a no-op DO block. (2) The grant text is exact: `GRANT SELECT ON shared.number_sequences TO app_runtime, app_readonly;` and `GRANT UPDATE (next_value, current_period) ON shared.number_sequences TO app_runtime;`, preceded by the comment `-- INSERT / DELETE: deliberately NO policy and NO grant for runtime roles.` Only `sel_number_sequences_tenant` (SELECT) and `upd_number_sequences_tenant` (UPDATE) policies exist; RLS is ENABLE + FORCE. (3) The lookup in the CURRENTLY deployed allocator (20260729090000, lines 132-142) is `WHERE ns.tenant_id = v_tenant_id AND ns.sequence_code = p_sequence_code AND ns.company_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM p_company_id AND ns.branch_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM p_branch_id FOR UPDATE;` then `RAISE EXCEPTION 'next_display_number: no sequence is configured for code % in this scope (provisioning is a configuration action — see docs/database/number-sequence-standard.md)' USING ERRCODE = 'no_data_found';` — so a tenant-wide row genuinely does NOT satisfy the branch-scoped call, and `ALLOCATION_SQLSTATE.noSequenceInScope = 'P0002'` (src/modules/shared-services/data/number-sequence-repository.ts:24) is right. (4) None of migrations 20260725…20260730 adds an INSERT grant or policy on shared.number_sequences.

WHY REFUTED. (a) A migration is not merely out of scope — it is FORBIDDEN. docs/database/number-sequence-standard.md §4 "Provisioning is configuration, never schema": sequence rows "are inserted by the administrative provisioning path … never by application runtime code and never hard-coded in a migration"; §7 rule 4 "never schema, never hard-coded"; the standard's own worked example is labelled "ILLUSTRATION ONLY (Phase 1-3+ provisioning path, administrative role)" with `ON CONFLICT ON CONSTRAINT uq_number_sequences_scope DO NOTHING`. A P1-22 migration seeding 'receipt' would violate the standard AND the no-fake-data policy. So the test "refuted=false only if a migration would genuinely be required" fails outright. (b) The administrative path EXISTS and is exercised today: `org.provision_organization(p_spec jsonb, p_idempotency_key text)` takes a `sequences` array (loop at 20260717107000:239-250), and tests/backend/p1-20-helpers.ts:708-722 provisions the branch-scoped 'quotation' row through the admin connection with `INSERT INTO shared.number_sequences (tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, sequence_code, prefix_template, next_value, pad_width, period_reset_rule, created_by) SELECT $1,$2,$3,'quotation','QUO-',1,6,'never',$4 WHERE NOT EXISTS (...)`. No migration. (c) The condition is universal and pre-existing, not a P1-22 discovery. supabase/packages/pilot-provisioning.package.json provisions exactly ONE sequence — `{"code": "org_document", "prefix_template": "DOC-", "pad_width": 6}` — tenant-wide. Seven of the eight codes in SEQUENCE_DEFINITIONS (appointment, business_partner, invoice, quotation, receipt, reception_visit, vehicle, work_order) are unprovisioned, and P1-16/17/18/19/20/21 all closed Go in that state. sequence-registry.ts states the boundary in its own header: "a code being registered here means 'this code is recognised', never 'this code is ready'." (d) The proposed mitigation is already the sanctioned house pattern (reception/crm/quality all call `isProvisioned` then degrade), so it is application composition that is clearly sufficient for what P1-22 may do.

THREE SHARPER FINDINGS THE CLAIM MISSED — record these instead. (1) The real, narrower gap: `org.provision_organization` — the ONLY `INSERT INTO shared.number_sequences` in any migration — inserts `(tenant_id, sequence_code, prefix_template, pad_width, period_reset_rule, created_by)` and CANNOT set company_id or branch_id. It is also `SECURITY INVOKER` with `REVOKE EXECUTE … FROM PUBLIC` and "Deliberately granted to no application role." So the documented onboarding function can only ever produce TENANT-WIDE rows, which by `IS NOT DISTINCT FROM` can never satisfy `sal.record_receipt`'s branch-scoped call. Branch-scoped rows are reachable only by raw admin SQL. That is a genuine hole in the provisioning SURFACE, and it is worth a finding — but it is P1-11/P1-03 scope, not a P1-22 blocker. (2) The claim is scoped too narrowly: `sal.issue_invoice` (20260724093000:222) has the identical dependency — `SELECT display_number INTO v_number FROM shared.next_display_number(v_seq_code, v_inv.company_id, v_inv.branch_id)` where `v_seq_code := COALESCE(sal.invoice_numbering_configs.sequence_code, 'invoice')`. Both P1-22 money paths need branch-scoped rows; flagging only 'receipt' understates it. (3) MUCH more valuable, and unreported: `sal.receipts` has NO insert-time provenance gate. `sal.invoices` does — `sal.guard_invoice_freeze` raises on `TG_OP = 'INSERT'` when `NEW.status <> 'draft'`, with the comment that this closes the bypass of "the gapless shared.next_display_number allocator AND the invoice_issued completeness event". `sal.receipts` has only `tg_receipts_freeze` (BEFORE UPDATE), `tg_receipts_touch_metadata` (BEFORE UPDATE) and `tg_receipts_immutable` (BEFORE UPDATE) — no BEFORE INSERT trigger at all — while holding `GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON sal.receipts TO app_runtime` and policy `ins_receipts_gated`. `receipt_number` is `text NOT NULL` with only `uq_receipts_number UNIQUE (tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, receipt_number)`. A direct INSERT with an application-invented number therefore SUCCEEDS, skipping both the allocator and the `receipt_recorded` financial event. P1-22 must route every receipt through `sal.record_receipt(uuid, uuid, uuid, uuid, text, numeric, uuid, text, uuid)` by discipline because the database does not enforce it — that is the finding that actually protects the phase. Two implementation notes for whatever P1-22 writes: `NumberAllocationService.translate` is `private`, so P1-22 cannot reuse it — when P0002 surfaces from inside `sal.record_receipt` the module must map it itself, matching the existing shape `new AppFailure('ERR-RES-001', { message: 'No number sequence is provisioned for "receipt" in this scope' })`; and `isProvisioned` is a non-atomic pre-flight (a separate `describe` SELECT), so it improves the error, it does not remove the race.

gaps.reality: They cannot. `CONSTRAINT fk_receipts_method FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, payment_method_id) REFERENCES sal.payment_methods (tenant_id, id)` — `sal.receipts.tenant_id` is NOT NULL, and `ck_payment_methods_scope_tenant CHECK ((scope = 'platform' AND tenant_id IS NULL) OR (scope = 'tenant' AND tenant_id IS NOT NULL))` forces every platform row to have `tenant_id IS NULL`. With neither FK column null, MATCH SIMPLE requires an exact `(tenant_id, id)` match, which a NULL-tenant platform row can never satisfy. The P1-11 test fixture concedes it in a comment: `-- 5. A tenant-A payment method (receipts cannot use a platform method — FK is (tenant_id,id)).` `phase-1-11-payment-method-contract.md` does not mention this at all.

P1-22 must therefore ship a tenant payment-method management operation (create/list/deactivate, kind restricted to the three CHECK values) and must present the platform rows as TEMPLATES only, never as selectable methods on a receipt form. Without this operation, no receipt can be recorded in a fresh tenant.

verdict.reasoning:
The archaeologist's FACTUAL diagnosis is correct and I reproduced it from the DDL, but the BLOCKER classification is wrong: no migration is required, so by the stated criterion it is refuted.

VERIFIED FACTS (supabase/migrations/20260724092000_sal_payments.sql):
- L77 `tenant_id uuid NOT NULL`, L81 `payment_method_id uuid NOT NULL` on sal.receipts.
- L104-105 `CONSTRAINT fk_receipts_method FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, payment_method_id) REFERENCES sal.payment_methods (tenant_id, id) ON DELETE RESTRICT` — no MATCH FULL, no DEFERRABLE, no NOT VALID clause.
- L46-47 `CONSTRAINT ck_payment_methods_scope_tenant CHECK ((scope = 'platform' AND tenant_id IS NULL) OR (scope = 'tenant' AND tenant_id IS NOT NULL))`.
Both referencing columns being NOT NULL, MATCH SIMPLE's null-escape never applies; the referenced row must satisfy `tenant_id = <receipt tenant>`, which a NULL tenant_id never does. supabase/seeds/08_sal_payment_methods.sql inserts all three rows as ('platform', NULL, ...). tests/db/p1-11-helpers.ts L144 concedes it: "-- 5. A tenant-A payment method (receipts cannot use a platform method — FK is (tenant_id,id))." So platform methods are genuinely unusable on a receipt.

WHY IT IS NOT A BLOCKER (application composition is clearly sufficient, zero DDL needed):
- L69 `GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON sal.payment_methods TO app_runtime`.
- L64-65 `CREATE POLICY ins_payment_methods_tenant ON sal.payment_methods FOR INSERT TO app_runtime WITH CHECK (scope = 'tenant' AND tenant_id = iam.current_tenant_id())`.
- L66-68 `upd_payment_methods_tenant` USING/WITH CHECK the same predicate — deactivate via `status='inactive'` (ck_payment_methods_status CHECK (status IN ('active','inactive'))) or `deleted_at`; `tg_payment_methods_immutable` freezes only 'scope','tenant_id','created_at','created_by', so status/display_name/method_code/deleted_at remain updatable.
- L54 `uq_payment_methods_platform_code ... WHERE scope='platform'` and L55 `uq_payment_methods_tenant_code (tenant_id, method_code) WHERE scope='tenant'` are SEPARATE partial indexes, so a tenant may create method_code='cash' with no collision — a faithful clone of the platform template is legal.
- L49 `ck_payment_methods_kind CHECK (kind IN ('cash','card_terminal','bank_transfer'))` admits exactly the three seeded kinds.
Therefore a P1-22 tenant payment-method management operation (create/list/deactivate) is fully composable from already-granted DML. No migration 120.

THREE ADDITIONS/CORRECTIONS THE ARCHAEOLOGIST MISSED:
1. They under-sold their evidence. sal.receipts is the ONLY dual-scope-catalog consumer with a composite FK. `inv.item_master` uses `CONSTRAINT fk_item_master_uom FOREIGN KEY (uom_id) REFERENCES inv.units_of_measure (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT` (20260723093000_inv_reference.sql L235) and `shared.documents` uses `FOREIGN KEY (category_id) REFERENCES shared.document_categories (id) ON DELETE RESTRICT` (20260718100000 L155) — both SINGLE-column, so their platform rows ARE usable. The receipts FK is the schema's odd one out, which makes the behaviour look unintended. Still not migration-requiring.
2. THE SHARPER GAP THEY MISSED: there is NO permission code for payment-method management. supabase/seeds/04_iam_permission_catalog.sql carries exactly ten sal.* codes (sal.invoice.manage, sal.invoice.issue, sal.payment.record, sal.payment.allocate, sal.credit.manage, sal.reversal.approve, sal.finance.view, sal.delivery.manage, sal.delivery.complete, sal.delivery.view) and no sal.payment_method.*. The ins_/upd_ policies carry NO iam.has_permission(...) predicate at all, only a tenant match, so at DB level any app_runtime session in the tenant can mint a payment method; the gate must be purely application-side. Still not a migration: the catalog is a SEED, and P1-21 commit 08544ca ("expose the inventory API surface and register its catalogs") added four inv.* codes to that same seed file with no migration.
3. There is NO DELETE grant (only SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE), so "deactivate" must be an UPDATE, never a DELETE.

DIVERGENCE (DDL authoritative): phase-1-11-payment-method-contract.md states the composite FK shape but never draws the conclusion, and asserts "SELECT is visible for scope='platform' OR tenant_id = iam.current_tenant_id()" as though platform rows were selectable on a receipt. seeds/08_sal_payment_methods.sql L4-6 is affirmatively misleading: "a receipt is meaningless without a payment method, so the platform ships the three allowed methods". phase-1-11-receipt-contract.md L12-13 and phase-1-11-p1-22-backend-contract.md L18 mention the FK / p_method_id with no scope guidance. The prose should be corrected; the schema should not.

NET: downgrade from BLOCKER to a P1-22 scope requirement plus a documentation-correction finding. The mitigation the archaeologist proposed is exactly right and is fully supported by existing grants — which is precisely what makes it not a blocker.
