verdict.reasoning:
The archaeologist's FACTS are 100% correct — I confirmed every one and found three more supporting facts they missed. What I refute is the BLOCKER classification: no migration is required, because the backend can close this completely, not merely mitigate it.

=== CONFIRMED (deployed catalog + source) ===

sal.credit_notes deployed constraints (9): ck_credit_notes_amount `CHECK (amount > 0)`, ck_credit_notes_approval_state, ck_credit_notes_approved_distinct, ck_credit_notes_approved_shape, fk_credit_notes_currency `FOREIGN KEY (currency_code) REFERENCES shared.currencies(code) ON DELETE RESTRICT`, fk_credit_notes_invoice `FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, invoice_id) REFERENCES sal.invoices(tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, id)` — carries NO currency, fk_credit_notes_tenant, pk_credit_notes, uq_credit_notes_scope_id. Triggers exactly as claimed: tg_credit_notes_stamp_maker, tg_credit_notes_approval, tg_credit_notes_touch_metadata, tg_credit_notes_immutable, tg_credit_notes_event_completeness. NONE compares currency to the invoice.

sal.receipt_reversals deployed constraints (10): same shape; fk_receipt_reversals_receipt carries no currency. NONE compares currency to the receipt.

`sal.approve_credit_note` compares only `IF v_cn.amount > v_open`. `sal.approve_receipt_reversal` compares only `IF v_rev.amount <> v_rcpt.amount`. `sal.allocate_receipt` is the ONLY currency enforcement in the whole schema: `IF v_inv.currency_code <> v_rcpt.currency_code THEN RAISE EXCEPTION ... USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation'`.

`sal.invoice_open_receivable` sums credit notes with NO currency predicate — confirmed verbatim: `SELECT COALESCE(sum(amount), 0) INTO v_credit FROM sal.credit_notes WHERE tenant_id = v_tenant AND invoice_id = p_invoice_id AND approval_state = 'approved';`

Docs claiming enforcement that does not exist: phase-1-11-design.md:381 "(CHECK/composite FK)"; phase-1-11-review-response.md:94 "(CHECK + composite FK)"; phase-1-11-financial-precision-currency-contract.md:21 "Coherence is enforced (M-fin-4)"; abuse-case-ledger.md:37 case 22 residual "none"; both table COMMENTs; and the 20260724092000 migration header itself lists M-fin-4 under "Binding design amendments IMPLEMENTED HERE".

=== THREE FACTS THE ARCHAEOLOGIST MISSED ===

(A) The composite-FK mechanism named in the design doc is STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE against the deployed parent keys. A composite FK carrying currency needs a parent unique key containing currency_code. sal.invoices has only pk_invoices(id), uq_invoices_scope_id(tenant_id,company_id,branch_id,id), uq_invoices_number, uq_invoices_idempotency, uq_invoices_work_order_active. sal.receipts has only pk_receipts(id), uq_receipts_scope_id, uq_receipts_number. None contains currency_code. So M-fin-4 was not merely omitted — as documented it was never buildable.

(B) A DRIFT WINDOW survives naive server-side forcing. `sal.guard_invoice_freeze` freezes currency only when `OLD.status <> 'draft'`, and tg_invoices_immutable does NOT list currency_code. So a draft invoice's currency is mutable: create a credit note against a USD draft, flip the draft to JOD, issue it — approve_credit_note is currency-blind and approves. Forcing currency only at credit-note creation does NOT close this; P1-22 must ALSO re-validate at approval.

(C) `sal.reverse_receipt` DOES NOT EXIST anywhere in the 119 migrations, despite the sal.receipt_reversals COMMENT asserting "amount = original receipt amount (enforced in reverse_receipt)". There is no creation-side primitive for reversals or credit notes at all — so P1-22 must INSERT into both tables directly, which is precisely why server-side forcing is load-bearing.

=== WHY NOT A BLOCKER ===

A migration is not genuinely required, on three verified grounds:

1. `currency_code` is settable ONLY at INSERT. The deployed, untruncated trigger args are `org.guard_immutable_columns('tenant_id','company_id','branch_id','invoice_id','currency_code','created_at','created_by')` on credit_notes and `(...,'original_receipt_id','currency_code',...)` on receipt_reversals. The function raises `check_violation` on ANY change. A value written correctly at insert is frozen by the DATABASE forever.
2. `app_runtime` is the only application role with INSERT (deployed privileges: app_runtime INSERT/SELECT/UPDATE, app_readonly SELECT, postgres as owner). The backend is the sole writer — there is no second path.
3. Therefore a backend that reads the parent's currency server-side and never accepts it from the client produces rows correct at birth and immutable thereafter. That is COMPLETE CLOSURE at the only mutable point, not a mitigation. The archaeologist's own MITIGATION section concedes exactly this.

A gap that the phase's own permitted, backend-only work can fully close is not a BLOCKER — it is a required named backend invariant plus a documentation-accuracy defect.

=== WHAT SHOULD STILL BE RAISED ===
- P1-22 must force credit_notes.currency_code from sal.invoices.currency_code and receipt_reversals.currency_code from sal.receipts.currency_code, server-side at insert, never client-supplied — a named, tested invariant.
- It must ALSO re-validate currency at approval to close drift window (B), which the archaeologist's prescription does not cover.
- Abuse case 22's "residual: none" is FALSE, and the "CHECK + composite FK" claims are unsupported by deployed DDL. Per the P1-21 model's rule that the DDL is authoritative, raise this as a documentation-divergence finding against P1-11, carried into P1-22 as residual risk — the correct severity is a documented residual-risk/defence-in-depth finding, not a blocker.

reports.lens: Cancellation, credit notes, financial events, and immutability — protected-contract archaeology of `sal.financial_events`, `sal.credit_notes`, `sal.receipt_reversals`, and the invoice/receipt freeze surface, read from the deployed DDL in migrations `20260724091000_sal_invoices.sql`, `20260724092000_sal_payments.sql`, `20260724093000_sal_financial_events.sql` (plus `20260724090000`, `20260724095000`, `0002`, `0003`, `20260717101000`, `20260718096000`, `20260718097000`, `20260725090000`) at `d9a2c1dc8d09e8fe2b3cf9ca8a2d4a6c905756de`. Where the P1-11 handoff prose and the deployed DDL disagree, the DDL is recorded as authoritative.
reports.summary: The protected schema makes financial facts append-only by *withholding privilege*, not by trigger: `sal.financial_events`, `sal.payment_allocations`, `sal.invoice_status_history` and `wty.warranty_status_history` hold `GRANT SELECT, INSERT` only, and every one of the 27 P1-11 tables has zero `DELETE` grant and zero `FOR DELETE`/`FOR ALL` policy under `ENABLE`+`FORCE` RLS, so UPDATE and DELETE on a financial event are denied at two independent layers. The event vocabulary is closed at six `event_type` values and five `source_type` values, each event is single-use per `(tenant, source_type, source_id, event_type)`, its amount and currency are bound to the named source row in its terminal state by `sal.guard_financial_event_provenance`, and five `DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED` constraint triggers make the matching event a commit-time obligation. Cancellation is deliberately narrow: an invoice may only be voided while still `draft` (`void_before_issue`), an issued invoice can never be un-issued and may only advance to the terminal `credited`, a recorded receipt's money facts are frozen and may only be undone through a dual-control full-receipt reversal, and corrections are always new linked rows — never edits or deletes. Dual control is server-stamped: `sal.stamp_dual_control_maker` overwrites `requested_by` on INSERT and nulls the approval columns, and `sal.guard_dual_control_approval` stamps `approved_by`/`approved_at` and rejects maker=approver. The credit-note surface is thinner than the handoff prose claims: there is no credit-note number and no `credit_note` sequence code, no credit-note lines, no `sal.reverse_receipt` function despite the table comment naming it, no currency-equality constraint between a credit note and its invoice (M-fin-4 is documented as "CHECK + composite FK" and no such CHECK exists), no primitive or guard that ever sets `sal.invoices.status = 'credited'`, and "immutable once approved" is false for `reason`, `approved_at`, `issued_at`, `reversed_at` and `idempotency_key`. Two further contract holes matter operationally: `sal.issue_invoice` and `sal.record_receipt` demand a *branch-scoped* `shared.number_sequences` row that no seed and no provisioning path creates and that `app_runtime` has no INSERT privilege to create, and `sal.invoice_open_receivable` returns `0` rather than an error to a caller lacking `sal.finance.view`. Every financial command in this lens additionally requires `sal.finance.view`, because the `ins_financial_events_gated` RLS policy gates the event insert on it.

findings.fact: `sal.financial_events` immutability is enforced by absent privilege and absent policy, not by a trigger. `app_runtime` receives only SELECT+INSERT, and the table carries exactly two policies (SELECT, INSERT) under ENABLE + FORCE RLS, so UPDATE and DELETE are denied both by missing grant and by having no permissive policy.
findings.evidence: `ALTER TABLE sal.financial_events ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;` / `ALTER TABLE sal.financial_events FORCE  ROW LEVEL SECURITY;` / `CREATE POLICY sel_financial_events_gated ... FOR SELECT TO app_runtime, app_readonly` / `CREATE POLICY ins_financial_events_gated ... FOR INSERT TO app_runtime` / `GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON sal.financial_events TO app_runtime;` `GRANT SELECT ON sal.financial_events TO app_readonly;`
findings.consequence: The P1-22 backend must never emit an UPDATE or DELETE against `sal.financial_events` and must not build any correction path that assumes one. A correction is a new event from a new source row. There is no 'fix the event' code path to write.

findings.fact: There is no DELETE grant on ANY table created by the six P1-11 migrations, and no `FOR DELETE` or `FOR ALL` policy exists on any `sal`/`wty`/`rpt` table. `app_runtime` and `app_readonly` are `NOBYPASSRLS` non-owners.
findings.identifier: GRANT statements in 20260724091000/092000/093000/094000/095000/096000; CREATE ROLE app_runtime in 0002_base_schemas.sql
findings.evidence: Every grant is one of `GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON <t> TO app_runtime;`, `GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON <t> TO app_runtime;`, `GRANT SELECT ON <t> TO app_readonly;` — the token DELETE never appears in a GRANT. `CREATE ROLE app_runtime NOLOGIN NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOREPLICATION NOBYPASSRLS;`
findings.consequence: Hard deletion is unreachable from the backend for the entire billing/payment/delivery/warranty surface. Any P1-22 route shaped as 'delete invoice', 'delete credit note', 'delete receipt' must be refused at design time; the only removal verbs available are soft-delete (where a `deleted_at` column exists) and status transition.

findings.fact: The financial-event vocabulary is closed and exactly six values; the source vocabulary is exactly five values. Nothing else may be written.
findings.evidence: `CONSTRAINT ck_financial_events_event_type CHECK (event_type IN ('invoice_issued', 'receipt_recorded', 'payment_allocated', 'credit_note_issued', 'receipt_reversed', 'warranty_split_recorded')),` and `CONSTRAINT ck_financial_events_source_type CHECK (source_type IN ('invoice', 'receipt', 'payment_allocation', 'credit_note', 'receipt_reversal'))`
findings.consequence: P1-22 transcribes these twelve literals verbatim into its domain constants. There is NO `invoice_voided`, `invoice_credited`, `credit_note_rejected`, `receipt_reversal_requested`, `delivery_completed`, or `warranty_issued` event type — voiding, rejecting, delivering and warranty issue produce NO financial event and the backend must not pretend otherwise.

findings.fact: Every financial event is single-use per source command, which is what makes replay safe at the data layer.
findings.evidence: `-- Single-use: one event per (source command, event type). invoice_issued and warranty_split_recorded share source_type='invoice' but differ by event_type.` / `CONSTRAINT uq_financial_events_source UNIQUE (tenant_id, source_type, source_id, event_type)`
findings.consequence: A replayed P1-22 command that re-emits its event fails with `23505` on this constraint, aborting the whole transaction. The backend must short-circuit replays before the insert (read the source row's state first), not rely on catching the unique violation, because the abort also discards any display number allocated in the same transaction.

findings.fact: `sal.guard_financial_event_provenance` (BEFORE INSERT) requires the named source row to exist in the event's tenant, to be in its authorized/terminal state, and binds both `amount` and `currency_code` to that source. A forged event with no valid source is rejected with `check_violation`.
findings.evidence: `ELSIF NEW.event_type = 'credit_note_issued' THEN SELECT amount, currency_code INTO v_amount, v_currency FROM sal.credit_notes WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND id = NEW.source_id AND approval_state = 'approved';` … `IF NOT v_ok THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'sal.financial_events: no authorized % source % for event %' ... USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation'; END IF; IF NEW.amount <> v_amount THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'sal.financial_events: amount % does not bind the source amount %' ...; END IF; IF NEW.currency_code <> v_currency THEN RAISE EXCEPTION ...`
findings.consequence: P1-22 must write the source row to its terminal state FIRST and only then insert the event, with the amount and currency copied verbatim from the persisted source row — not from the request body. The ordering inside `sal.approve_credit_note` (UPDATE the credit note to 'approved', then INSERT the event) is the mandatory shape; reversing it fails.

findings.fact: Five commit-time constraint triggers make the matching event mandatory: a financial command that fails to write its event aborts at COMMIT, not at statement time.
findings.evidence: `CREATE CONSTRAINT TRIGGER tg_credit_notes_event_completeness AFTER UPDATE ON sal.credit_notes DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED FOR EACH ROW WHEN (NEW.approval_state = 'approved') EXECUTE FUNCTION sal.guard_event_completeness();` and in the function `RAISE EXCEPTION 'sal.%: financial command produced no % event (completeness)', TG_TABLE_NAME, v_type USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation';`
findings.consequence: P1-22 must keep the source-row write and the event insert in ONE transaction. Because the trigger is DEFERRED, the failure surfaces at COMMIT with SQLSTATE 23514 and no statement context — the backend's error mapper must handle a commit-time `check_violation` and not assume every 23514 arrives from the failing statement.

findings.fact: `sal.financial_events.seq` is `bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY` and `amount` is `numeric(18,4)` with a `>= 0` (not `> 0`) check — so a zero-amount event is legal at the event layer even though every source amount check is `> 0`.
findings.evidence: `seq            bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY,` / `amount         numeric(18, 4) NOT NULL,` / `CONSTRAINT ck_financial_events_amount CHECK (amount >= 0)`
findings.consequence: P1-22 must never supply `seq` on insert (GENERATED ALWAYS rejects an explicit value without OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE), and must carry `amount` as an exact decimal string across the `pg` boundary — never `parseFloat`/`Number`/`toFixed`. The `>= 0` asymmetry means a zero `warranty_split_recorded` is representable; `sal.issue_invoice` nevertheless only emits it `IF v_wty > 0`.

findings.fact: The `ins_financial_events_gated` INSERT policy requires `iam.has_permission('sal.finance.view')`. Because every financial command must emit an event, `sal.finance.view` is a hard prerequisite for issuing an invoice, recording a receipt, allocating, approving a credit note and approving a reversal.
findings.evidence: `CREATE POLICY ins_financial_events_gated ON sal.financial_events FOR INSERT TO app_runtime WITH CHECK (tenant_id = iam.current_tenant_id() AND iam.has_permission('sal.finance.view') AND (iam.allowed_company_ids() IS NULL OR company_id = ANY (iam.allowed_company_ids())) AND (iam.allowed_branch_ids() IS NULL OR branch_id = ANY (iam.allowed_branch_ids())));`
findings.consequence: Holding `sal.invoice.issue` alone is NOT sufficient — the transaction dies on the event insert with SQLSTATE 42501 ('new row violates row-level security policy'). P1-22 must require BOTH the command permission and `sal.finance.view` in its own authorization layer, and say so in the route contract, rather than letting an RLS 42501 surface as an opaque 500.

findings.fact: The RLS gates use the scope-blind `iam.has_permission('sal.finance.view')`, not `iam.has_permission_in_scope`.
findings.identifier: sel_/ins_/upd_ policies on sal.invoice_amounts, sal.invoice_line_amounts, sal.receipts, sal.payment_allocations, sal.credit_notes, sal.receipt_reversals, sal.financial_events
findings.evidence: `USING (tenant_id = iam.current_tenant_id() AND iam.has_permission('sal.finance.view') AND (iam.allowed_company_ids() IS NULL OR company_id = ANY (iam.allowed_company_ids())) ...)` — `iam.has_permission(p_code text)` resolves `bool_or(rp.effect = 'allow') ... AND NOT ... deny` across ALL active grants with no scope predicate.
findings.consequence: Per P1-18-A-01 the allowed_company/branch arrays are the union of every active grant regardless of which permission carries it, so RLS is defence in depth only. Every branch-scoped P1-22 finance operation must still pass a concrete authorization target so the application evaluates `iam.has_permission_in_scope(code, company, branch)`.

findings.fact: `sal.credit_notes` is a header-only, invoice-linked, whole-row finance-gated table with server-stamped dual control. There are no credit-note lines and no credit-note number column.
findings.evidence: Column list is exactly `id, tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, invoice_id, currency_code, amount numeric(18, 4), reason text NOT NULL, approval_state text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending', requested_by, approved_by, approved_at, issued_at, idempotency_key, record_version, created_at, created_by, updated_at, updated_by` — note there is NO `deleted_at`. `CONSTRAINT fk_credit_notes_invoice FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, invoice_id) REFERENCES sal.invoices (tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, id) ON DELETE RESTRICT`
findings.consequence: A P1-22 credit note is one amount against one invoice with a mandatory free-text `reason`, in the invoice's own (tenant, company, branch). No line-level credit is representable. Because there is no `deleted_at`, a credit note can never be soft-deleted either — the only retraction is the `rejected` decision.

findings.fact: Credit-note approval vocabulary and shape are fixed by four CHECK constraints; self-approval AND self-rejection are both blocked, because `ck_credit_notes_approved_distinct` also applies on the reject path where the guard stamps `approved_by`.
findings.evidence: `CONSTRAINT ck_credit_notes_approval_state CHECK (approval_state IN ('pending', 'approved', 'rejected')),` `CONSTRAINT ck_credit_notes_approved_distinct CHECK (approved_by IS NULL OR approved_by <> requested_by),` `CONSTRAINT ck_credit_notes_approved_shape CHECK ((approval_state = 'approved') = (approved_by IS NOT NULL AND approved_at IS NOT NULL AND issued_at IS NOT NULL))` and in the guard `ELSIF OLD.approval_state = 'pending' AND NEW.approval_state = 'rejected' THEN NEW.approved_by := iam.current_user_id(); NEW.approved_at := now();`
findings.consequence: The three-value vocabulary `pending|approved|rejected` is transcribed as-is. A requester CANNOT withdraw or reject their own pending credit note — the CHECK fires with 23514. P1-22 must model retraction as 'a second person rejects', and must not offer a 'cancel my request' route that would always fail.

findings.fact: Dual control is server-stamped on both sides and cannot be client-supplied.
findings.identifier: sal.stamp_dual_control_maker / tg_credit_notes_stamp_maker / tg_receipt_reversals_stamp_maker; sal.guard_dual_control_approval / tg_credit_notes_approval / tg_receipt_reversals_approval
findings.evidence: `NEW.requested_by := iam.current_user_id(); IF NEW.requested_by IS NULL THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'dual control: no user context (requested_by cannot be stamped)' USING ERRCODE = 'insufficient_privilege'; END IF; NEW.approved_by := NULL; NEW.approved_at := NULL;` and `NEW.approved_by := iam.current_user_id(); NEW.approved_at := now(); ... IF NEW.approved_by = NEW.requested_by THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'dual control: the approver must differ from the requester (maker<>approver)' USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation';`
findings.consequence: P1-22 must not send `requested_by`, `approved_by` or `approved_at` in any insert or update — they are overwritten. A missing session user context yields SQLSTATE 28000 (`insufficient_privilege`), which the backend must map to an auth failure, not a validation failure.

findings.fact: `sal.approve_credit_note` bounds the credit by the derived open receivable under an explicit invoice row lock, and is idempotent by approval state. It does NOT accept or check an idempotency key.
findings.identifier: sal.approve_credit_note(p_credit_id uuid, p_correlation_id uuid DEFAULT NULL)
findings.evidence: `IF v_cn.approval_state = 'approved' THEN RETURN; END IF; -- idempotent` / `IF v_cn.approval_state <> 'pending' THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'sal.approve_credit_note: credit note is %', v_cn.approval_state USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation'; END IF;` / `PERFORM 1 FROM sal.invoices WHERE id = v_cn.invoice_id ... FOR UPDATE; v_open := sal.invoice_open_receivable(v_cn.invoice_id); IF v_cn.amount > v_open THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'sal.approve_credit_note: credit % exceeds invoice open receivable %' ... USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation';`
findings.consequence: P1-22 calls this primitive rather than hand-rolling approval: the FOR UPDATE on the invoice before deriving is what stops concurrent credits driving the receivable below zero. Its two-argument signature is `(uuid, uuid)`; replay protection for the approve command is the state check, so the backend's Idempotency-Key store is the only request-level replay defence for approvals.

findings.fact: A credit note against a draft or voided invoice can be CREATED but can never be APPROVED, because `sal.invoice_open_receivable` returns 0 for those statuses and `ck_credit_notes_amount CHECK (amount > 0)` makes `amount <= 0` unrepresentable.
findings.evidence: `IF v_status IS NULL OR v_status IN ('draft', 'void_before_issue') THEN RETURN 0; END IF;` and `CONSTRAINT ck_credit_notes_amount CHECK (amount > 0)`
findings.consequence: The FK only requires the invoice to exist in scope, so P1-22 must reject credit-note creation against a non-issued invoice in the application layer; otherwise a caller can park a permanently unapprovable pending row that no one can delete and only a second user can reject.

findings.fact: Receipt reversal is full-amount only, at most one per receipt, and the amount equality is enforced inside the approval primitive under the receipt row lock — not by a constraint.
findings.identifier: uq_receipt_reversals_receipt, sal.approve_receipt_reversal(p_reversal_id uuid, p_correlation_id uuid DEFAULT NULL)
findings.evidence: `-- H-fin-1: full-receipt reversal — at most one reversal per receipt.` / `CONSTRAINT uq_receipt_reversals_receipt UNIQUE (tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, original_receipt_id),` and `IF v_rev.amount <> v_rcpt.amount THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'sal.approve_receipt_reversal: full-receipt reversal amount % must equal receipt amount %', v_rev.amount, v_rcpt.amount USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation'; END IF;`
findings.consequence: P1-22 must not expose a partial-reversal amount field. It must also validate amount = receipt amount before insert, because the DDL alone permits a mismatched pending reversal row to be stored and only rejects it at approval time.

findings.fact: A receipt can reach `reversed` ONLY when an approved reversal already exists — the freeze guard closes the raw-UPDATE path, and `reversed` is terminal.
findings.evidence: `IF NEW.status = 'reversed' THEN IF NOT EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM sal.receipt_reversals rr WHERE ... AND rr.approval_state = 'approved') THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'sal.receipts: a receipt may be reversed only via an approved receipt reversal (sal.approve_receipt_reversal)' USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation'; END IF; END IF;` / `IF OLD.status = 'reversed' THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'sal.receipts: reversed is terminal' USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation';` / `CONSTRAINT ck_receipts_status CHECK (status IN ('recorded', 'partially_allocated', 'allocated', 'reversed'))`
findings.consequence: The receipt status vocabulary is exactly those four values. P1-22 has no 'un-reverse' path and must not build one. The ordering inside `sal.approve_receipt_reversal` (approve the reversal, THEN flip the receipt) is mandatory and is documented in the migration itself as such.

findings.fact: A recorded receipt's money-bearing facts are frozen; only status advances. `received_by`, `evidence_document_version_id`, `idempotency_key` and `deleted_at` are NOT in the frozen set.
findings.evidence: `IF NEW.amount <> OLD.amount OR NEW.currency_code <> OLD.currency_code OR NEW.payment_method_id <> OLD.payment_method_id OR NEW.payer_partner_id <> OLD.payer_partner_id OR NEW.received_at IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.received_at OR NEW.receipt_number <> OLD.receipt_number THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'sal.receipts: a recorded receipt''s amount/method/payer/currency/received_at/number are frozen (corrections via reversal only)'` plus `org.guard_immutable_columns('tenant_id', 'company_id', 'branch_id', 'created_at', 'created_by')`
findings.consequence: P1-22 may attach or replace payment evidence after the fact, but must forbid edits to who received the money (`received_by`) and must never soft-delete a receipt — neither is blocked by the database (see gaps).

findings.fact: Invoice cancellation is only possible before issue. `void_before_issue` is reachable only from `draft`, `credited` and `void_before_issue` are terminal, an invoice is born draft, and status advances forward only.
findings.evidence: `IF TG_OP = 'INSERT' THEN IF NEW.status <> 'draft' THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'sal.invoices: a new invoice must be created as draft (status % is not allowed on insert; issue via sal.issue_invoice)'` / `IF OLD.status = 'issued' AND NEW.status <> 'credited' THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'sal.invoices: an issued invoice may only advance to credited'` / `IF OLD.status IN ('credited', 'void_before_issue') THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'sal.invoices: % is terminal'` / `CONSTRAINT ck_invoices_status CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'issued', 'credited', 'void_before_issue'))` / `CONSTRAINT ck_invoices_number_iff_issued CHECK ((invoice_number IS NULL AND issued_at IS NULL) = (status IN ('draft', 'void_before_issue')))`
findings.consequence: P1-22's cancellation contract is exactly: void a draft (no number consumed, no financial event, no history row written automatically), or credit an issued invoice. `partially_paid`/`paid` are NOT invoice statuses — they exist only in the history CHECK (`ck_invoice_status_history_to_status CHECK (to_status IN ('draft','issued','partially_paid','paid','credited','void_before_issue'))`) and are derived, never stored on the invoice.

findings.fact: Issued invoice content is frozen at three layers: the header identity by the freeze guard, and BOTH amount tables reject every INSERT and UPDATE once the parent invoice leaves draft.
findings.identifier: sal.guard_invoice_freeze, sal.guard_invoice_amount_frozen / tg_invoice_amounts_frozen, sal.guard_invoice_line_frozen, sal.guard_invoice_line_amount_frozen, tg_invoice_line_amounts_reconcile
findings.evidence: `IF v_status <> 'draft' THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'sal.invoice_amounts: parent invoice is % (not draft); header totals are frozen', v_status USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation'; END IF;` (identically worded guards exist for `sal.invoice_lines` and `sal.invoice_line_amounts`), plus the deferred `CREATE CONSTRAINT TRIGGER tg_invoice_line_amounts_reconcile AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON sal.invoice_line_amounts DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED`
findings.consequence: P1-22 must write ALL amounts while the invoice is still `draft`. `sal.issue_invoice` deliberately writes the header totals before flipping the status; a backend that composes issue by hand must preserve that order or the amounts write is rejected with 23514.

findings.fact: Open receivable is derived, never stored, and reversed receipts' allocations are excluded — which is what restores the receivable without touching the append-only allocation rows.
findings.evidence: `SELECT COALESCE(sum(pa.amount), 0) INTO v_alloc FROM sal.payment_allocations pa JOIN sal.receipts r ON ... WHERE pa.tenant_id = v_tenant AND pa.invoice_id = p_invoice_id AND r.status <> 'reversed'; SELECT COALESCE(sum(amount), 0) INTO v_credit FROM sal.credit_notes WHERE tenant_id = v_tenant AND invoice_id = p_invoice_id AND approval_state = 'approved'; RETURN round(v_gross - v_alloc - v_credit, 4);`
findings.consequence: The formula is fixed by the schema: `open = gross − Σ(non-reversed allocations) − Σ(approved credit notes)`, rounded to 4. P1-22 must call these `STABLE SECURITY INVOKER` functions (granted to `app_runtime` AND `app_readonly`) rather than reimplement the arithmetic, and must not cache the result without invalidating on allocation, credit and reversal.

findings.fact: Allocation to an invoice in the terminal `credited` state is explicitly permitted.
findings.evidence: `IF v_inv.status NOT IN ('issued', 'credited') THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'sal.allocate_receipt: invoice is % (must be issued)', v_inv.status USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation'; END IF;`
findings.consequence: P1-22 must not treat `credited` as 'closed to payment'. A partially credited invoice with residual open receivable can still receive allocations, and the route contract must allow it.

findings.fact: The append-only status ledgers are server-stamped and their actor cannot be forged or backdated.
findings.evidence: `NEW.actor_id := iam.current_user_id(); IF NEW.actor_id IS NULL THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'status history requires an actor in the session context' USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation'; END IF; NEW.occurred_at := now();`
findings.consequence: P1-22 supplies only `(tenant, company, branch, <entity>_id, from_status, to_status, reason, correlation_id)`; sending `actor_id`/`occurred_at` is pointless. `reason` is nullable on `sal.invoice_status_history`, so any requirement that a void carries a reason is an application-layer rule with no database backing.

findings.fact: The permission codes that exist for this lens are exactly seven `sal` codes, seeded as platform structural reference.
findings.identifier: supabase/seeds/04_iam_permission_catalog.sql — sal.invoice.manage, sal.invoice.issue, sal.payment.record, sal.payment.allocate, sal.credit.manage, sal.reversal.approve, sal.finance.view (plus sal.delivery.manage/complete/view, wty.policy.manage, wty.warranty.issue)
findings.evidence: `('sal.credit.manage', 'sal', 'Request and manage credit notes', 'high', ...), ('sal.reversal.approve', 'sal', 'Approve receipt reversals (dual control)', 'high', ...), ('sal.finance.view', 'sal', 'View financial amounts (invoices/receipts/events)', 'high', ...)`
findings.consequence: P1-22 reuses these before minting anything. `sal.credit.manage` already carries request AND manage of credit notes by its own description; there is NO `sal.invoice.void` and NO `sal.credit.approve` code (see gaps). Any new code must be justified as naming an authority no existing code carries, exactly as P1-21 did for its four `inv` codes.

findings.fact: `sal.issue_invoice` resolves the numbering sequence code from a per-(tenant,company) config with a hard-coded fallback of `'invoice'`, and the config's `sequence_code` is only spelling-constrained.
findings.evidence: `SELECT sequence_code INTO v_seq_code FROM sal.invoice_numbering_configs WHERE tenant_id = v_inv.tenant_id AND company_id = v_inv.company_id AND status = 'active' AND deleted_at IS NULL; v_seq_code := COALESCE(v_seq_code, 'invoice');` / `CONSTRAINT ck_invoice_numbering_configs_sequence_code CHECK (sequence_code ~ '^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,62}$')` / `CONSTRAINT ck_invoice_numbering_configs_mode CHECK (mode IN ('gapless', 'gapped'))`
findings.consequence: A tenant may configure a `sequence_code` that the application-side allow-list `SEQUENCE_DEFINITIONS` in src/modules/shared-services/domain/sequence-registry.ts does not recognise (it knows only 8 codes: appointment, business_partner, invoice, quotation, receipt, reception_visit, vehicle, work_order). P1-22 must validate a configured code against that registry when exposing a numbering-config write route, and must transcribe `gapless|gapped` and `active|inactive` verbatim.

gaps.assumed: A credit note and a receipt reversal are immutable once approved — `phase-1-11-append-only-immutability-matrix.md` lists both under "Immutable-after-issue / approval" and the credit-note contract says "Once approved, the row is immutable".
gaps.reality: Only four columns freeze. `sal.guard_dual_control_approval`'s post-decision branch is `IF NEW.approval_state <> OLD.approval_state OR NEW.requested_by <> OLD.requested_by OR NEW.approved_by IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.approved_by OR NEW.amount <> OLD.amount THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'dual control: a % decision is frozen'`, and `org.guard_immutable_columns` covers only `('tenant_id','company_id','branch_id','invoice_id','currency_code','created_at','created_by')`. Therefore `reason`, `approved_at`, `issued_at` and `idempotency_key` on an APPROVED credit note remain writable by any holder of `sal.finance.view` (`upd_credit_notes_gated` permits the UPDATE), subject only to `ck_credit_notes_approved_shape` keeping them non-null. `sal.receipt_reversals` is identical for `reason`, `approved_at`, `reversed_at`, `idempotency_key`.
gaps.mitigation: P1-22 must never expose an update route for an approved credit note or reversal, and should treat the four mutable columns as write-once in its repository layer. There is no database backstop, so the guarantee is application-only and must be recorded as such rather than inherited from the P1-11 matrix.

gaps.assumed: A credit note carries a human-facing credit-note number, allocated the way invoice and receipt numbers are.
gaps.reality: `sal.credit_notes` has NO number column of any kind — the column list is `id, tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, invoice_id, currency_code, amount, reason, approval_state, requested_by, approved_by, approved_at, issued_at, idempotency_key, record_version, created_at, created_by, updated_at, updated_by`. There is no `credit_note` entry in `shared.number_sequences` seeding, and `SEQUENCE_DEFINITIONS` in src/modules/shared-services/domain/sequence-registry.ts registers only `appointment, business_partner, invoice, quotation, receipt, reception_visit, vehicle, work_order`. Receipt reversals have no number either.
gaps.mitigation: P1-22 must identify credit notes and reversals by their `id` (and their invoice/receipt linkage) and MUST NOT invent a numbering scheme, prefix, or `credit_note` sequence code — adding one is a migration, which this phase is forbidden to write. If a printed credit-note number is a product requirement it is a documented carried-forward obligation for a later DB phase, not something P1-22 fabricates.

gaps.assumed: `sal.reverse_receipt` exists — `COMMENT ON TABLE sal.receipt_reversals` names it as the enforcement point: "amount = original receipt amount (enforced in reverse_receipt)", and `phase-1-11-receipt-reversal-contract.md` repeats "(enforced in the approval primitive under the receipt lock)".
gaps.reality: There is NO function named `sal.reverse_receipt` anywhere in the 119 migrations. `grep -rn "reverse_receipt" supabase/` returns exactly one hit — that table comment. The amount equality is in fact enforced in `sal.approve_receipt_reversal`. Symmetrically, there is NO primitive to CREATE a credit note or a reversal request at all: `sal.credit_notes` and `sal.receipt_reversals` are populated by raw `INSERT` under the `ins_*_gated` policies.
gaps.mitigation: P1-22 writes its own request-creation services doing raw scoped INSERTs, and calls `sal.approve_credit_note` / `sal.approve_receipt_reversal` for the decisions. The stale comment should be recorded as a documentation divergence; the migration itself must NOT be edited.

gaps.assumed: Every command in this lens has an in-lock idempotency short-circuit that "returns the original row before allocating a number or emitting an event" (`phase-1-11-invoice-issue-idempotency-contract.md` §M-fin-3, `phase-1-11-review-response.md` §M-fin-3), covering credit-note requests and reversals via `uq_credit_notes_idempotency` / `uq_receipt_reversals_idempotency`.
gaps.reality: Only `sal.issue_invoice` (by status: `IF v_inv.status = 'issued' THEN RETURN v_inv.invoice_number;` after `FOR UPDATE`) and `sal.record_receipt` short-circuit at all — and `record_receipt`'s pre-check is an UNLOCKED plain read: `IF p_idempotency_key IS NOT NULL THEN SELECT id INTO v_existing FROM sal.receipts WHERE tenant_id = v_tenant AND idempotency_key = p_idempotency_key; IF FOUND THEN RETURN v_existing; END IF;` with no `FOR UPDATE` and no lock on any row, so two concurrent replays both miss and one dies on `uq_receipts_idempotency` with 23505. For credit notes and reversals there is NO creation primitive whatsoever, so a replayed request is a raw INSERT that raises a bare `23505` to the caller. `sal.approve_credit_note` and `sal.approve_receipt_reversal` never read `idempotency_key`.
gaps.mitigation: P1-22 must layer the Phase 1-4 `shared.idempotency_keys` store over all five commands and must additionally handle `23505` on `uq_invoices_idempotency`, `uq_receipts_idempotency`, `uq_credit_notes_idempotency`, `uq_receipt_reversals_idempotency` as 'replay detected → return the stored response', never as a 500. The database-level constraint is the real defence; the prose short-circuit is not.

gaps.assumed: A caller reading an invoice's open balance either sees the true figure or is refused.
gaps.reality: `sal.invoice_open_receivable` is `STABLE SECURITY INVOKER`, granted to both `app_runtime` and `app_readonly`, and reads `sal.invoice_amounts`, `sal.payment_allocations` and `sal.credit_notes` — all three gated by `iam.has_permission('sal.finance.view')` in their SELECT policies. A caller WITHOUT `sal.finance.view` sees no rows, `v_gross` comes back NULL, `v_gross := COALESCE(v_gross, 0)`, and the function returns `round(0 - 0 - 0, 4)` = **0** with no error. `sal.partner_outstanding_balance` sums those zeros (invoices themselves are readable without the finance permission, since `sel_invoices_scope` has no permission predicate) and also returns 0.
gaps.mitigation: P1-22 must gate every balance-reading route on `sal.finance.view` in the application authorization layer BEFORE calling the function, and must never render a derived 0 as an authoritative 'nothing outstanding'. A permission-denied read must produce 403, not a plausible-looking zero.

gaps.assumed: There is a dedicated authority for approving a credit note, and one for requesting a receipt reversal, mirroring `sal.reversal.approve`.
gaps.reality: The catalog has `sal.credit.manage` ('Request and manage credit notes', high) and `sal.reversal.approve` ('Approve receipt reversals (dual control)', high) — and nothing else. There is NO `sal.credit.approve` and NO reversal-REQUEST code. At the database layer both tables gate INSERT and UPDATE on `sal.finance.view` alone (`ins_credit_notes_gated`, `upd_credit_notes_gated`, `ins_receipt_reversals_gated`, `upd_receipt_reversals_gated`), so the DB cannot distinguish maker from approver by permission at all — only `ck_*_approved_distinct` distinguishes them, and only by user identity.

REFUTED as a BLOCKER, not as a fact. Every piece of DDL the archaeologist quotes is verbatim correct — I re-read all of it — but the conclusion "this is a blocker" fails the stated test: no migration is required, is possible, or is even permitted, and the application-level handling they propose as "mitigation (a)" is already shipped, already the cross-phase pattern, and already mandated by the protected standard. One identifier in the claim is wrong.

WHAT VERIFIED EXACTLY AS CLAIMED

WHY IT IS NOT A BLOCKER
1. The missing object is DATA, not schema. The protected schema already supports the exact row required: `ck_number_sequences_branch_requires_company CHECK (branch_id IS NULL OR company_id IS NOT NULL)` explicitly PERMITS (company set, branch set); `uq_number_sequences_scope UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT (tenant_id, sequence_code, company_id, branch_id)`; `fk_number_sequences_company`/`fk_number_sequences_branch` (20260717106000) and index `ix_number_sequences_tenant_company_branch` all exist for precisely this scope. Nothing needs to be built.
2. A migration is not merely unnecessary, it is FORBIDDEN. docs/database/number-sequence-standard.md §4: sequence rows "are inserted by the administrative provisioning path … never by application runtime code and never hard-coded in a migration"; a tenant invoice sequence "is never schema, never a migration literal". Its risk register row 3: "Runtime roles must never gain INSERT/DELETE on `shared.number_sequences`." So neither of the two things a migration could do (insert the row, or grant runtime INSERT) is legal.

"Mitigation (a)" is already built and already in use. src/modules/shared-services/data/number-sequence-repository.ts defines `ALLOCATION_SQLSTATE.noSequenceInScope = 'P0002'`; src/modules/shared-services/application/number-allocation-service.ts maps it to `AppFailure('ERR-RES-001', 'No number sequence is provisioned for "<code>" in this scope')` with metric `METRICS.numberAllocationCount{result:'not-provisioned'}`, and exposes `isProvisioned(db, {sequenceCode, companyId, branchId})` documented as existing exactly because "`app_runtime` holds no INSERT on `shared.number_sequences`". `invoice` and `receipt` are already registered in domain/sequence-registry.ts (targets sal.invoices.invoice_number, sal.receipts.receipt_number).

The claim also overstates blast radius for invoices. `sal.invoices.invoice_number text NULL` and `ck_invoices_number_iff_issued CHECK ((invoice_number IS NULL AND issued_at IS NULL) = (status IN ('draft','void_before_issue')))` mean draft invoicing is entirely unaffected; only `sal.issue_invoice` fails. Receipts have no such relief — `sal.receipts.receipt_number text NOT NULL` — so `sal.record_receipt` is hard-blocked without the row. That distinction matters and the claim did not make it.

MITIGATION (b) IS MECHANICALLY POSSIBLE AND SHOULD STILL BE REJECTED. app_runtime does hold `GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON sal.invoices`, policy `upd_invoices_scope` permits the update, `sal.guard_invoice_freeze()` permits draft→issued, and `GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON sal.financial_events` + `ins_financial_events_gated` permit the event. Forking the issue path away from the single audited primitive is the wrong call; option (a) is the only defensible one.

FINDINGS I WOULD RAISE INSTEAD (narrower, and genuinely new)
A. DOC/DDL DIVERGENCE — DDL AUTHORITATIVE. docs/database/number-sequence-standard.md §4's own worked provisioning illustration inserts the `invoice` sequence at COMPANY scope: `INSERT INTO shared.number_sequences (tenant_id, company_id, sequence_code, prefix_template, pad_width, period_reset_rule, created_by) VALUES (:tenant_id, :company_id, 'invoice', 'INV-{period}-', 6, 'yearly', :provisioning_actor_id)` — branch_id absent, i.e. NULL. `sal.issue_invoice` always passes a NOT-NULL branch_id, and the predicate is `IS NOT DISTINCT FROM`, so an operator who follows the standard verbatim provisions a row the deployed function can never match and gets P0002 anyway. The standard, not the schema, is what needs correcting.
B. SCOPE MISMATCH INSIDE P1-11. `sal.invoice_numbering_configs` is keyed per (tenant, company) — `uq_invoice_numbering_configs_active ON (tenant_id, company_id) WHERE status='active' AND deleted_at IS NULL`, FK `fk_invoice_numbering_configs_company` to org.legal_companies, `mode` CHECK IN ('gapless','gapped'), `sequence_code` default `'invoice'`. So the numbering POLICY is company-scoped while the COUNTER it names is consumed at branch scope, and `uq_invoices_number ON (tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, invoice_number) WHERE invoice_number IS NOT NULL` permits the same rendered number in two branches of one company. Company-unique invoice numbering is ABSENT from the deployed schema — P1-22 must not invent it.
C. ASYMMETRIC WRITE SURFACE. P1-22 CAN create the config (`GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON sal.invoice_numbering_configs TO app_runtime`, policy `ins_invoice_numbering_configs_scope`) but CANNOT create the counter row it points at. A "configure invoice numbering" endpoint can therefore succeed and issue still fail — the preflight must check the counter, not the config.
D. CROSS-PHASE NOTE (out of P1-22 scope). Making `org.provision_organization` able to express company/branch sequence scope requires editing a P1-03 function = a new migration, which P1-22 must not write. Record it as a cross-phase item; do not act on it here.

NET RECOMMENDATION FOR THE ARCHAEOLOGY RECORD: downgrade from BLOCKER to a documented CONFIGURATION PRECONDITION plus a required error-mapping obligation. P1-22 must (i) call `numbers.isProvisioned` at branch scope before expensive work, (ii) map SQLSTATE P0002 raised out of `sal.issue_invoice`/`sal.record_receipt` to `ERR-RES-001` naming the sequence code and the (company, branch) scope, and (iii) ship the branch-scoped `invoice`/`receipt` rows as a test fixture on the admin connection exactly as tests/backend/p1-20-helpers.ts does, plus an operator runbook step. No migration.

gaps.assumed: An issued invoice and a recorded receipt cannot be removed from the books.
gaps.reality: Both carry `deleted_at`/`deleted_by` and NOTHING guards them. `sal.guard_invoice_freeze`'s post-draft branch checks only `invoice_number`, `issued_at`, `work_order_id`, `quotation_revision_id`, `currency_code` and the status edge; `tg_invoices_immutable` covers only `('tenant_id','company_id','branch_id','created_at','created_by')`. `sal.guard_receipt_freeze` likewise never mentions `deleted_at`. So `UPDATE sal.invoices SET deleted_at = now()` on an ISSUED invoice succeeds. The consequences are silent and asymmetric: `uq_invoices_work_order_active` is `WHERE status <> 'void_before_issue' AND deleted_at IS NULL`, so soft-deleting an issued invoice frees the work order for a SECOND invoice; `sal.partner_outstanding_balance` filters `AND deleted_at IS NULL` and drops it, while `sal.invoice_open_receivable` does NOT filter `deleted_at` and still reports it as open — the two derivations disagree. For receipts, `sal.invoice_open_receivable` joins `sal.receipts r ... WHERE r.status <> 'reversed'` with no `deleted_at` predicate, so soft-deleting a receipt does NOT restore the invoice's receivable while removing the receipt from any deleted_at-aware listing.
gaps.mitigation: P1-22 must forbid soft-delete of any invoice that has left `draft` and of any receipt, at the repository layer, and must never write `deleted_at` on `sal.invoices`/`sal.receipts` from any route. Note that the amount tables are genuinely safe — `sal.guard_invoice_amount_frozen` and `sal.guard_invoice_line_amount_frozen` reject EVERY update (including a soft-delete) once the parent is non-draft — so the hole is only on the two parent tables. There is no DB backstop; record it as an application-only invariant.

verdict.reasoning:
VERDICT: refuted=true — every DDL fact in the report is ACCURATE (I confirmed all of them), but the BLOCKER classification and the "no DB backstop, must be forced" framing do not hold. No migration is required; the invariant is an application-level OMISSION that is clearly sufficient, and I found a partial accidental DB backstop the report missed. Two of its supporting claims also need correction.

=== WHAT I CONFIRMED (the DDL facts are right) ===

1. `sal.invoices` (supabase/migrations/20260724091000_sal_invoices.sql:50-51) carries `deleted_at timestamptz NULL, deleted_by uuid NULL`. `sal.receipts` (20260724092000_sal_payments.sql) likewise.

2. `sal.guard_invoice_freeze()` (091000:97-131) post-draft branch checks exactly `NEW.invoice_number`, `NEW.issued_at`, `NEW.work_order_id`, `NEW.quotation_revision_id`, `NEW.currency_code` and the status edge (`issued`->`credited` only; `credited`/`void_before_issue` terminal). `deleted_at` is never mentioned.

3. `tg_invoices_immutable` (091000:135-136) = `org.guard_immutable_columns('tenant_id','company_id','branch_id','created_at','created_by')`. `org.guard_immutable_columns()` (20260717101000_org_tenants.sql:57-73) iterates `TG_ARGV` only, so unlisted columns are free.

4. `sal.guard_receipt_freeze()` (092000) checks `amount`, `currency_code`, `payment_method_id`, `payer_partner_id`, `received_at`, `receipt_number` and the reversal edge. No `deleted_at`. `tg_receipts_immutable` = same five-column list.

5. `uq_invoices_work_order_active` (091000:73-74) is `ON sal.invoices (tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, work_order_id) WHERE status <> 'void_before_issue' AND deleted_at IS NULL` — soft-deleting an issued invoice DOES free the work-order slot, and `sal.issue_invoice` has no "another invoice exists for this WO" check, so a second invoice can be created and issued.

6. The two derivations DO disagree, exactly as claimed. `sal.partner_outstanding_balance` (093000) loops `WHERE tenant_id = iam.current_tenant_id() AND payer_partner_id = p_partner_id AND status = 'issued' AND deleted_at IS NULL` — drops it. `sal.invoice_open_receivable` selects `FROM sal.invoices i LEFT JOIN sal.invoice_amounts a ON ... AND a.deleted_at IS NULL WHERE i.id = p_invoice_id` — filters the AMOUNTS row's deleted_at but NOT the invoice's, so it still returns the open receivable.

7. Receipts: `sal.invoice_open_receivable` joins `sal.payment_allocations pa JOIN sal.receipts r ... WHERE ... AND r.status <> 'reversed'` — no deleted_at predicate; `sal.receipt_unallocated` likewise has none. Soft-deleting a receipt does not restore the receivable.

8. The amount tables really are safe. `sal.guard_invoice_amount_frozen()` (091000:200-213) and `sal.guard_invoice_line_amount_frozen()` (091000:366-388) are `BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE` and raise on ANY write once the parent is non-draft, irrespective of which column moved. `sal.guard_invoice_line_frozen()` protects `sal.invoice_lines` the same way. So the hole is confined to the two parent tables — correct.

9. NO DB GUARD EXISTS. Exhaustive object list on the two tables across all 119 migrations: invoices — `tg_invoices_freeze`, `tg_invoices_touch_metadata`, `tg_invoices_immutable`, `tg_invoices_event_completeness`; receipts — `tg_receipts_freeze`, `tg_receipts_touch_metadata`, `tg_receipts_immutable`, `tg_receipts_event_completeness`. Policies `upd_invoices_scope` / `upd_receipts_gated` gate scope and `sal.finance.view` only. Grants are TABLE-LEVEL all-column: `GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON sal.invoices TO app_runtime` (091000:155) and the same for `sal.receipts` (092000:177). No CHECK, no view, no generated column, no seed, no later migration.

=== CORRECTION 1 — an accidental partial backstop the report missed ===
`tg_invoices_event_completeness` (093000:382-383) is `AFTER UPDATE ON sal.invoices DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED FOR EACH ROW WHEN (NEW.status = 'issued')`. It fires on a soft-delete UPDATE too, and `sal.guard_event_completeness()` is SECURITY INVOKER doing `SELECT 1 FROM sal.financial_events fe WHERE ...` — a table with FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY whose `sel_financial_events_gated` policy requires `iam.has_permission('sal.finance.view')`. A session WITHOUT `sal.finance.view` therefore sees zero rows and gets `sal.invoices: financial command produced no invoice_issued event (completeness)` (check_violation) at COMMIT. So `UPDATE sal.invoices SET deleted_at = now()` on an ISSUED invoice succeeds only for an actor holding `sal.finance.view`. Conversely the WHEN clause is false for a `credited` invoice, so a credited invoice is entirely unguarded, and `tg_receipts_event_completeness` is `AFTER INSERT` only, so receipts are entirely unguarded. This narrows the hole; it does not close it, and it is accidental, not a control.

=== CORRECTION 2 — `uq_receipts_number` is not partial ===
`CONSTRAINT uq_receipts_number UNIQUE (tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, receipt_number)` is a full table constraint, NOT a partial index on `deleted_at IS NULL`. Soft-deleting a receipt does NOT free its number for reuse — a mitigating fact the report omits while asserting the asymmetry is one-directionally bad.

=== WHY refuted=true ===
(a) There is NO authorized delete operation to guard. `supabase/seeds/04_iam_permission_catalog.sql` lines 60-70 define the entire sal vocabulary: `sal.invoice.manage`, `sal.invoice.issue`, `sal.payment.record`, `sal.payment.allocate`, `sal.credit.manage`, `sal.reversal.approve`, `sal.finance.view`, `sal.delivery.manage`, `sal.delivery.complete`, `sal.delivery.view`. `sal.invoice.delete` and any receipt-delete permission are ABSENT. No P1-22 route can be built for an operation with no permission code.
(b) The schema already supplies the intended removal semantics, so no route needs `deleted_at`: pre-issue removal is `status='void_before_issue'` (`ck_invoices_status`), post-issue reduction is `sal.credit_notes` + `sal.approve_credit_note`, and receipt correction is `sal.receipt_reversals` + `sal.approve_receipt_reversal` ("corrections via reversal only", per `sal.guard_receipt_freeze`'s own error text).
(c) The required discipline is an omission, not a control: never name `deleted_at`/`deleted_by` in an UPDATE column list against `sal.invoices` or `sal.receipts`. That is enforceable in the repository layer with explicit column lists, provable by a repository-level test, and needs no schema change. The double-billing consequence additionally requires the app to insert a second invoice on the same work order — which it never will if it never soft-deletes the first.
(d) A migration is not merely unnecessary, it is forbidden: P1-22 is backend-only, 119 migrations, no 120. And the platform-consistent DB remedy is well established and available to a FUTURE DBCR, not to this phase: `20260726090000_iam_org_runtime_administration_capabilities.sql:117,144` and `20260728090000_shared_services_runtime_write_capabilities.sql:124,133,153` grant column-scoped `GRANT UPDATE (col, ...)`. Replacing the table-level `GRANT ... UPDATE ON sal.invoices` with a column list omitting `deleted_at` would close this at the grant layer in one line — evidence that the fix is a routine future capability migration, not a blocker for the backend phase.

=== WHAT SHOULD STILL BE RECORDED ===
The finding is genuine and worth carrying, at the right severity.
