reports.summary: The protected `wty` schema (migration `supabase/migrations/20260724095000_wty_warranty.sql`, 361 lines, the only migration that ever touches `wty`) contains exactly five tables — `wty.warranty_policies`, `wty.warranty_coverage`, `wty.warranty_records`, `wty.warranty_record_items`, `wty.warranty_status_history` — three functions (`wty.issue_warranty`, `wty.guard_warranty_record_freeze`, `wty.guard_warranty_record_coherence`), eleven triggers and fourteen RLS policies. Warranty terms ARE configured in the database, but only as tenant/company data: `wty.warranty_coverage.duration_months integer NOT NULL` has **no DEFAULT**, `odometer_limit integer NULL` has no default, and there is **no warranty seed anywhere** in `supabase/seeds/` — `tests/db/no-fake-data.test.ts` line 52 actively asserts every `wty` table is empty. There is therefore **no configured policy source and no default duration whatsoever**: a tenant must create a policy and an effective-dated coverage row before any warranty can be issued, and P1-22 must never supply a fallback number. The link back to the delivered work is `wty.warranty_records.delivery_record_id` → `sal.delivery_records`, hardened by `tg_warranty_records_coherence` (delivery must be `'delivered'` and its `vehicle_id`/`work_order_id` must match), but the link back to a work-order *line* is `wty.warranty_record_items.source_job_id` / `source_part_id`, which carry **no foreign key, no NOT NULL, and no coupling to `item_kind`** — they are opaque uuids the database never validates. Duplicate prevention rests on two structures only: `ex_warranty_records_no_overlap` (gist EXCLUDE over `tenant_id, vehicle_id, coverage_id, daterange(start_date, expiry_date, '[]')` while `status IN ('issued','active')`) and the partial `uq_warranty_records_idempotency (tenant_id, idempotency_key) WHERE idempotency_key IS NOT NULL`; nothing forbids two warranties against the same delivery under different policies. The single largest gap is that **no warranty claim table exists** even though P1-11's own prose says claim structures "activate with the P1-22 backend" — only the `claimed_against` status literal was prepared, and P1-22 may not create migration 120.

findings.fact: The `wty` schema is exactly five tables, three functions and eleven triggers, all created by one migration. No later migration (including 20260725…–20260730… IAM/shared capability migrations) references `wty` at all.
findings.identifier: supabase/migrations/20260724095000_wty_warranty.sql — wty.warranty_policies, wty.warranty_coverage, wty.warranty_records, wty.warranty_record_items, wty.warranty_status_history; wty.issue_warranty, wty.guard_warranty_record_freeze, wty.guard_warranty_record_coherence
findings.evidence: `CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS wty; -- Warranty module (P1-11): policies, effective-dated coverage, records.` and `COMMENT ON SCHEMA wty IS 'Warranty module (Phase 1-11, Figure 4.25). Owns warranty policies, effective-dated coverage … Full warranty claim adjudication is deferred to Phase 1-22 (P1-OD-024).'` (20260724090000_salwtyrpt_schemas.sql lines 59, 64-65). `grep -rn "wty\." --include=*.sql supabase/` outside the warranty migration returns only the two permission-catalog seed lines.
findings.consequence: P1-22's warranty surface is bounded by these five tables. Any endpoint whose persistence is not one of these five tables is inventing storage and must not be written.

findings.fact: Warranty durations ARE configured in the database — as effective-dated tenant/company data on wty.warranty_coverage — but with NO DEFAULT on any term column. duration_months is NOT NULL with no default; odometer_limit is nullable with no default.
findings.identifier: wty.warranty_coverage.duration_months integer NOT NULL; wty.warranty_coverage.odometer_limit integer NULL; ck_warranty_coverage_duration; ck_warranty_coverage_odometer
findings.evidence: `duration_months integer NOT NULL,` / `odometer_limit integer NULL,` … `CONSTRAINT ck_warranty_coverage_duration CHECK (duration_months > 0),` `CONSTRAINT ck_warranty_coverage_odometer CHECK (odometer_limit IS NULL OR odometer_limit > 0),`
findings.consequence: Every duration is caller-supplied tenant configuration. The backend must reject a coverage-create request that omits duration_months (400) and must NEVER substitute 12, 24, or any other number. No 'default warranty period' exists to fall back on.

findings.fact: There is NO warranty seed data of any kind. The no-fake-data guard actively asserts the wty tables are empty, and P1-11 states policies are 'Structural only (no business-content seeds)'.
findings.evidence: `COMMENT ON TABLE wty.warranty_policies IS 'Phase 1-11 warranty policy (tenant/company-scoped). Terms live in effective-dated wty.warranty_coverage. Structural only (no business-content seeds).'` and tests/db/no-fake-data.test.ts:52 `AND table_schema IN ('org', 'iam', 'shared', 'crm', 'veh', 'apt', 'rec', 'wo', 'dia', 'tech', 'qms', 'svc', 'quo', 'inv', 'sal', 'wty', 'rpt')`
findings.consequence: A fresh tenant has zero policies and zero coverages. `wty.issue_warranty` will raise `no coverage effective at % for policy %` until a human configures one. The backend's warranty-issue endpoint must surface that as a business error, not seed a policy, and P1-22 must not add warranty rows to any seed file.

findings.fact: Coverage is effective-dated with a half-open gist EXCLUDE per policy+scope; warranty records use a CLOSED range for their own EXCLUDE. The two boundary conventions differ.
findings.evidence: coverage: `CONSTRAINT ex_warranty_coverage_no_overlap EXCLUDE USING gist (tenant_id WITH =, company_id WITH =, policy_id WITH =, covered_scope WITH =, daterange(effective_from, effective_to, '[)') WITH &&) WHERE (status = 'active' AND deleted_at IS NULL)`; records: `CONSTRAINT ex_warranty_records_no_overlap EXCLUDE USING gist (tenant_id WITH =, vehicle_id WITH =, coverage_id WITH =, daterange(start_date, expiry_date, '[]') WITH &&) WHERE (status IN ('issued', 'active') AND deleted_at IS NULL)`
findings.consequence: Back-to-back coverage rows may share a boundary date (`effective_to` = next `effective_from`) and succeed. Back-to-back warranty RENEWALS may NOT: a new record whose start_date equals the prior record's expiry_date raises 23P01 `exclusion_violation`. The backend must start a renewal at expiry_date + 1 day, or void/expire the prior record first.

findings.fact: The warranty record's exact date/duration/odometer columns and their types are fixed: two `date` columns and two `integer` odometer columns. There is no timestamp, no timezone, and no unit column.
findings.identifier: wty.warranty_records.start_date date NOT NULL; expiry_date date NOT NULL; odometer_at_issue integer NOT NULL; odometer_limit integer NULL; ck_warranty_records_dates; ck_warranty_records_odometer
findings.evidence: `start_date date NOT NULL,` `expiry_date date NOT NULL,` `odometer_at_issue integer NOT NULL,` `odometer_limit integer NULL,` … `CONSTRAINT ck_warranty_records_dates CHECK (expiry_date > start_date),` `CONSTRAINT ck_warranty_records_odometer CHECK (odometer_at_issue >= 0 AND (odometer_limit IS NULL OR odometer_limit >= odometer_at_issue))`
findings.consequence: The API carries warranty dates as `date` strings (YYYY-MM-DD), never as instants, and odometer values as plain integers with no unit field. Expiry is a calendar date; there is no time-of-day expiry semantics to model.

findings.fact: The warranty status vocabulary is exactly five values, duplicated on the record and on the history ledger. There is NO transition graph table, no allowed-transition CHECK, and no trigger requiring a history row when the status changes.
findings.identifier: ck_warranty_records_status; ck_warranty_status_history_to_status; wty.warranty_records.status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'issued'
findings.evidence: `CONSTRAINT ck_warranty_records_status CHECK (status IN ('issued', 'active', 'expired', 'voided', 'claimed_against')),` and `CONSTRAINT ck_warranty_status_history_to_status CHECK (to_status IN ('issued', 'active', 'expired', 'voided', 'claimed_against'))`. Contrast `wo.work_order_states` / `wo.work_order_transitions` (20260722091000_wo_state_catalogs.sql), which are data-driven graphs — `wty` has no equivalent.
findings.consequence: Transcribe exactly these five literals; invent no sixth. The legal transition graph and the obligation to append a `wty.warranty_status_history` row on every change are 100% backend responsibilities — the database will happily accept `voided → issued` with no ledger row.

findings.fact: `from_status` on the status ledger is UNCHECKED and unbound: it has no CHECK constraint and nothing verifies it equals the record's current status. Only `to_status` is constrained. `actor_id` and `occurred_at` are server-stamped and cannot be forged.
findings.identifier: wty.warranty_status_history.from_status text NULL; tg_warranty_status_history_stamp → shared.stamp_status_history(); wty.warranty_status_history.seq bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY
findings.evidence: `from_status text NULL,` (no CHECK) vs `CONSTRAINT ck_warranty_status_history_to_status CHECK (to_status IN (…))`; `CREATE TRIGGER tg_warranty_status_history_stamp BEFORE INSERT ON wty.warranty_status_history FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION shared.stamp_status_history();` whose body is `NEW.actor_id := iam.current_user_id(); IF NEW.actor_id IS NULL THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'status history requires an actor in the session context' USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation'; END IF; NEW.occurred_at := now();`
findings.consequence: The backend must set from_status from the row it just read under lock and must never accept actor_id or occurred_at from the client (they are overwritten). A missing session actor surfaces as 23514, not 401.

findings.fact: The issued warranty record is frozen in its identity and terms, but status, idempotency_key, record_version and the soft-delete columns are deliberately NOT frozen.
findings.evidence: `IF NEW.vehicle_id <> OLD.vehicle_id OR NEW.work_order_id <> OLD.work_order_id OR NEW.delivery_record_id <> OLD.delivery_record_id OR NEW.policy_id <> OLD.policy_id OR NEW.coverage_id <> OLD.coverage_id OR NEW.start_date <> OLD.start_date OR NEW.expiry_date <> OLD.expiry_date OR NEW.odometer_at_issue <> OLD.odometer_at_issue OR NEW.odometer_limit IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.odometer_limit THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'wty.warranty_records: an issued warranty record''s terms are frozen (corrections via a linked record)' USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation';`
findings.consequence: Only a status advance (and a soft delete) is a legal UPDATE. Any 'edit warranty' endpoint is impossible: corrections are a new record. Note the guard uses `<>` (not `IS DISTINCT FROM`) on the NOT NULL columns, which is safe because they are NOT NULL, and `IS DISTINCT FROM` on the nullable odometer_limit.

findings.fact: The structural link from the warranty back to the delivered work is the delivery record, and it is enforced on INSERT only — not on UPDATE.
findings.identifier: wty.guard_warranty_record_coherence() / tg_warranty_records_coherence BEFORE INSERT; fk_warranty_records_delivery → sal.delivery_records (tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, id)
findings.evidence: `IF v_del.status <> 'delivered' THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'wty.warranty_records: delivery % is % (a warranty may only be issued against a delivered vehicle)' … USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation'; END IF; IF v_del.vehicle_id <> NEW.vehicle_id OR v_del.work_order_id <> NEW.work_order_id THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'wty.warranty_records: vehicle/work order must match delivery %'` and `CREATE TRIGGER tg_warranty_records_coherence BEFORE INSERT ON wty.warranty_records`
findings.consequence: A raw INSERT path is safe against a non-delivered or mismatched delivery. The freeze guard covers UPDATE, so the INSERT-only scope is not a hole — but the backend must still pass company_id and branch_id that match the delivery, because the guard looks the delivery up by the record's own (tenant, company, branch, delivery_record_id) and raises 23503 `foreign_key_violation` with 'delivery % not found in scope' if they do not.

findings.fact: `wty.issue_warranty` is the only granted warranty primitive. It derives expiry_date and odometer_limit by an exact formula the backend must not re-derive differently.
findings.identifier: wty.issue_warranty(p_delivery_id uuid, p_policy_id uuid, p_correlation_id uuid DEFAULT NULL, p_idempotency_key text DEFAULT NULL) RETURNS uuid, LANGUAGE plpgsql VOLATILE SECURITY INVOKER SET search_path = ''
findings.evidence: `VALUES (v_tenant, v_del.company_id, v_del.branch_id, v_del.vehicle_id, v_del.work_order_id, v_del.id, p_policy_id, v_cov.id, v_start, (v_start + (v_cov.duration_months || ' months')::interval)::date, v_odo, CASE WHEN v_cov.odometer_limit IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE v_odo + v_cov.odometer_limit END, 'issued', p_idempotency_key, v_actor)` and `GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION wty.issue_warranty(uuid, uuid, uuid, text) TO app_runtime;`
findings.consequence: expiry_date = (delivered_at::date + N months)::date with PostgreSQL month-end clamping (2026-01-31 + 1 month = 2026-02-28). odometer_limit on the RECORD is an ABSOLUTE ceiling (odometer_at_issue + coverage.odometer_limit), whereas odometer_limit on the COVERAGE is a RELATIVE allowance. Same column name, different meaning — do not conflate them in the API.

findings.fact: `wty.issue_warranty` selects the effective coverage WITHOUT filtering covered_scope, and the caller cannot pass one. A policy carrying more than one scope at the same date yields a non-deterministic pick.
findings.identifier: wty.issue_warranty coverage lookup; wty.warranty_coverage.covered_scope; ck_warranty_coverage_scope CHECK (covered_scope IN ('all','service','part'))
findings.evidence: `SELECT * INTO v_cov FROM wty.warranty_coverage WHERE tenant_id = v_tenant AND company_id = v_del.company_id AND policy_id = p_policy_id AND status = 'active' AND deleted_at IS NULL AND effective_from <= v_start AND (effective_to IS NULL OR effective_to > v_start) ORDER BY effective_from DESC LIMIT 1;` — note `covered_scope` is absent from the predicate, while `ex_warranty_coverage_no_overlap` keys on `covered_scope`, so 'all', 'service' and 'part' coverages of one policy MAY legally coexist on the same date.
findings.consequence: P1-22 must either (a) constrain a policy to a single active covered_scope per date at the application layer before issuing, or (b) reject issue when more than one coverage is effective, or (c) insert the record directly (raw INSERT is granted) after selecting the coverage explicitly — in which case it must replicate the M-wty-2 value binding itself, because that binding is NOT enforced by any constraint (accepted residual M-wty-2b / WVR-P1-12-001).

findings.fact: `wty.issue_warranty` reads the raw odometer `value` and casts it to integer, discarding both the unit and the tenth-of-a-unit precision. It does NOT use the canonical `value_km` generated column.
findings.identifier: veh.odometer_readings.value numeric(12,1); veh.odometer_readings.unit text CHECK (unit IN ('km','mi')); veh.odometer_readings.value_km numeric(14,4) GENERATED ALWAYS AS … STORED; sal.complete_delivery(p_delivery_id uuid, p_final_odometer_value numeric, p_odometer_unit text DEFAULT 'km', p_correlation_id uuid)
findings.evidence: `SELECT o.value::integer, v_del.delivered_at::date INTO v_odo, v_start FROM veh.odometer_readings o WHERE o.tenant_id = v_del.tenant_id AND o.vehicle_id = v_del.vehicle_id AND o.id = v_del.final_odometer_reading_id;` versus `COMMENT ON COLUMN veh.odometer_readings.value_km IS 'Generated (STORED) canonical kilometres from (value, unit) … Sole basis for monotonicity and point-in-time resolution'`.
findings.consequence: If a delivery is completed with p_odometer_unit = 'mi', wty.warranty_records.odometer_at_issue is stored in MILES while the coverage's odometer_limit allowance is unitless — the ceiling silently becomes miles. The backend must record and surface the unit from veh.odometer_readings alongside every warranty read, and should treat mixed-unit tenants as a documented limitation. It must also expect `value::integer` to ROUND (45000.5 → 45001), so the API's odometer_at_issue will not always equal the delivery's recorded reading.

findings.fact: Duplicate warranties are prevented only by the vehicle+coverage overlap EXCLUDE and by an OPTIONAL idempotency key. There is no unique constraint on delivery_record_id or on (delivery, policy).
findings.identifier: ex_warranty_records_no_overlap; uq_warranty_records_idempotency ON wty.warranty_records (tenant_id, idempotency_key) WHERE idempotency_key IS NOT NULL
findings.evidence: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_warranty_records_idempotency ON wty.warranty_records (tenant_id, idempotency_key) WHERE idempotency_key IS NOT NULL;` and `CREATE INDEX ix_warranty_records_delivery ON wty.warranty_records (tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, delivery_record_id);` — an ordinary index, NOT unique.
findings.consequence: Two warranties against the same delivery under two different policies (hence different coverage_id) are legal by design. Two calls without an idempotency key for the same delivery+policy collide only via 23P01 on the identical daterange — and NOT at all if the first record was voided or expired. P1-22 must always pass an idempotency key on the issue path and must layer the Phase 1-4 idempotency store on top.

findings.fact: `wty.issue_warranty`'s idempotency short-circuit is an unlocked read subject to RLS and does not fingerprint the request.
findings.evidence: `IF p_idempotency_key IS NOT NULL THEN SELECT id INTO v_existing FROM wty.warranty_records WHERE tenant_id = v_tenant AND idempotency_key = p_idempotency_key; IF FOUND THEN RETURN v_existing; END IF; END IF;`
findings.consequence: Three consequences: (1) the SELECT runs under the caller's RLS, so a key consumed in a branch the caller cannot see is invisible and the INSERT then fails with 23505 unique_violation rather than returning the prior id; (2) two concurrent calls with the same key race to 23505 (no advisory lock, no ON CONFLICT); (3) the same key reused with a DIFFERENT delivery silently returns the first record. The backend must own request-fingerprint validation and map 23505 on this path to the idempotent-replay response.

findings.fact: The covered-item child table has NO referential integrity on its source links and no uniqueness. `source_job_id` and `source_part_id` are opaque uuids with no FK, no NOT NULL, and no coupling to `item_kind`.
findings.identifier: wty.warranty_record_items.source_job_id uuid NULL; wty.warranty_record_items.source_part_id uuid NULL; ck_warranty_record_items_kind CHECK (item_kind IN ('service','part'))
findings.evidence: The full constraint list is `CONSTRAINT pk_warranty_record_items PRIMARY KEY (id), CONSTRAINT fk_warranty_record_items_tenant …, CONSTRAINT fk_warranty_record_items_record …, CONSTRAINT ck_warranty_record_items_kind CHECK (item_kind IN ('service', 'part'))` — there is no fk to wo.jobs, no fk to inv.part_issues, no fk to wo.required_parts, no check that (item_kind='service') = (source_job_id IS NOT NULL), and no unique index on (warranty_record_id, source_job_id) or (warranty_record_id, source_part_id). The P1-11 data dictionary itself calls them 'Opaque source work-job link (FR-WTY-002, nullable)'.
findings.consequence: The database will accept a covered item with both source ids NULL, with both set, with item_kind='part' pointing at a job, with ids from a different tenant, or with the same job listed five times. Every one of those checks is the backend's: it must resolve source_job_id against wo.jobs and source_part_id against the part tables in the SAME work order as the record's work_order_id, enforce the kind↔link pairing, and de-duplicate.

findings.fact: Grants to app_runtime are SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE on the four mutable wty tables and SELECT/INSERT on the ledger. There is NO DELETE grant and no DELETE policy anywhere in wty. app_readonly is SELECT-only on all five.
findings.identifier: GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON wty.warranty_policies|warranty_coverage|warranty_records|warranty_record_items TO app_runtime; GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON wty.warranty_status_history TO app_runtime; GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION wty.issue_warranty(uuid, uuid, uuid, text) TO app_runtime
findings.evidence: `GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON wty.warranty_status_history TO app_runtime;` `GRANT SELECT ON wty.warranty_status_history TO app_readonly;` and `REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION wty.guard_warranty_record_freeze() FROM PUBLIC;` / `REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION wty.guard_warranty_record_coherence() FROM PUBLIC;`
findings.consequence: Write feasibility is proven for policies, coverage, records, items and history WITHOUT a new migration. Deletion is impossible — removal is soft-delete via UPDATE of deleted_at/deleted_by (and the status ledger has no deleted_at at all, so a history row is permanent). The two guard functions are not callable by app_runtime, which is correct.

findings.fact: All 14 wty RLS policies gate on tenant + allowed_company_ids / allowed_branch_ids ONLY. No wty policy references any permission code — unlike inv's cost tables or sal's finance detail.
findings.evidence: `CREATE POLICY sel_warranty_records_scope ON wty.warranty_records FOR SELECT TO app_runtime, app_readonly USING (tenant_id = iam.current_tenant_id() AND (iam.allowed_company_ids() IS NULL OR company_id = ANY (iam.allowed_company_ids())) AND (iam.allowed_branch_ids() IS NULL OR branch_id = ANY (iam.allowed_branch_ids())));` — the P1-11 RLS matrix confirms the gate column is '—' for all five wty tables.
findings.consequence: Permission enforcement for warranty is 100% application-level. Per P1-18-A-01 the allowed_* arrays are the union of every active grant regardless of which permission it carries, so RLS is defence-in-depth only. Every branch-scoped warranty operation must pass a concrete authorizationTarget so evaluation uses iam.has_permission_in_scope; per the P1-21 H6 lesson, a branch-scoped warranty READ needs BOTH company_id AND branch_id as SQL predicates because iam.has_permission_in_scope matches company OR branch.

findings.fact: Warranty policies and coverage are COMPANY-scoped; warranty records, items and history are BRANCH-scoped. The record's FKs to policy and coverage are company-level composites.
findings.identifier: fk_warranty_records_policy FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, company_id, policy_id); fk_warranty_records_coverage FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, company_id, coverage_id); fk_warranty_records_branch FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, company_id, branch_id)
findings.evidence: `CONSTRAINT fk_warranty_records_coverage FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, company_id, coverage_id) REFERENCES wty.warranty_coverage (tenant_id, company_id, id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,` and wty.warranty_policies / wty.warranty_coverage have no branch_id column at all.
findings.consequence: Policy/coverage management endpoints take a companyId authorization target with NO branchId; issue/read endpoints take companyId + branchId. A policy configured in company A1 applies to every branch of A1 and to none of company A2.

findings.fact: Exactly two warranty permission codes exist in the catalog. There is no read, void, expire, or claim permission code for warranty anywhere.
findings.identifier: wty.policy.manage (module wty, risk medium); wty.warranty.issue (module wty, risk medium) — supabase/seeds/04_iam_permission_catalog.sql lines 72-73
findings.evidence: `('wty.policy.manage',        'wty', 'Manage warranty policies and coverage',      'medium', '00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001'),` and `('wty.warranty.issue',       'wty', 'Issue warranty records',                     'medium', '00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001'),`
findings.consequence: Reuse these two before minting anything. `wty.policy.manage` by its own text already covers BOTH policies and coverage — do not split it. Note the catalog currently holds 100 rows and `.github/ci-baselines/schema-baseline.json` pins `permissionCount: 100`, checked by scripts/ci/migration-replay-checks.mjs:238 — adding any new code requires updating that baseline in the same change or CI fails.

findings.fact: The warranty payer split on an invoice is a money column with a balance CHECK, and it is completely disconnected from wty.warranty_records — no FK, no warranty_record_id column anywhere on the invoice side.
findings.identifier: sal.invoice_line_amounts.warranty_pay_amount numeric(18,4) NOT NULL; ck_invoice_line_amounts_payer_split; sal.invoice_lines.source_service_line_id / source_part_issue_id / source_quotation_item_id
findings.evidence: `CONSTRAINT ck_invoice_line_amounts_payer_split CHECK (customer_pay_amount + warranty_pay_amount = gross_amount),` and the full sal.invoice_lines column list contains `source_service_line_id uuid NULL, source_part_issue_id uuid NULL, source_quotation_item_id uuid NULL` — there is no warranty_record_id on sal.invoice_lines or sal.invoice_line_amounts.
findings.consequence: P1-22 may mark a line as warranty-borne, but the database will never check that a warranty record exists, is live, covers that job/part, or has not exhausted its odometer/date limit. If the backend wants a warranty-covered line to be provably backed by a warranty, that check is application-level and unenforceable at rest. Money stays a numeric(18,4) exact-decimal string end to end.

findings.fact: `warranty_split_recorded` is one of six financial event types, is emitted only by sal.issue_invoice when the sum is positive, is provenance-bound to the issued invoice, is single-use per invoice — and is NOT covered by the completeness constraint triggers.
findings.identifier: ck_financial_events_event_type CHECK (event_type IN ('invoice_issued','receipt_recorded','payment_allocated','credit_note_issued','receipt_reversed','warranty_split_recorded')); uq_financial_events_source UNIQUE (tenant_id, source_type, source_id, event_type); sal.guard_financial_event_provenance(); sal.guard_event_completeness()
findings.evidence: emission: `IF v_wty > 0 THEN INSERT INTO sal.financial_events (…) VALUES (…, 'warranty_split_recorded', 'invoice', v_inv.id, v_inv.currency_code, round(v_wty, 4), …); END IF;`; provenance: `ELSIF NEW.event_type = 'warranty_split_recorded' THEN SELECT COALESCE(sum(la.warranty_pay_amount), 0), i.currency_code INTO v_amount, v_currency … WHERE i.status = 'issued' AND la.deleted_at IS NULL GROUP BY i.currency_code;`; completeness: `IF TG_TABLE_NAME = 'invoices' THEN v_needed := (NEW.status = 'issued'); v_type := 'invoice_issued';` — 'warranty_split_recorded' never appears in sal.guard_event_completeness.
findings.consequence: The event type literal is `warranty_split_recorded` (source_type `invoice`) — transcribe it exactly. Because only invoice_issued is completeness-enforced, an invoice issued by any path other than sal.issue_invoice could carry warranty_pay > 0 with no split event. P1-22's invoice-issue path must go through sal.issue_invoice.

findings.fact: Error-code mapping is coarse: three distinct business failures inside wty.issue_warranty all raise the same SQLSTATE, distinguishable only by message text.
findings.identifier: SQLSTATE 23514 check_violation (issue_warranty x3, freeze guard, coherence status/vehicle mismatch); 23503 foreign_key_violation (coherence 'delivery % not found in scope'); 23P01 exclusion_violation (both EXCLUDEs); 23505 unique_violation (uq_warranty_records_idempotency)
findings.evidence: `RAISE EXCEPTION 'wty.issue_warranty: delivery % not found or not delivered', p_delivery_id USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation';` / `RAISE EXCEPTION 'wty.issue_warranty: delivery has no final odometer reading' USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation';` / `RAISE EXCEPTION 'wty.issue_warranty: no coverage effective at % for policy %', v_start, p_policy_id USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation';`
findings.consequence: The backend must pre-validate each precondition itself (delivery exists and is 'delivered'; delivery has final_odometer_reading_id; a coverage is effective at delivered_at::date) so it can return distinct, actionable business errors, and treat a 23514 escaping from the function as a last-resort generic conflict.

findings.fact: There is no warranty number, certificate number, or numbering scheme. The record's only identifier is its uuid primary key.
findings.identifier: wty.warranty_records — full column list; shared.number_sequences / shared.next_display_number (used by sal.issue_invoice with sequence_code 'invoice')
findings.evidence: The wty.warranty_records column list is `id, tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, vehicle_id, work_order_id, delivery_record_id, policy_id, coverage_id, start_date, expiry_date, odometer_at_issue, odometer_limit, status, idempotency_key, record_version, created_at, created_by, updated_at, updated_by, deleted_at, deleted_by` — no *_number column. `grep -rn warranty supabase/seeds/05_shared_reference.sql` returns nothing, i.e. no warranty sequence code is registered.
findings.consequence: ABSENT: do not invent a warranty numbering scheme, prefix, or sequence code. The API exposes the uuid. `wty.warranty_policies.policy_code` (`CHECK (policy_code ~ '^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,62}$')`) is the only warranty-side code format the schema defines.

gaps.assumed: A warranty naturally moves issued → active and expires on its own; the phase plan is likely to assume an expiry sweep exists the way inv.expire_reservations does.
gaps.reality: There is no wty.expire_warranties function, no scheduled job, no transition table, and nothing in the DDL that ever changes a warranty's status after wty.issue_warranty writes 'issued'. The distinction between `issued` and `active` is defined NOWHERE — no comment, no contract document, no constraint explains when one becomes the other. `ix_warranty_records_expiry ON wty.warranty_records (tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, expiry_date)` exists and is clearly shaped for such a sweep, but no code uses it.
gaps.mitigation: The backend owns the entire lifecycle. It must define and document the transition graph itself, always writing a wty.warranty_status_history row in the SAME transaction as the wty.warranty_records UPDATE (nothing forces this). An expiry sweep is buildable with the existing SELECT/UPDATE grants against ix_warranty_records_expiry. Critical side effect to get right: ex_warranty_records_no_overlap only excludes rows with status IN ('issued','active'), so moving a record to 'expired' or 'voided' FREES the vehicle+coverage slot for a new overlapping record. The issued/active semantics must be an owner decision, not an invention — if no basis exists, treat 'issued' as the only state the backend sets and leave 'active' unused rather than inventing a rule.

gaps.assumed: A warranty's covered items are traceably linked to the specific delivered work-order jobs and parts.
gaps.reality: wty.warranty_record_items.source_job_id and source_part_id have NO foreign key, are both nullable, are not coupled to item_kind, and are not unique per record. The P1-11 data dictionary calls them 'opaque'. The database accepts an item with no source at all, with a source from another tenant, or with the same job repeated.
gaps.mitigation: Application-level composition is the only option and is fully achievable: resolve source_job_id against wo.jobs and source_part_id against the part tables (inv.part_issues / wo.required_parts) constrained to the record's own work_order_id and scope, enforce (item_kind='service') ⇔ source_job_id IS NOT NULL and (item_kind='part') ⇔ source_part_id IS NOT NULL, and de-duplicate on (warranty_record_id, source id) before insert. Every one of those must carry a regression test that fails against the unguarded path, because the database will never object.

gaps.assumed: Issuing a warranty selects the coverage matching the intended covered scope (all / service / part).
gaps.reality: wty.issue_warranty takes only (delivery, policy, correlation, idempotency_key). Its coverage query omits covered_scope from the predicate and ends `ORDER BY effective_from DESC LIMIT 1`, while ex_warranty_coverage_no_overlap keys ON covered_scope — so a policy legitimately holding 'service' and 'part' coverages effective on the same date makes the pick non-deterministic (identical effective_from, arbitrary tie-break).
gaps.mitigation: Either constrain each policy to one active coverage per date in the application (validate on coverage create and reject a second active scope overlapping in time), or refuse to issue when more than one coverage is effective for the policy at the delivery date and return a business error naming the ambiguity. The third option — raw INSERT into wty.warranty_records with an explicitly chosen coverage — is granted and structurally guarded by tg_warranty_records_coherence, but then the backend must itself bind start_date := delivered_at::date and odometer_at_issue := the delivery's final reading, because that value binding lives only inside wty.issue_warranty (accepted residual M-wty-2b / WVR-P1-12-001).

gaps.assumed: odometer_at_issue and odometer_limit are comparable numbers in a known unit.
gaps.reality: They are bare `integer` columns with no unit. wty.issue_warranty stores `o.value::integer` from veh.odometer_readings, whose `value numeric(12,1)` is stored VERBATIM in km or mi (`ck_odometer_readings_unit CHECK (unit IN ('km','mi'))`), and whose own comment names the generated `value_km` as the 'Sole basis for monotonicity and point-in-time resolution'. issue_warranty ignores value_km. sal.complete_delivery's `p_odometer_unit text DEFAULT 'km'` is caller-supplied, so a mi delivery is fully reachable.
gaps.mitigation: No schema fix is possible. The backend must join veh.odometer_readings on delivery.final_odometer_reading_id and surface `unit` (and ideally value_km) alongside every warranty representation, so a consumer is never handed a unitless ceiling. It must also expect the ::integer cast to round and therefore must not assert odometer_at_issue equals the recorded reading. A tenant mixing km and mi deliveries under one odometer-limited policy is a documented accepted limitation, not something the backend can silently normalise (normalising would change the stored value away from what the protected function writes).

gaps.assumed: A warranty-borne invoice line is backed by a real, live, covering warranty record.
gaps.reality: sal.invoice_line_amounts.warranty_pay_amount is enforced only by `ck_invoice_line_amounts_payer_split CHECK (customer_pay_amount + warranty_pay_amount = gross_amount)`. Neither sal.invoice_lines nor sal.invoice_line_amounts has a warranty_record_id column, and no FK, trigger, or RLS policy connects the two modules. The `warranty_split_recorded` financial event binds only to the invoice's own line sum.
gaps.mitigation: Application-level only, and it is a genuine soft spot: P1-22 can look up a live warranty for the invoice's work order / vehicle before allowing warranty_pay_amount > 0, but nothing persists that link, so the association is unauditable after the fact. Record this explicitly as an accepted limitation rather than implying the split is warranty-verified. Also note that `sal.guard_event_completeness` does NOT require warranty_split_recorded, so the split event exists only if the invoice is issued through sal.issue_invoice — the backend must use that primitive.

gaps.assumed: Effective-dated coverage terms are immutable once created, so eligibility is stable. The P1-11 policy-version contract states: 'Coverage is immutable in its identity anchors (org.guard_immutable_columns freezes policy_id/effective_from/scope)'.
gaps.reality: THE DDL DISAGREES AND IS AUTHORITATIVE. tg_warranty_coverage_immutable freezes exactly `'tenant_id', 'company_id', 'policy_id', 'effective_from', 'created_at', 'created_by'`. `covered_scope` is NOT in that list — the prose's claim that scope is frozen is wrong. Neither is `duration_months`, `odometer_limit`, `effective_to`, or `status`, and app_runtime holds UPDATE on the table. A live coverage row's duration can be edited in place.
gaps.mitigation: Records already issued are protected by tg_warranty_records_freeze, so history genuinely cannot be rewritten — the P1-11 conclusion survives, but for a different reason than the prose gives. For FUTURE issues, an in-place duration edit silently changes terms with no version trail. P1-22 should treat a terms change as close-the-interval-and-open-a-new-one (set effective_to, insert a new coverage) rather than an UPDATE of duration_months, and should restrict the coverage-update endpoint to effective_to / status transitions. Raise the prose-vs-DDL divergence on covered_scope as a documentation finding against docs/phase-1/phase-1-11/phase-1-11-warranty-policy-version-contract.md.

gaps.assumed: wty.warranty_policies.policy_code is a stable business identifier.
gaps.reality: tg_warranty_policies_immutable freezes only `'tenant_id', 'company_id', 'created_at', 'created_by'`. policy_code is mutable via the granted UPDATE, subject only to `ck_warranty_policies_code CHECK (policy_code ~ '^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,62}$')` and the partial `uq_warranty_policies_code ON wty.warranty_policies (tenant_id, company_id, policy_code) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`. This diverges from the org-module convention whose guard comment says 'codes and scope columns are immutable after creation … controlled recoding is soft-delete + recreate, never in-place edit'.
gaps.mitigation: The backend should not expose policy_code in an update payload; treat it as create-only and require soft-delete + recreate for recoding, matching the org convention. Note the uniqueness index is partial on deleted_at IS NULL, so a soft-deleted policy frees its code for reuse.

gaps.assumed: Calling wty.issue_warranty twice with the same idempotency key is safe under concurrency and across scopes.
gaps.reality: The pre-check `SELECT id INTO v_existing FROM wty.warranty_records WHERE tenant_id = v_tenant AND idempotency_key = p_idempotency_key` is an unlocked, RLS-filtered read with no request fingerprinting. Concurrent duplicates race to 23505 on uq_warranty_records_idempotency; a key consumed outside the caller's allowed branches is invisible and also produces 23505; the same key reused against a different delivery returns the FIRST record silently.
gaps.mitigation: Layer the Phase 1-4 idempotency store over the call as the P1-11 P1-22 contract already directs ('Idempotency-Key request handling (the Phase 1-4 store) layered over the P1-11 unique business keys'), fingerprint the request body so a key reused with different inputs is a 422 rather than a silent wrong answer, and map a 23505 on uq_warranty_records_idempotency to the idempotent-replay response rather than a 500.

gaps.assumed: Renewing a warranty can start the day the previous one expires.
gaps.reality: ex_warranty_records_no_overlap uses `daterange(start_date, expiry_date, '[]')` — a CLOSED range on both ends — so a renewal starting exactly on the prior record's expiry_date overlaps at that single day and raises 23P01. This differs from the coverage EXCLUDE, which uses '[)' and does permit boundary-sharing.
gaps.mitigation: Purely application-level: the backend must either start a renewal at expiry_date + 1 day, or transition the prior record out of ('issued','active') first. It should map 23P01 on wty.warranty_records to a specific business error naming the overlapping vehicle+coverage window, and must not confuse it with 23P01 on wty.warranty_coverage (overlapping active coverage), which needs a different message.

gaps.assumed: P1-22 delivers warranty CLAIM adjudication. P1-11's own documents state this repeatedly and explicitly: the schema comment says 'Full warranty claim adjudication is deferred to Phase 1-22 (P1-OD-024)', and the warranty-record contract says 'Claim structures activate with the P1-22 backend'.
gaps.reality: NO CLAIM TABLE EXISTS. `grep -rn "claim" --include=*.sql supabase/` returns hits only in shared.event_outbox (worker claim/claimed_by/claim_outbox_events) and prose comments — there is no wty.warranty_claims, no wty.claim_lines, no wty.claim_status_history, no claim function, no claim permission code, and no claim event type. The ONLY claim affordance in the entire protected schema is the string literal `claimed_against` inside ck_warranty_records_status and ck_warranty_status_history_to_status. P1-22 is backend-only: no migration 120 may be created and migrations 1-119 may not be modified.
gaps.mitigation: None at the application layer for real claim adjudication — a claim has no row to live in, so claim intake, assessment, approval/rejection, cost attribution and claim history CANNOT be persisted without inventing storage, which is forbidden. The only thing P1-22 can legitimately build is a status advance to `claimed_against` on wty.warranty_records plus a wty.warranty_status_history row carrying a free-text `reason` and a `correlation_id` — an unstructured marker, not adjudication. This must be declared loudly as an out-of-scope carry-forward in the phase's accepted limitations (mirroring how P1-21 handled D-04), NOT silently half-built. If the P1-22 task list contains a claim-adjudication task, that task is unbuildable as specified and needs an owner decision before any code is written.

verdict.searched: (1) Full read of supabase/migrations/20260724095000_wty_warranty.sql (the entire wty DDL, all 6 sections). (2) Object enumeration: `grep -rhoE "CREATE TABLE (IF NOT EXISTS )?[a-z_]+\.[a-z_]+" supabase/migrations/` → 242 tables total; filtered to sal|wty|rec → wty has EXACTLY 5 tables (warranty_policies, warranty_coverage, warranty_records, warranty_record_items, warranty_status_history). (3) `grep -rhn "wty\.[a-z_]*" -o supabase/migrations/` → EXACTLY 8 wty objects repo-wide (5 tables + guard_warranty_record_freeze, guard_warranty_record_coherence, issue_warranty). No claim function. (4) `grep -rni "claim" --include=*.sql supabase/` — every hit triaged; non-outbox hits are prose comments plus the two CHECK constraints. (5) Synonym hunt for a differently-named table: `claim|adjudicat|rma|goodwill|redress|recourse|chargeback|reimburs`, then `case|ticket|dispute|incident|grievance|complaint` across all migrations — only rec.complaints, which is FK-bound to rec.reception_visits (intake complaints, not warranty). (6) Seeds: `ls supabase/seeds/` (6 files) + `grep -rniE "wty|warranty" supabase/seeds/` → only two permission codes exist, `wty.policy.manage` and `wty.warranty.issue`. No claim permission, no claim seed. (7) Generated/JSONB escape hatch: `grep -nE "jsonb" supabase/migrations/20260724*.sql` → jsonb appears ONLY in rpt (parameter_schema, filter_definition); zero jsonb/payload column anywhere in wty or sal. (8) Application-composition escape hatch: read shared.notes DDL (polymorphic entity_type/entity_id) and then its write capability migration 20260730090000_crm_customer_notes_write_capability.sql — policies `ins_notes_crm_customer`/`upd_notes_crm_customer` pin `entity_type = 'crm.business_partners'`. (9) Source tree: `grep -rniE "warranty|wty\." src/ --include=*.ts` → 2 comment-only hits, no warranty module exists yet. (10) Docs: phase-1-11-p1-22-backend-contract.md, phase-1-11-warranty-record-contract.md, phase-1-11-warranty-eligibility-contract.md, phase-1-11-data-dictionary-wty.md, phase-1-11-object-inventory.md, phase-1-11-od-linkage.md (P1-OD-024), and docs/phase-1/phase-1-22/execution-checkpoint.md.
verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED — refutation failed on every avenue. This is a genuine BLOCKER contract gap.

WHAT DOES NOT EXIST (verified by enumeration, not by absence of a grep hit):
The wty schema contains exactly 8 objects repo-wide. There is no wty.warranty_claims, no wty.claim_lines, no wty.claim_status_history, no claim function, no claim permission code, no jsonb payload column, and no implemented claim event type. I searched for a differently-named table (dispute/case/ticket/incident/RMA/chargeback/reimbursement) and for a seed-rather-than-DDL definition; nothing. The ONLY claim affordance in 119 migrations is one string literal in two CHECK vocabularies:
  CONSTRAINT ck_warranty_records_status CHECK (status IN ('issued', 'active', 'expired', 'voided', 'claimed_against'))
  CONSTRAINT ck_warranty_status_history_to_status CHECK (to_status IN ('issued', 'active', 'expired', 'voided', 'claimed_against'))

THE APPLICATION-COMPOSITION ESCAPE HATCH IS CLOSED AT THE RLS LAYER — this is the strongest new evidence, and it makes the gap worse than stated. shared.notes is a generic polymorphic table (entity_type/entity_id, ck_notes_entity_type_format `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`) and looked like a viable place to persist unstructured claim narrative. It is not. Its only runtime write policies, added by DBCR-P1-16-001 in 20260730090000_crm_customer_notes_write_capability.sql, hard-pin `AND entity_type = 'crm.business_partners'` in BOTH the INSERT and UPDATE predicates. A note attached to a wty.warranty_records row is rejected by RLS. That migration's own header states the rule: "A future module that needs to annotate its own entities adds its own scoped policy" — i.e. a migration. Confirmed there is no generic fallback store reachable from app_runtime for warranty.

ONE NUANCE THAT DOES NOT RESCUE IT: permission codes are seed rows, not DDL (`INSERT INTO iam.permissions ...` lives only in supabase/seeds/04_iam_permission_catalog.sql, and DBCR-P1-16-001 explicitly notes "the permission code lives in the seed catalog, seed 04"). So minting `wty.claim.adjudicate` would not strictly need migration 120. This still refutes nothing: a permission is inert with no table to gate and no policy to reference, and inventing a permission code is forbidden by the archaeology rules regardless.

THE MITIGATION PATH IS REAL BUT WEAKER THAN THE ARCHAEOLOGIST DESCRIBES. The status advance is genuinely buildable with no migration — app_runtime holds GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE on wty.warranty_records under upd_warranty_records_scope, and wty.guard_warranty_record_freeze deliberately guards only vehicle_id/work_order_id/delivery_record_id/policy_id/coverage_id/start_date/expiry_date/odometer_at_issue/odometer_limit, leaving status free to advance; wty.warranty_status_history has GRANT SELECT, INSERT under ins_warranty_status_history_scope. But that marker cannot carry adjudication: `status` is a single scalar with exactly ONE claim value, so the schema cannot represent a second claim on the same record, nor any outcome (there is no approved/rejected/assessed value); wty.warranty_status_history has no claim_id, no amount/cost column, and a single actor_id, so cost attribution and maker/checker approval are structurally impossible.

BONUS DEFECT THE ARCHAEOLOGIST MISSED — the mitigation silently disarms a binding amendment. The M-wty-1 no-overlap guard is `CONSTRAINT ex_warranty_records_no_overlap EXCLUDE USING gist (...) WHERE (status IN ('issued', 'active') AND deleted_at IS NULL)`. `claimed_against` is OUTSIDE that predicate. Advancing a record to `claimed_against` therefore drops it out of the exclusion constraint and makes a second overlapping warranty record for the same vehicle+coverage insertable — the only legitimate P1-22 claim affordance weakens a P1-11 binding amendment as a side effect. This must be stated in the limitation and covered by a regression test.

DIVERGENCE FINDING (handoff prose vs deployed DDL; DDL is authoritative). phase-1-11-warranty-record-contract.md:38 asserts the `claimed_against` status "is prepared so a later claim links to the record without schema change." The deployed DDL contradicts this: there is nothing for a claim to link FROM. A status value on the parent is not storage for a child entity. Note that P1-11's own P1-22 contract already hedges at line 46 — `warranty-claim.status.changed.v1` (EVT-WTY-001, **if claims activate**) — and od-linkage.md records P1-OD-024 as "Held / deferred". The "without schema change" sentence is the single misleading claim and should be raised as a documentation finding against P1-11.

VERDICT: a migration would genuinely be required, and P1-22 is backend-only. The archaeologist's recommendation stands — declare it loudly as an out-of-scope carry-forward in accepted limitations (mirroring P1-21's D-04), and escalate to the owner before any claim-adjudication task is coded.

gaps.assumed: Warranty read endpoints (list/get a vehicle's warranties, list covered items, read the status history) are authorized by a warranty read permission.
gaps.reality: No such permission code exists. The catalog has exactly `wty.policy.manage` and `wty.warranty.issue` (supabase/seeds/04_iam_permission_catalog.sql:72-73) and nothing else in module `wty`. Neither code's stated meaning ('Manage warranty policies and coverage' / 'Issue warranty records') covers reading a warranty. There is also no code for voiding a warranty, expiring one, or recording a claim.
gaps.mitigation: Adding permission codes does not require a migration — the codes live in the seed file, and P1-16 set the precedent by adding `crm.customer.read` / `crm.customer.create` there. So P1-22 can add e.g. a warranty read code and a void code to supabase/seeds/04_iam_permission_catalog.sql. BUT: `.github/ci-baselines/schema-baseline.json` pins `permissionCount: 100` and scripts/ci/migration-replay-checks.mjs:238 fails the build on any drift, so the baseline must be updated in the same commit. Do NOT fall back to gating warranty reads on `wty.warranty.issue` — that would grant read to issuers only and deny it to everyone else.

verdict.reasoning:
The archaeologist's factual claims are all CONFIRMED, but the BLOCKER severity is REFUTED: no migration is required, and the decisive proof is stronger than the one they offered.

CONFIRMED FACTS (verified against DDL, not prose):
1. Exactly two `wty` codes exist. `supabase/seeds/04_iam_permission_catalog.sql:72-73`:
   ('wty.policy.manage', 'wty', 'Manage warranty policies and coverage', 'medium', '00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001'),
   ('wty.warranty.issue', 'wty', 'Issue warranty records', 'medium', '00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001'),
   A repo-wide `rg "wty\.[a-z_]+\.[a-z_]+"` returns ONLY those two lines plus their mirror in docs/database/permission-catalog-reference.md:63-64. There is no warranty read code, no void code, no expire code, no claim code. ABSENT.
2. Only the seed inserts into iam.permissions (line 15). NO migration inserts permissions anywhere (`rg "iam.permissions"` across supabase/, src/, scripts/ — every migration hit is a FK reference, a GRANT, an RLS policy on the catalog itself, or a lookup inside a function).
3. No wildcard, no implication mechanism. `rg "implication|implies|parent_permission|permission_group"` over supabase/migrations/ and src/modules/iam/ returns only unrelated "Security implications" section headers. The seed header states "no wildcard permission".
4. An unseeded code FAILS CLOSED, so you cannot simply invent one in a route. supabase/migrations/20260718097000_iam_context_and_permission_functions.sql:99-102 (has_permission) and :159-162 (has_permission_in_scope) both contain: `SELECT id INTO v_perm FROM iam.permissions WHERE permission_code = p_code; IF v_perm IS NULL THEN RETURN false; END IF;` — an unknown code denies everyone.
5. Void/expire/claim are real, unnamed authorities. supabase/migrations/20260724095000_wty_warranty.sql:150 `CONSTRAINT ck_warranty_records_status CHECK (status IN ('issued', 'active', 'expired', 'voided', 'claimed_against'))` and :306 `CONSTRAINT ck_warranty_status_history_to_status CHECK (to_status IN ('issued','active','expired','voided','claimed_against'))`.
6. The baseline pin is real and will break the build. reports.lens: Permissions, RLS, and tenancy on the protected `sal.*` / `wty.*` schema (P1-11 migrations 20260724090000–20260724095000), read at `feature/p1-22-billing-payment-delivery-warranty-backend` = `d9a2c1dc8d09e8fe2b3cf9ca8a2d4a6c905756de`, 119 migrations, no migration 120.
reports.summary: The seeded catalogue (`supabase/seeds/04_iam_permission_catalog.sql`, 100 permissions total) contains exactly twelve `sal`/`wty` codes and two `rpt` codes, and **only three of the twelve are enforced anywhere in the deployed DDL**: `sal.finance.view` (26 policy clauses), `sal.delivery.manage` (4) and `sal.delivery.view` (2). The other nine — `sal.invoice.manage`, `sal.invoice.issue`, `sal.payment.record`, `sal.payment.allocate`, `sal.credit.manage`, `sal.reversal.approve`, `sal.delivery.complete`, `wty.policy.manage`, `wty.warranty.issue` — are catalogue entries with **no RLS enforcement point at all**, so they only become real if P1-22 declares them in `defineOperation`. All 24 `sal`/`wty` tables carry `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` **and** `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`; 18 are branch-scoped (`tenant_id`+`company_id`+`branch_id`), 5 are company-only (no `branch_id` column: `sal.invoice_numbering_configs`, `sal.delivery_checklist_templates`, `sal.delivery_checklist_template_items`, `wty.warranty_policies`, `wty.warranty_coverage`), and `sal.payment_methods` is dual-scope with neither column. Every permission clause uses the **scope-blind `iam.has_permission(...)`, never `iam.has_permission_in_scope(...)`**, and `app.company_ids` / `app.branch_ids` are the union of every active grant regardless of which permission it carries (`src/server/context/resolve-context.ts`), so RLS is defence in depth only and every branch-scoped P1-22 operation must still call `authorizeScope` with the row's own company **and** branch. `sal.finance.view` is misnamed: it gates INSERT and UPDATE as well as SELECT on seven tables, so recording a receipt, allocating one, approving a credit note or reversal, and issuing an invoice all require it *in addition to* whatever the catalogue code suggests. Six UPDATE policies silently drop the company/branch narrowing that their own SELECT/INSERT siblings carry, contradicting `docs/phase-1/phase-1-11/phase-1-11-rls-matrix.md`. And the three balance derivations are `SECURITY INVOKER` + RLS-filtered, so a caller without `sal.finance.view` gets **`0` rather than an error** — a silent wrong answer, not a denial. The single largest gap is that P1-11 defers "full warranty claim adjudication" to P1-22 while shipping **no claim table, no claim permission code, and no claim event type**.

No occurrence of 'sal.invoice.manage', 'sal.invoice.issue', 'sal.payment.record', 'sal.payment.allocate', 'sal.credit.manage', 'sal.reversal.approve', 'sal.delivery.complete', 'wty.policy.manage', or 'wty.warranty.issue' anywhere in any migration.

findings.fact: `sal.finance.view` is not a read gate — it gates INSERT and UPDATE too, on every one of the seven finance tables. Its catalogue description says only 'View financial amounts'.
findings.identifier: ins_receipts_gated, ins_payment_allocations_gated, ins_credit_notes_gated, ins_receipt_reversals_gated, ins_financial_events_gated, ins_invoice_amounts_gated, ins_invoice_line_amounts_gated (and the matching upd_* / sel_* policies)
findings.evidence:
CREATE POLICY ins_receipts_gated ON sal.receipts FOR INSERT TO app_runtime
  WITH CHECK (tenant_id = iam.current_tenant_id() AND iam.has_permission('sal.finance.view')
    AND (iam.allowed_company_ids() IS NULL OR company_id = ANY (iam.allowed_company_ids()))
    AND (iam.allowed_branch_ids() IS NULL OR branch_id = ANY (iam.allowed_branch_ids())));
findings.consequence: Every P1-22 money-writing operation must declare `sal.finance.view` IN ADDITION to its semantic code, because the conjunction in `defineOperation` is exactly what the DB requires: record-receipt = ['sal.payment.record','sal.finance.view']; allocate = ['sal.payment.allocate','sal.finance.view']; approve credit note = ['sal.credit.manage','sal.finance.view']; approve reversal = ['sal.reversal.approve','sal.finance.view']. Declaring only the semantic code produces a runtime SQLSTATE 42501 RLS violation from inside the protected function instead of a clean ERR-IAM-001 403.

findings.fact: `sal.issue_invoice` requires `sal.finance.view` even though the catalogue implies `sal.invoice.issue` is sufficient: the function writes `sal.invoice_amounts` and `sal.financial_events`, both finance-gated on INSERT/UPDATE.
findings.identifier: sal.issue_invoice(p_invoice_id uuid, p_correlation_id uuid) — GRANT EXECUTE TO app_runtime; SECURITY INVOKER
findings.consequence: The issue-invoice operation must declare `permissions: ['sal.invoice.issue', 'sal.finance.view']`. Without the second code the UPDATE matches zero rows under `upd_invoice_amounts_gated` and the follow-on INSERT fails `ins_invoice_amounts_gated` — a 42501 three layers down, not a denial.

findings.fact: `sal.complete_delivery` de-facto requires `sal.delivery.view`, not `sal.delivery.complete`. Both of its pre-gates are SELECTs against `sal.delivery.view`-gated tables, so a caller without it is told there is 'no verified authorized receiver' when in fact the row exists but is invisible.
findings.identifier: sal.complete_delivery(uuid, numeric, text, uuid); sel_authorized_receivers_gated; sel_delivery_signatures_gated
findings.consequence: The complete-delivery operation must declare `permissions: ['sal.delivery.complete', 'sal.delivery.view']`. P1-22 must NOT surface the raw 23514 message to the caller: it is misleading (it reports missing evidence when the real cause is a missing permission). The backend should pre-check the receiver and signature under the same transaction and map a genuine absence to a distinct error from a permission failure.

findings.fact: The three balance derivations are `SECURITY INVOKER` and RLS-filtered, so a caller without `sal.finance.view` receives `0` — a valid-looking number — instead of a denial. `sal.invoice_open_receivable` LEFT JOINs the gated amount table and COALESCEs the NULL to zero.
findings.identifier: sal.invoice_open_receivable(p_invoice_id uuid), sal.receipt_unallocated(p_receipt_id uuid), sal.partner_outstanding_balance(p_partner_id uuid) — all GRANT EXECUTE TO app_runtime, app_readonly
findings.consequence: Every P1-22 operation that returns or acts on an open receivable / unallocated amount / partner balance MUST declare `sal.finance.view`. Returning `0` to a non-finance caller would report a fully-paid invoice for an unpaid one. Note also that `sal.invoices` itself is NOT finance-gated, so status is visible while the amount is not — the read model must not mix the two under one permission.

-- `invoice_amounts` / `invoice_line_amounts` / `authorized_receivers` all say Scope = branch.
findings.consequence: On these six tables RLS gives NO branch isolation on UPDATE — a tenant-wide finance holder can update a receipt, credit note, reversal, invoice-amount row or receiver in ANY branch of the tenant. The row-freeze triggers (`sal.guard_receipt_freeze`, `sal.guard_dual_control_approval`, `sal.guard_invoice_amount_frozen`) limit WHAT can change but not WHERE. P1-22 must therefore treat `authorizeScope({ companyId, branchId })` after locking the row as the only branch control on every update path touching these six tables, and must not rely on RLS to catch a wrong-branch id. No migration may be added to fix the policies; this is an application-level obligation. Raise as an accepted-limitation finding and correct the matrix in the P1-22 archaeology record.

findings.fact: Every sal/wty policy calls the scope-blind `iam.has_permission(text)`. `iam.has_permission_in_scope` is never used in `sal` or `wty`. Combined with P1-18-A-01 — `app.company_ids`/`app.branch_ids` are aggregated over ALL active grants irrespective of which permission each grant carries — RLS narrowing is defence in depth only.

findings.evidence:
-- resolve-context.ts:
  `SELECT
      bool_or(g.scope_mode = 'unrestricted')                     AS unrestricted,
      array_remove(array_agg(DISTINCT s.company_id), NULL)       AS company_ids,
      array_remove(array_agg(DISTINCT s.branch_id), NULL)        AS branch_ids

Every branch-scoped P1-22 command addressed by a resource id must call `authorizeScope` with the resource's own `companyId` AND `branchId` once the row is locked, exactly as `requireScopedPermissions` demands ('deferred scoped authorization requires the resource\'s own company or branch, and neither was supplied').

findings.fact: `iam.has_permission_in_scope` matches a company scope row on `company_id` and a branch scope row on `branch_id` independently — the P1-21 H6 trap. Passing only one of the two under-constrains the decision.
findings.identifier: iam.has_permission_in_scope(p_code text, p_company uuid, p_branch uuid, p_department uuid)
findings.evidence:
OR EXISTS (
          SELECT 1 FROM iam.grant_scopes s
          WHERE s.tenant_id = g.tenant_id AND s.grant_id = g.id
            AND (

Passing branch alone admits a company-scoped grant in a different company only if that company row matches — but passing company alone admits every branch inside it, which is wrong for a branch-scoped write.

findings.fact: RLS is ENABLED and FORCED on all 24 `sal`/`wty` tables without exception, and every application role is NOLOGIN NOBYPASSRLS. There is no privileged bypass path: all 26 P1-11 functions are `SECURITY INVOKER … SET search_path = ''`, zero `SECURITY DEFINER`.

findings.fact: Column shape is not uniform: five tables have no `branch_id` column and one has neither `company_id` nor `branch_id`. Their policies narrow only as far as their columns allow.
findings.identifier: company-only (tenant_id, company_id): sal.invoice_numbering_configs, sal.delivery_checklist_templates, sal.delivery_checklist_template_items, wty.warranty_policies, wty.warranty_coverage. Payment-method administration is TENANT-scoped and structurally cannot be branch-narrowed; platform rows are readable by every tenant and are not writable by any application role (`ins_payment_methods_tenant` forbids `scope='platform'`).

findings.fact: `sal.guard_authorized_receiver` accepts ANY of the seven `rec.reception_party_roles.relationship_role` values — it never checks that the role is `authorized_receiver` — and it contains NO CRM authorized-person branch. The P1-11 contract document claims it also validates 'a valid CRM authorized-person relationship for the vehicle at delivered_at'. The DDL is authoritative; the doc is wrong.

    WHERE pr.tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND pr.company_id = NEW.company_id AND pr.branch_id = NEW.branch_id

    'service_requester', 'vehicle_owner', 'vehicle_user', 'payer',
    'billing_party', 'approving_party', 'authorized_receiver')),

-- authorized-person relationship for the vehicle at delivered_at.'

If P1-22 intends 'authorized receiver' to mean the `authorized_receiver` role, it must enforce `relationship_role = 'authorized_receiver'` in the application layer — the schema does not. findings.fact: The mandatory-checklist gate in `sal.complete_delivery` is COMPANY-WIDE and ignores template status: it counts every `is_mandatory` item of every template in the company, not the items of the template the delivery was built from (delivery records carry no template reference at all).
findings.consequence: Adding one mandatory item to ANY template in a company retroactively blocks every in-flight delivery in every branch of that company, including deliveries assembled against a different or archived template. P1-22's checklist-result API must record results for all company-wide mandatory items, and template administration must be treated as a high-blast-radius company-scoped operation. Do not model 'the delivery's template' — there is no such column.

findings.fact: `sal.complete_delivery` writes across two other schemas whose grants and policies P1-22 inherits: `rec.custody_history` (branch-scoped, SELECT+INSERT, no permission gate) and `veh.odometer_readings` (TENANT-scoped only — no company/branch columns — SELECT+INSERT, no permission gate). `capture_method = 'delivery'` is a legal value.
findings.identifier: rec.custody_history / ins_custody_history_scope / uq_custody_history_released; veh.odometer_readings / ins_odometer_readings_tenant / ck (capture_method IN ('reception','delivery','manual','correction'))

The exactly-once custody release is enforced by `uq_custody_history_released` (23505 on replay), so the backend must treat a duplicate as idempotent success rather than an error.

findings.fact: There is NO central permission-constant module anywhere under `src/`. Permission codes are inline string literals inside each route's `defineOperation({ permissions: [...] })`, validated only by the seed-catalogue cross-check in the phase endpoint-inventory scripts.
findings.consequence: P1-22 follows the same shape: literals in the route file, `scope: 'branch'` (or `'company'` for policy/coverage/template/numbering admin), and a conjunction when both a semantic code and `sal.finance.view` / `sal.delivery.view` are required ('ALL must pass (conjunction) — an operation needing "any of" is two operations'). Precedent for a multi-code declaration already exists (`permissions: ['qms.quality_control.read', 'iam.sensitive.view']`).

findings.fact: Not one `sal.*` or `wty.*` permission code is used by any existing route. P1-22 is the first consumer of all twelve.
findings.evidence: grep -rn "'sal\.|'wty\." src/app/api/v1 --include=*.ts → no matches. The 60 distinct permissions arrays in the route tree cover apt/crm/dia/iam/inv/org/qms/quo/rec/rpt/shared/svc/tech/veh/wo only.
findings.consequence: There is no existing usage to copy or to be consistent with. The permission-to-operation mapping is entirely P1-22's to establish, and the endpoint-inventory script for the phase must cross-check every declared code against `supabase/seeds/04_iam_permission_catalog.sql` (the P1-19/P1-20/P1-21 scripts all do this).

findings.fact: `iam.permissions` is SELECT-only to every application role, with no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policy or grant. New permission codes therefore come from seed 04, applied by the migration/owner role — not from a migration and not at runtime.
findings.consequence: P1-22 CAN add missing permission codes without violating the no-migration rule, by appending to `supabase/seeds/04_iam_permission_catalog.sql` (idempotent `ON CONFLICT (permission_code) DO NOTHING`) exactly as P1-21 did for the four `inv.*` codes. New codes must match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[a-z0-9_]+)+$` and carry a risk level in low|medium|high|critical.

findings.fact: `app_runtime` write feasibility is complete for the P1-22 surface without any migration: SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE on the 18 mutable tables, SELECT+INSERT only on the six append-only ledgers, DELETE on nothing, and EXECUTE on ten `SECURITY INVOKER` primitives. `app_worker` receives no grant at all.
findings.identifier: Append-only (SELECT, INSERT only): sal.invoice_status_history, sal.payment_allocations, sal.financial_events, sal.delivery_signatures, sal.delivery_status_history, wty.warranty_status_history. EXECUTE: sal.issue_invoice, sal.record_receipt, sal.allocate_receipt, sal.approve_credit_note, sal.approve_receipt_reversal, sal.complete_delivery, sal.invoice_open_receivable, sal.receipt_unallocated, sal.partner_outstanding_balance, wty.issue_warranty
findings.consequence: P1-22 needs no new migration for write access. Corrections on the six ledgers are new rows, never edits; there is no soft-delete on them either (no `deleted_at` column on `sal.payment_allocations`, `sal.financial_events`, `sal.delivery_signatures` or any status history). No P1-22 background worker can touch sal/wty — `app_worker` holds no grant, not even USAGE on the schemas.

findings.fact: `sal.payment_methods`'s SELECT policy exposes every platform row without any tenant predicate, by design; its write policies are tenant-only and forbid platform rows. Three platform methods are seeded and no other kind is representable.
findings.evidence:
CREATE POLICY sel_payment_methods_scope ON sal.payment_methods FOR SELECT TO app_runtime, app_readonly
  USING (scope = 'platform' OR tenant_id = iam.current_tenant_id());
  CONSTRAINT ck_payment_methods_kind CHECK (kind IN ('cash', 'card_terminal', 'bank_transfer')),
-- seed 08: ('platform', NULL, 'cash', 'cash', 'Cash', …), ('platform', NULL, 'card_terminal', …), ('platform', NULL, 'bank_transfer', …)
findings.consequence: P1-22 must never invent a payment-method kind: the vocabulary is exactly `cash`, `card_terminal`, `bank_transfer` (ASM-14 / CON-04 — no online gateway or settlement). A method-list read is tenant-scope and needs no permission gate; a tenant method-write operation has no catalogue code (see gaps).

findings.fact: The controlled audit-action catalogue contains ZERO `sal.*` / `wty.*` action codes; `defineOperation` throws at module load for any audited operation whose `auditAction` is not registered there.
findings.consequence: P1-22 must append `sal.*` / `wty.*` entries to `src/server/auth/audit-actions.ts` (an application file — permitted) BEFORE any route can declare an audited billing operation; the `financial` audit class already exists for them. Codes are permanent once shipped ('written into an append-only, hash-chained table … never be renamed').

gaps.assumed: A billing/delivery/warranty backend needs low-risk READ permissions so that a service advisor, receptionist or workshop controller can see an invoice, a receipt list, a delivery or a warranty record without holding a high-risk capability. Every other recent phase seeded exactly such a code (`inv.item.read`, `crm.customer.read`, `veh.vehicle.read`, `wo.work_order.read`, `quo.quotation.read`, `svc.service.read`, `dia.diagnostic.read`, `qms.quality_control.read`, `tech.technician.read`).
gaps.reality: NO read code exists for any of sal or wty. `sal.invoice.read`, `sal.payment.read`, `sal.receipt.read`, `sal.delivery.read`, `wty.warranty.read`, `wty.policy.read` are ALL ABSENT from `supabase/seeds/04_iam_permission_catalog.sql`. The only read-shaped codes are `sal.finance.view` and `sal.delivery.view`, both `risk_level = 'high'`.
gaps.mitigation: Two lawful options, no third. (a) Add the missing read codes to seed 04 — permitted, this is a seed and not a migration, and P1-21 set the precedent by adding four `inv.*` codes there. (b) Authorize reads with an existing code and accept that seeing an invoice requires a high-risk grant. Option (a) is strongly preferable and must be a named, reviewable decision; whichever is chosen, the code must NOT be invented at the call site — `iam.has_permission` returns false for a code absent from `iam.permissions`, so an unseeded code fails closed and silently denies everyone.

gaps.assumed: `sal.delivery.complete` ('Complete deliveries and close custody', high) is a real, enforced capability distinct from `sal.delivery.manage`.
gaps.reality: `sal.delivery.complete` appears in exactly one place in the whole repository: the seed row. It is referenced by no policy, no trigger, no function, and no route. Meanwhile `sal.complete_delivery` — the primitive it names — actually requires `sal.delivery.view` to see its own gates, and requires nothing else from the database.
gaps.mitigation: Declare it in the operation registry and make it real there: `permissions: ['sal.delivery.complete', 'sal.delivery.view'], scope: 'branch'`, plus `authorizeScope({ companyId, branchId })` on the locked `sal.delivery_records` row. Document in the P1-22 archaeology record that this code has no database enforcement point, so removing the declaration removes the control entirely — there is no RLS backstop.

gaps.assumed: Warranty lifecycle management — activating, expiring, voiding a warranty record — is an authority the schema recognises.
gaps.reality: `wty.warranty.issue` is the ONLY warranty write code. `ck_warranty_records_status CHECK (status IN ('issued','active','expired','voided','claimed_against'))` admits five states but there is NO transition guard: `wty.guard_warranty_record_freeze` freezes vehicle/work order/delivery/policy/coverage/dates/odometer and deliberately lets `status` change to anything in the vocabulary, in any order, including straight back from `voided`. `upd_warranty_records_scope` carries no permission clause at all.
gaps.mitigation: The warranty state machine is entirely P1-22's to define and enforce in the application layer; the database will not reject an illegal transition. Either add a `wty.warranty.status.manage` code to seed 04 (mirroring the `veh.vehicle.status.manage` split from `veh.vehicle.manage`) or explicitly declare that voiding/expiring is out of scope. Do NOT invent an ordering rule and present it as a schema contract — there is none.

gaps.assumed: Administering tenant payment methods, invoice numbering configuration, and delivery checklist templates are authorized capabilities.
gaps.reality: No permission code covers any of the three. `sal.payment_methods`, `sal.invoice_numbering_configs`, `sal.delivery_checklist_templates` and `sal.delivery_checklist_template_items` all carry `GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE … TO app_runtime` and RLS policies with NO permission clause — only tenant (and, for the latter three, company) narrowing. `sal.invoice_numbering_configs.mode` admits only `'gapless'`/`'gapped'` and `sal.payment_methods.kind` only the three seeded kinds, but nothing says who may set them.
gaps.mitigation: Either reuse `org.settings.manage` (the P1-15 precedent: 'a message template is tenant configuration, and minting a second code for it would split one authority across two names') for numbering and checklist-template administration, or seed new codes. Whichever is chosen must be an explicit decision recorded in the archaeology document, because with no RLS clause the declared permission IS the only control. Note also that the checklist-template gate is company-wide with company-wide blast radius (see findings), so it should not be a low-risk code.

gaps.assumed: The RLS matrix's claim that `receipts`, `credit_notes`, `receipt_reversals`, `invoice_amounts`, `invoice_line_amounts` and `authorized_receivers` are branch-scoped on all commands, so RLS backstops a wrong-branch write.
gaps.reality: Their UPDATE policies key on tenant + permission ONLY. `upd_receipts_gated USING (tenant_id = iam.current_tenant_id() AND iam.has_permission('sal.finance.view'))` — no `company_id = ANY (iam.allowed_company_ids())`, no `branch_id = ANY (iam.allowed_branch_ids())`. The handoff prose is wrong; the DDL is authoritative.
gaps.mitigation: Application-level only, since no migration may be added. Every P1-22 update path touching these six tables must (1) lock the row, (2) read its own `company_id`/`branch_id`, (3) call `authorizeScope({ companyId, branchId })`, and (4) include both as explicit SQL predicates on the UPDATE rather than trusting RLS to add them. Record the divergence as a finding against `docs/phase-1/phase-1-11/phase-1-11-rls-matrix.md` and carry the residual as an accepted limitation.

gaps.assumed: `sal.finance.view` denial is a clean authorization failure that a caller will recognise.
gaps.reality: On the READ path it is not a failure at all: `sal.invoice_open_receivable`, `sal.receipt_unallocated` and `sal.partner_outstanding_balance` are `SECURITY INVOKER` + RLS-filtered and return `0` for a caller who cannot see the amounts. `sal.invoice_open_receivable` LEFT JOINs `sal.invoice_amounts` and then executes `v_gross := COALESCE(v_gross, 0);` — so an unpaid invoice reports a zero open receivable. `sal.receipt_unallocated` short-circuits on the invisible row: `IF v_amount IS NULL OR v_status = 'reversed' THEN RETURN 0; END IF;`
gaps.mitigation: Declare `sal.finance.view` on every operation that reads or acts on a derived balance, so the request is denied at the middleware with ERR-IAM-001 (403) before the function is ever called. Additionally, never surface a derivation result to a caller whose permission set was not checked in the same transaction, and never use these functions as an authorization signal ('balance is 0, therefore paid').

gaps.assumed: An outbox event contract exists for the P1-22 surface — `phase-1-11-p1-22-backend-contract.md` names `invoice.issued.v1`, `payment.recorded.v1`, `payment.allocated.v1`, `credit-note.issued.v1`, `receipt.reversed.v1`, `delivery.completed.v1`, `warranty.issued.v1`, `warranty-claim.status.changed.v1`.
gaps.reality: They are labelled 'documented, not implemented' / 'Anticipated contracts' in that very document, and none of the eight strings appears anywhere under `src/`. The only closed vocabulary that actually exists is `ck_financial_events_event_type CHECK (event_type IN ('invoice_issued','receipt_recorded','payment_allocated','credit_note_issued','receipt_reversed','warranty_split_recorded'))` with `ck_financial_events_source_type CHECK (source_type IN ('invoice','receipt','payment_allocation','credit_note','receipt_reversal'))`.
gaps.mitigation: P1-22 may define the outbox event names in application code (`src/server/events/`), but must derive them from the six DEPLOYED `event_type` values rather than the eight aspirational names — note the deployed set has `warranty_split_recorded` (which the doc omits) and no claim event at all. `sal.financial_events` is append-only, provenance-guarded (`sal.guard_financial_event_provenance` binds amount and currency to the source row) and single-use (`uq_financial_events_source UNIQUE (tenant_id, source_type, source_id, event_type)`), so it is a sound projection source; the event names are not a schema contract and must not be presented as one.

gaps.assumed: Audit actions for billing/delivery/warranty operations can be named at the call site.
gaps.reality: `defineOperation` calls `auditActionViolation()` against the frozen `AUDIT_ACTIONS` array and throws `OperationRegistrationError` at module load for any unregistered code. `src/server/auth/audit-actions.ts` contains no `sal.*` or `wty.*` entry.
gaps.mitigation: Append the required `sal.*` / `wty.*` definitions to `src/server/auth/audit-actions.ts` before writing any route — an application-file change, fully permitted under the backend-only rule. Use the existing `financial` audit class. Remember the file's own rule: codes land in an append-only hash-chained table and can never be renamed.

gaps.assumed: A route declaring an operation is automatically visible to the OpenAPI contract check.
gaps.reality: It is not. `tests/openapi-contract.test.ts` builds the document from the module registry, and a route that no test imports is simply absent — the file carries the explicit note that importing the route is what 'puts the operation in the registry'.
gaps.mitigation: Every new P1-22 route file must be added as an `import '@/app/api/v1/…/route';` line in `tests/openapi-contract.test.ts`, or both sides of the contract check will agree on the same incomplete registry and pass. This is the recorded P1-20 trap and it applies unchanged.

gaps.assumed: P1-11 explicitly assigns 'full warranty claim adjudication (P1-OD-024)' to P1-22 — stated in the schema comment on `wty`, in `phase-1-11-p1-22-backend-contract.md` §'What P1-22 owns', in `phase-1-11-od-linkage.md`, `phase-1-11-warranty-record-contract.md` and `phase-1-11-warranty-eligibility-contract.md`.
gaps.reality: THERE IS NO CLAIM TABLE ANYWHERE IN THE DATABASE. `grep -rn "CREATE TABLE.*claim" supabase/migrations/` returns nothing across all 119 migrations. The `wty` schema is exactly five tables: `warranty_policies`, `warranty_coverage`, `warranty_records`, `warranty_record_items`, `warranty_status_history`. The ONLY trace of a claim is the string `'claimed_against'` in `ck_warranty_records_status` and `ck_warranty_status_history_to_status`. There is no claim permission code (`wty.claim.*` does not exist in the catalogue), no claim event type (`ck_financial_events_event_type` is closed to six values, none of them a claim), and no claim audit action.
