gaps.mitigation: None at the schema level, and no migration is authorized. P1-22 can at most record that a warranty record has been claimed against, by transitioning `wty.warranty_records.status` to `'claimed_against'` and appending a `wty.warranty_status_history` row — which stores a status and a free-text `reason`, and nothing else: no claimant, no claim amount, no adjudication decision, no approver, no claim number. Any operation named 'submit/adjudicate/approve/reject a warranty claim' must be declared OUT OF SCOPE and carried forward as an accepted limitation, in the manner of P1-21 D-04. Building a partial claim workflow on top of `reason` text would be inventing persistence.

verdict.searched: (1) `grep -rniE "claim" supabase/migrations/` across all 119 migrations — every hit is `shared.event_outbox` worker-lease vocabulary (`claim_outbox_events`, `claimed_by`, `ck_event_outbox_claim_pair`), the two `'claimed_against'` CHECK values, or prose in comments. (2) `grep -rniE "CREATE (TABLE|VIEW|MATERIALIZED VIEW|TYPE|FUNCTION|SEQUENCE)[^;]*claim" supabase/` — exit 1, zero matches. (3) `CREATE TABLE` inventory of `supabase/migrations/20260724095000_wty_warranty.sql` — exactly 5 tables. (4) Cross-checked against the DEPLOYED catalog snapshot `supabase/.temp/pgdelta/catalog-local-migrations-2d15e803…-1785261654495.json` (pgdelta dump of migrations applied, 291 relations incl. Supabase-managed schemas) via a node probe over `tables`/`views`/`materializedViews`/`enums`/`procedures`/`sequences`: wty tables = warranty_coverage, warranty_policies, warranty_record_items, warranty_records, warranty_status_history (5); tables matching /claim/ = `auth.mfa_amr_claims` ONLY (Supabase auth MFA authentication-method-reference rows, unrelated); views /claim/ = none; enums = 12 total, none /claim/; procedures /claim/ = `shared.claim_outbox_events` only; sequences /claim|warrant/ = none; wty functions = `guard_warranty_record_coherence`, `guard_warranty_record_freeze`, `issue_warranty`. (5) Generic-table composition sweep: `grep "^CREATE TABLE "` filtered on approv|request|case|ticket|dispute|reimburs|adjud → `iam.approval_limits` (a limits table, not a request/adjudication workflow), `wo.additional_work_requests`, `wo.customer_approvals`, `quo.approval_decisions`, `quo.approval_evidence`, `svc.pricing_approval_policies` — all domain-pinned by FK, none polymorphic. (6) Read `shared.status_history`/`shared.status_evidence` DDL (20260718096000): app_runtime holds SELECT only, with the explicit line `-- Deliberately ABSENT: INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE for both roles on both tables.` (7) Read `ins_notes_crm_customer` (20260730090000): note INSERT is pinned to `entity_type = 'crm.business_partners'`. (8) Read `ins_document_links_scoped` (20260728090000). (9) Permission catalogue `supabase/seeds/04_iam_permission_catalog.sql` (100 rows): `grep "'wty\."` → exactly `wty.policy.manage`, `wty.warranty.issue`; `grep "claim"` → one prose comment on line 198 only. (10) `sal.financial_events` constraints and `sal.guard_financial_event_provenance()` read in full. (11) `iam.audit_records` CHECK constraints. (12) `shared.event_outbox` column constraints + grants (20260725090000). (13) Repo-wide `grep -rn "warranty claim|warranty_claim|claim_number|claimant|adjudicat" --include=*.sql --include=*.ts --include=*.json` — no application or schema hit. (14) `git log -- supabase/seeds/04_iam_permission_catalog.sql`. (15) P1-11 docs: p1-22-backend-contract §"What P1-22 owns" line 39, od-linkage line 16 (P1-OD-024), warranty-record-contract lines 34-38, warranty-eligibility-contract lines 11/30-31.
verdict.reasoning:
NOT REFUTED. The gap is real and a migration would genuinely be required.

CORE FACTS CONFIRMED, twice over (migration DDL text AND the deployed pgdelta catalog):

`wty` is exactly five tables. No claim table, view, materialized view, enum, sequence, or function exists in ANY schema across all 119 migrations. The only /claim/ relation in the deployed catalog is `auth.mfa_amr_claims`, a Supabase-managed auth artefact with no relation to warranty; the only /claim/ routine is `shared.claim_outbox_events(text, integer, interval)`, the outbox worker lease.

The entire trace of a claim is the string `'claimed_against'` in exactly two constraints:
  CONSTRAINT ck_warranty_records_status CHECK (status IN ('issued', 'active', 'expired', 'voided', 'claimed_against'))
  CONSTRAINT ck_warranty_status_history_to_status CHECK (to_status IN ('issued', 'active', 'expired', 'voided', 'claimed_against'))

`wty.warranty_status_history` is the whole available persistence surface, and its full column list is: id uuid, tenant_id uuid, company_id uuid, branch_id uuid, warranty_record_id uuid, from_status text NULL, to_status text NOT NULL, reason text NULL, correlation_id uuid NULL, actor_id uuid NOT NULL, occurred_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), seq bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY. There is no claimant, no claim amount, no decision, no approver, no claim number, no claim date distinct from occurred_at. Note `reason` is NULLABLE here (unlike `shared.status_history.reason`, which is NOT NULL) — so the schema does not even force a textual justification.

The transition itself IS mechanically possible: `GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON wty.warranty_records TO app_runtime` with `upd_warranty_records_scope`, and `wty.guard_warranty_record_freeze()` freezes only vehicle_id/work_order_id/delivery_record_id/policy_id/coverage_id/start_date/expiry_date/odometer_at_issue/odometer_limit — its comment says "identity + terms immutable; status may advance". `GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON wty.warranty_status_history TO app_runtime` with `tg_warranty_status_history_stamp` server-stamping actor_id/occurred_at. So "record that a warranty was claimed against" is buildable; "adjudicate a claim" is not.

EVERY GENERIC COMPOSITION SURFACE IS CLOSED — I checked each one specifically because that was the strongest refutation path:
  - `shared.status_history` + `shared.status_evidence` (which carries evidence_type/evidence_ref/note and would have been a natural claim-evidence home): app_runtime has SELECT only. The migration states it outright — "Deliberately ABSENT: INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE for both roles on both tables." UNUSABLE.
  - `shared.notes` (entity_type/entity_id polymorphic, body text): the only runtime INSERT path is `ins_notes_crm_customer`, whose WITH CHECK pins `entity_type = 'crm.business_partners'` AND requires an EXISTS against `crm.business_partners`. A note CANNOT be authored against a warranty record. UNUSABLE.
  - `iam.approval_limits`: an effective-dated limit table (limit_type/amount, gist no-overlap). There is no approval-REQUEST table anywhere; every approval object in the schema (`wo.customer_approvals`, `quo.approval_decisions`, `svc.pricing_approval_policies`) is FK-pinned to its own domain. UNUSABLE.
  - `sal.financial_events`: doubly closed. `ck_financial_events_event_type CHECK (event_type IN ('invoice_issued','receipt_recorded','payment_allocated','credit_note_issued','receipt_reversed','warranty_split_recorded'))` AND `ck_financial_events_source_type CHECK (source_type IN ('invoice','receipt','payment_allocation','credit_note','receipt_reversal'))`, plus `sal.guard_financial_event_provenance()` which has an IF/ELSIF branch per event_type and RAISEs 'no authorized % source % for event %' when none matches. Even if a claim row existed, no source_type value could name it. The archaeologist understated this — source_type is closed too.
  - `shared.document_links` is the ONE partial surface they missed: `ins_document_links_scoped` allows app_runtime INSERT under `iam.has_permission_in_scope('shared.document.manage', d.company_id, d.branch_id)` with `entity_type` constrained only by format `'^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$'`, so a claim FORM could legitimately be attached as a document to `entity_type = 'wty.warranty_records'`. That is an opaque file reference with no queryable claim state, no amount, no decision. It mitigates evidence capture, not adjudication.

THREE CORRECTIONS to the archaeologist's supporting reasoning (none change the verdict, but the write-up should not assert them as schema blocks):
  1. "no claim audit action" — `iam.audit_records.action` is constrained ONLY by `ck_audit_records_action_not_blank CHECK (btrim(action) <> '')`. Audit actions are free text, application-defined throughout this codebase. This is not a closed vocabulary and is not evidence of a gap.
  2. Outbox event types are NOT schema-constrained either: `ck_event_outbox_event_type_format CHECK (event_type ~ '^[a-z][a-z0-9_.-]{1,62}$')`. `warranty-claim.status.changed` (29 chars) is publishable today — app_runtime holds `GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON shared.event_outbox` with `ins_event_outbox_producer` since migration 20260725090000. The registry in `src/server/events/envelope.ts` is a TypeScript array, not DDL.
  3. A permission code is NOT migration-gated: codes live in `supabase/seeds/04_iam_permission_catalog.sql`, and backend phases have added them there — `69d749e feat(p1-20): seed the commercial read permissions`, `08544ca feat(p1-21): expose the inventory API surface and register its catalogs`. So "`wty.claim.*` does not exist" is true today but is a seed edit, not a schema change. (It is also worth noting there is no `wty.warranty.read` or `wty.warranty.view` code at all — wty RLS is scope-only, with no permission predicate on any of the five tables.)

ONE ADDITIONAL FINDING THAT STRENGTHENS THE VERDICT, not in the original claim: the financial half of warranty IS modelled — `sal.invoice_line_amounts.warranty_pay_amount numeric(18,4) NOT NULL` under `ck_invoice_line_amounts_payer_split CHECK (customer_pay_amount + warranty_pay_amount = gross_amount)` (FR-WTY-004), projected by the `warranty_split_recorded` event bound to `Σ la.warranty_pay_amount` on an issued invoice. But `sal.invoice_line_amounts` has NO foreign key to `wty.warranty_records`, `wty.warranty_policies`, or `wty.warranty_coverage`. The schema can say "the warranty pays 300.0000 of this line" and CANNOT say WHICH warranty. So even the money side cannot be reconciled to a claim without new DDL.

ALSO WORTH CARRYING FORWARD (adjacent, not part of this claim): there is no status-transition-legality guard on `wty.warranty_records` at all — no `wty.transition_warranty_status` function exists, and nothing prevents `'voided' -> 'claimed_against'` or `'expired' -> 'active'`. Transition legality is entirely a P1-22 backend responsibility, unlike the DB-enforced graphs in `wo`/`apt`.

FINALLY, THE DDL-VS-PROSE DIVERGENCE, which should be raised as a finding in the archaeology record: `docs/phase-1/phase-1-11/phase-1-11-warranty-record-contract.md` lines 37-38 assert "the `…claimed_against` status is prepared so a later claim links to the record without schema change." The deployed DDL contradicts that. `'claimed_against'` is a status token; there is no claim entity for it to link TO. Per the P1-21 wave-1 rule, the DDL is authoritative and the handoff prose is wrong. Combined with `phase-1-11-p1-22-backend-contract.md` §"What P1-22 owns" line 39 ("Full warranty **claim adjudication** (P1-OD-024) — only records + status history exist now"), P1-11 simultaneously assigns claim adjudication to P1-22 and ships no table to hold it, while `docs/phase-1/phase-1-11/phase-1-11-od-linkage.md` line 16 marks P1-OD-024 "Held / deferred".

VERDICT: submit/adjudicate/approve/reject-a-warranty-claim must be declared OUT OF SCOPE for P1-22 and carried as an accepted limitation in the manner of P1-21 D-04. What P1-22 CAN legitimately build without a migration: (a) transition `wty.warranty_records.status` to `'claimed_against'` with a `wty.warranty_status_history` row carrying `reason` and `correlation_id`, under a new seed-added permission code, with transition legality enforced in application code; (b) attach a claim form via `shared.document_links` with `entity_type = 'wty.warranty_records'` under `shared.document.manage`; (c) publish a `warranty-claim.status.changed` outbox event. What it CANNOT build: any persisted claimant, claim amount, adjudication decision, approver, or claim number. Building a partial claim workflow on `reason` text would be inventing persistence.

reports.lens: Audit action catalogue, outbox/event envelope contract, error catalogue and code grammar, operation registry shape, route grammar, and module conventions — as deployed at `feature/p1-22-billing-payment-delivery-warranty-backend` = `d9a2c1dc8d09e8fe2b3cf9ca8a2d4a6c905756de` (119 migrations, no 120, working tree clean).
reports.summary: The platform enforces four closed catalogues in TypeScript, each with its own gate, and P1-22 has ZERO entries in three of them. The audit-action catalogue is `AUDIT_ACTIONS` in `src/server/auth/audit-actions.ts` (138 entries; codes `<schema>.<entity>.<verb_snake_case>`, schema-qualified `entityType`, an audit class that `defineOperation()` cross-checks) — it contains no `sal.` or `wty.` entry at all. The event catalogue is `EVENT_CATALOG` in `src/server/events/envelope.ts` (42 entries) and its most load-bearing convention is that **`eventType` carries NO version suffix**: `schema_version` is its own `integer NOT NULL` column on `shared.event_outbox`, the catalog supplies `schemaVersion` (the caller cannot), and `tests/foundation/p1-15-catalogs.test.ts` asserts `expect(entry.eventType).not.toMatch(/\.v\d+$/)` for every entry. The P1-22 plan name `billing.invoice-issued.v1` is therefore unshippable on three counts at once: the `.v1` suffix, the unregistered name, and the module owner (`buildEventEnvelope` throws unless `producer.split('.')[0] === entry.owner`, and no `billing` owner exists). The error catalogue is `ERROR_CODES`/`DEFINITIONS` in `src/server/errors/catalog.ts` (28 codes, grammar `ERR-<AREA>-<NNN>`, closed `owner` and `class` unions, and a `SafeDetails` shape that is the only thing that can reach a caller). The operation registry is `defineOperation()` in `src/server/auth/operation-registry.ts`, whose `PATH_PATTERN = /^(?:\/(?:[a-z0-9-]+|\{[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*\}))+$/` **structurally rejects colon-style action routes**: `POST /invoices/{id}:issue` cannot be registered, and the repo uses noun/sub-resource routes throughout (`/quotations/{quotationId}/issue`, `/receptions/{receptionId}/approve`, `/stock-reservations/{reservationId}/release`, `/opening-inventory-batches/{batchId}/approval`, `/work-orders/{workOrderId}/closure`). Separately and critically, `sal.financial_events` is a DATABASE ledger with its own closed six-value `event_type` vocabulary and is NOT the outbox — conflating the two would produce an event name the CHECK constraint rejects. Finally, `sal.` and `wty.` are absent from BOTH derived-evidence hooks in `scripts/check-operation-test-coverage.mjs`, which is the exact defect that made the P1-20 gate vacuous for thirteen operations.

findings.fact: The audit-action catalogue is a frozen TypeScript array of 138 entries; a code not present here cannot be declared by any operation, because `defineOperation()` calls `auditActionViolation()` at module-load time and throws. There are exactly ZERO `sal.`, `wty.` or `rpt.` entries.
findings.evidence: `export const AUDIT_ACTIONS: readonly AuditActionDefinition[] = Object.freeze([...])` with `{ code, class, entityType, description }` per entry; `grep -cE "^    code: '" = 138`; `grep -cE "code: '(sal|wty|rpt)\." = 0`. Enforcement in operation-registry.ts: `const catalogViolation = auditActionViolation(declaration.id, auditClass, declaration.auditAction); if (catalogViolation) { throw new OperationRegistrationError(catalogViolation); }`
findings.consequence: Every P1-22 audited operation must first append a new entry to `AUDIT_ACTIONS`. No `sal.*`/`wty.*` audit code may be invented at a call site; the last block in the file is `// ---- Phase 1-21 — inventory ----`, so P1-22 appends a `// ---- Phase 1-22 — billing, payment, delivery, warranty ----` block in the same style.

findings.fact: Audit action codes are permanent and follow `<db-schema>.<entity>.<verb_in_snake_case>`; `entityType` must be a schema-qualified `schema.table` (underscores only, exactly one dot); `class` is one of five values and MUST equal the operation's declared `auditClass`.
findings.evidence: Existing exemplars: `{ code: 'inv.opening_batch.approved', class: 'approval', entityType: 'inv.opening_inventory_batch' }`, `{ code: 'inv.external_purchase.recorded', class: 'financial', entityType: 'inv.external_purchase_part' }`, `{ code: 'quo.quotation_revision.issued', class: 'approval', ... }`. Mismatch message: "declares audit class \"${auditClass}\" for action \"${auditAction}\", but the catalog classifies that action as \"${action.class}\"". Test: `it('names a schema-qualified entity type on every action', ...) expect(action.entityType).toMatch(SCHEMA_QUALIFIED)`. File header: "An audit action code is written into an append-only, hash-chained table. It can never be renamed".
findings.consequence: P1-22 codes take the form `sal.invoice.issued`, `sal.receipt.recorded`, `sal.payment.allocated`, `sal.credit_note.approved`, `sal.receipt_reversal.approved`, `sal.delivery.completed`, `wty.warranty.issued` — with `entityType` `sal.invoices`, `sal.receipts`, `sal.payment_allocations`, `sal.credit_notes`, `sal.receipt_reversals`, `sal.delivery_records`, `wty.warranty_records`. Money-moving commands are class `financial`; dual-control approvals are class `approval` (P1-21 precedent: `inv.external_purchase.recorded` is `financial` purely because it carries a cost figure).

findings.fact: The DATABASE places no vocabulary constraint on the audit action at all — it only requires non-blank text. The controlled vocabulary is therefore entirely an application-side control, and it is the only one.
findings.evidence: supabase/migrations/20260718095000_iam_audit_subsystem.sql: `action text NOT NULL, entity_type text NOT NULL,` … `CONSTRAINT ck_audit_records_actor_kind CHECK (actor_kind IN ('user', 'system', 'service')), CONSTRAINT ck_audit_records_action_not_blank CHECK (btrim(action) <> ''), CONSTRAINT ck_audit_records_entity_type_not_blank CHECK (btrim(entity_type) <> '')`
findings.consequence: A misspelled P1-22 action would be accepted by PostgreSQL and land in an append-only hash-chained table that can never be corrected. The only thing standing between a typo and permanent corruption is `AUDIT_ACTIONS` plus `scripts/check-authorization-coverage.mjs`, so both must be extended in the same commit as the routes.

findings.fact: Audit records are written by `appendAudit()` inside the business transaction via the sole DB writer `iam.audit_append`; tenant, actor, and correlation come from the request context and are not caller-supplied. Detail entries are re-shaped to `{field, old, new, class}` before they reach the function.
findings.identifier: src/server/audit/audit.ts — `appendAudit()`, `auditForOperation()`, `toDetailEnvelope()`, `AUDIT_CLASSIFICATIONS`; DB `iam.audit_append(p_tenant, p_actor, p_actor_kind, p_action, p_entity_type, p_entity_id, p_company, p_branch, p_correlation, p_request_ref, p_details jsonb)`
findings.evidence: `await requireCapability(db, 'audit.append');` then `SELECT iam.audit_append(p_tenant => $1, p_actor => $2, ...)` with `db.context.principal.tenantId`, `db.context.principal.userId`, `db.context.correlationId`, `input.requestRef ?? db.context.operation`. `export const AUDIT_CLASSIFICATIONS = ['public', 'internal', 'restricted', 'secret'] as const;` mirrors `ck_audit_record_details_class`. P1-21 call site: `await appendAudit(db, { action: 'inv.stock.reserved', entityType: 'inv.stock_reservation', entityId: reservation.id, companyId, branchId, requestRef: 'inv.stock-reservation-create', details: [...] });`
findings.consequence: P1-22 services call `appendAudit(db, {...})` inside the same transaction as the `sal.*`/`wty.*` primitive, with `requestRef` set to the operation id.

findings.fact: Sixteen `sal` columns are classified `restricted` in the committed classification registry; every one of them is a money amount or a signed-evidence document reference. An audit detail carrying any of those values must be classified `restricted`, which `iam.audit_mask` collapses to a fixed marker.
findings.identifier: docs/database/sal-wty-rpt-personal-data-classification.json (427 sal/wty/rpt columns: 411 `internal`, 16 `restricted`); guarded by `scripts/check-sal-wty-rpt-classification.mjs` / `npm run validate:sal-wty-rpt-classification`
findings.evidence: restricted set = `sal.invoice_amounts.net_total|tax_total|gross_total`, `sal.invoice_line_amounts.unit_price|net_amount|tax_amount|gross_amount|customer_pay_amount|warranty_pay_amount`, `sal.receipts.amount`, `sal.payment_allocations.amount`, `sal.credit_notes.amount`, `sal.receipt_reversals.amount`, `sal.financial_events.amount`, `sal.authorized_receivers.identity_evidence_document_version_id`, `sal.delivery_signatures.signature_document_version_id`. `allowedClassifications: ['public','internal','restricted','secret']`. The guard also FAILS when "a column is marked both `restricted` and `searchable`".
findings.consequence: P1-22 audit details that name an amount use `classification: 'restricted'` (P1-21 used `'internal'` for quantities, correct there because `inv` carries no amount). Ids, statuses and references stay `'internal'`. Classifying an amount as `internal` would publish an unmasked figure into the audit trail.

findings.fact: The outbox envelope IS the `shared.event_outbox` row — there is no second serialization. Column-level CHECK constraints are reproduced verbatim in TypeScript so a bad envelope fails before SQL.
findings.evidence: DDL: `event_key text NOT NULL, event_type text NOT NULL, aggregate_type text NOT NULL, aggregate_id uuid NOT NULL, schema_version integer NOT NULL, aggregate_version bigint NOT NULL, producer text NOT NULL, ... CONSTRAINT uq_event_outbox_event_key UNIQUE (tenant_id, event_key), CONSTRAINT ck_event_outbox_event_key CHECK (btrim(event_key) <> '' AND char_length(event_key) <= 255), CONSTRAINT ck_event_outbox_event_type_format CHECK (event_type ~ '^[a-z][a-z0-9_.-]{1,62}$'), CONSTRAINT ck_event_outbox_schema_version CHECK (schema_version >= 1), CONSTRAINT ck_event_outbox_aggregate_version CHECK (aggregate_version >= 1), CONSTRAINT ck_event_outbox_producer_format CHECK (producer ~ '^[a-z][a-z0-9_.-]{1,62}$'), CONSTRAINT ck_event_outbox_payload_object CHECK (jsonb_typeof(payload) = 'object')`. TS: `const EVENT_TYPE = /^[a-z][a-z0-9_.-]{1,62}$/;` and `const EVENT_KEY_MAX = 255;`
findings.consequence: `aggregateId` must be a UUID, `aggregateVersion` an integer ≥ 1 (P1-21 uses a literal `1` for append-only ledger rows with the comment "Claiming anything else would imply a mutable ledger"), `payload` a JSON object, `eventKey` ≤ 255 characters.

findings.fact: THE DECISIVE NAMING FACT: `eventType` carries no version segment. `schemaVersion` is a separate envelope field sourced FROM THE CATALOG (never from the caller) and lands in its own `schema_version integer` column. Three separate phases explicitly rejected the `.v1` planning spelling, and a unit test enforces it across the whole catalogue.
findings.identifier: `EventCatalogEntry.schemaVersion`; `buildEventEnvelope()`; `shared.event_outbox.schema_version`; tests/foundation/p1-15-catalogs.test.ts `it('carries no version suffix in any wire name')`
findings.evidence: envelope.ts P1-15 block: "Names carry no version suffix. The planning text used `….v1`; the schema version is a separate column (`schema_version`) and duplicating it in the wire name would produce two ways to express the same fact." P1-20 block: "The `.v1` suffix is NOT used: every shipped name in this catalog is unsuffixed and carries its version in `schemaVersion`, which is also what `shared.event_outbox.schema_version` stores. Encoding the version twice, in two places that can disagree, is exactly the drift this registry exists to prevent." P1-21 block: "None of those names is expressible here: `event_type` carries no version segment because `schema_version` is its own column". Code: `return { ..., schemaVersion: entry.schemaVersion, aggregateType: entry.aggregateType, ... }` — both taken from `entry`, not `input`. Test: `expect(entry.eventType, `${entry.code} carries a version suffix`).not.toMatch(/\.v\d+$/); expect(entry.eventType).not.toContain('.v1');`
findings.consequence: The P1-22 plan's `billing.invoice-issued.v1` MUST be transcribed to an unsuffixed name with `schemaVersion: 1`. The mapping from every planned `….v1` name to the shipped name must be recorded in the P1-22 archaeology document, exactly as P1-20 and P1-21 did.

findings.fact: The catalog's `owner` field is ENFORCED, not documentary: `buildEventEnvelope()` refuses publication unless the leading dotted segment of `producer` equals `owner`. Producers in the repo are uniformly `<owner>.<service-file-name>`.
findings.evidence: `const producerModule = input.producer.split('.')[0]; if (producerModule !== entry.owner) { throw new EventEnvelopeError(`Producer "${input.producer}" may not publish "${input.eventType}": the catalog assigns that event to module "${entry.owner}".`); }`. Live producers: `'inventory.inventory-stock-service'`, `'quotation.quotation-service'`, `'wo.work-order-service'`, `'service-catalog.service-catalog-write-service'`, `'pricing.price-list-service'`, `'tech.labor-session-service'`. The catalogue mixes short schema owners (`wo`, `tech`, `dia`, `qms`, `apt`, `rec`, `veh`, `crm`, `iam`, `shared`) with long module owners (`inventory`, `quotation`, `pricing`, `service-catalog`). EVT-TEC-001's comment: "buildEventEnvelope refuses a producer whose leading segment differs from the owner, so 'tech' here would have made Wave 5's own write path throw."
findings.consequence: P1-22 must pick its `owner` string ONCE and use it as the leading producer segment everywhere. Whatever is chosen, the catalog entry and every producer id must agree or the first write path throws at runtime rather than at build time.

findings.fact: `eventKey` is the tenant-unique publication idempotency key and the established convention is `<eventType>:<aggregateId>`. A duplicate key aborts the producing transaction and surfaces as `ERR-INT-001`, not as a silent dedupe.
findings.evidence: P1-21 call sites: `eventKey: `stock.reserved:${reservation.id}``, `eventKey: `stock.reservation.released:${after.id}``, `eventKey: `stock.movement.posted:${input.movementId}``. Publisher: `if (isSqlState(error, SQLSTATE.uniqueViolation)) { throw new AppFailure('ERR-INT-001', { message: `Event key "${envelope.eventKey}" was already published for this tenant` }); }` with the comment "Deduplication is the intended behaviour, but the violation aborts this transaction — so it is surfaced as a conflict rather than swallowed, and the caller decides."
findings.consequence: P1-22 keys the invoice-issued event on the invoice id, the receipt event on the receipt id, the allocation event on the allocation id, and so on. Keying on anything a retry can vary (a timestamp, a request id) would let a retry emit a second event for the same fact.

findings.fact: `publishEvent()` writes into the caller's transaction and requires a runtime capability already granted by an existing migration; correlation is forced from the request context.
findings.evidence: `await requireCapability(db, 'outbox.publish');` then `INSERT INTO shared.event_outbox (tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, event_key, event_type, aggregate_type, aggregate_id, schema_version, aggregate_version, producer, occurred_at, correlation_id, causation_id, payload, headers, created_by) VALUES (...)` with `correlationId: db.context.correlationId`. Migration: `GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON shared.event_outbox TO app_runtime;`, `CREATE POLICY ins_event_outbox_producer ON shared.event_outbox`, `GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION iam.audit_append(uuid, uuid, text, text, text, uuid, uuid, uuid, uuid, text, jsonb) TO app_runtime;`
findings.consequence: P1-22 needs no new migration to audit or to publish. Both capabilities already exist for `app_runtime`, tenant-scoped, INSERT-only — write feasibility for the audit/outbox lens is proven.

findings.fact: `sal.financial_events` is a DATABASE ledger with its own closed six-value vocabulary and is NOT the outbox. Its rows are written by the protected `sal.*` primitives themselves, and five DEFERRABLE constraint triggers make the matching row a commit-time obligation.
findings.evidence: `CONSTRAINT ck_financial_events_event_type CHECK (event_type IN ('invoice_issued', 'receipt_recorded', 'payment_allocated', 'credit_note_issued', 'receipt_reversed', 'warranty_split_recorded'))`, `CONSTRAINT ck_financial_events_source_type CHECK (source_type IN ('invoice', 'receipt', 'payment_allocation', 'credit_note', 'receipt_reversal'))`, `CONSTRAINT uq_financial_events_source UNIQUE (tenant_id, source_type, source_id, event_type)`. Table comment: "The future accounting integration point (Figure 4.29) — NOT a general ledger: no debit/credit/account columns. Exactly one event per financial command (completeness constraint triggers); provenance-guarded; single-use per (source, event_type)." Grants: `GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON sal.financial_events TO app_runtime;` — no UPDATE, no DELETE.
findings.consequence: P1-22 must keep two vocabularies strictly apart: the DB `event_type` (snake_case, six values, written by the DB primitive) and the outbox `eventType` (dotted, catalog-registered, written by `publishEvent`). Inserting an outbox-style name into `sal.financial_events` violates a CHECK; registering a snake_case DB name in `EVENT_CATALOG` would break the dotted convention. The application must never insert into `sal.financial_events` itself — the primitives do it, and doing it twice trips `uq_financial_events_source`.

findings.fact: Inserting a financial event requires `iam.has_permission('sal.finance.view')` INSIDE the RLS policy, so every caller of `sal.issue_invoice`, `sal.record_receipt`, `sal.allocate_receipt`, `sal.approve_credit_note` and `sal.approve_receipt_reversal` must hold that permission in addition to the command permission.
findings.identifier: `POLICY ins_financial_events_gated ON sal.financial_events`, `POLICY sel_financial_events_gated ON sal.financial_events`
findings.evidence: `CREATE POLICY ins_financial_events_gated ON sal.financial_events FOR INSERT TO app_runtime WITH CHECK (tenant_id = iam.current_tenant_id() AND iam.has_permission('sal.finance.view') AND (iam.allowed_company_ids() IS NULL OR company_id = ANY (iam.allowed_company_ids())) AND (iam.allowed_branch_ids() IS NULL OR branch_id = ANY (iam.allowed_branch_ids())))`
findings.consequence: Every P1-22 money-moving operation declares BOTH its command permission and `sal.finance.view` in `permissions: [...]`. `defineOperation()` treats the array as a conjunction ("ALL must pass (conjunction) — an operation needing \"any of\" is two operations"). Omitting `sal.finance.view` produces a 42501/RLS failure deep inside a protected function rather than a clean 403.

findings.fact: The error catalogue is a closed 28-code registry; `problemFor()` can only render a registered code, `AppFailure` can only be constructed with one, and both the `owner` and `class` fields are closed string unions.
findings.evidence: `export const ERROR_CODES = ['ERR-REQ-001','ERR-REQ-002','ERR-VAL-001','ERR-PAG-001','ERR-IAM-001','ERR-IAM-002','ERR-TEN-001','ERR-CTX-001','ERR-RES-001','ERR-RES-002','ERR-DEP-001','ERR-INT-001','ERR-INT-002','ERR-INT-003','ERR-CON-001','ERR-CON-002','ERR-RTE-001','ERR-STB-001','ERR-DOC-001','ERR-NTF-001','ERR-EXP-001','ERR-TRN-001','ERR-WO-001','ERR-WO-002','ERR-TECH-001','ERR-DIA-001','ERR-QMS-001','ERR-SYS-001'] as const;` with `readonly owner: 'request'|'validation'|'authorization'|'entitlement'|'context'|'resource'|'idempotency'|'concurrency'|'throttling'|'stub'|'attachment'|'notification'|'export'|'transition'|'platform'` and `type ErrorClass = 'client'|'security'|'conflict'|'throttle'|'server'`. File header rule 1: "A code exists here or it does not exist."
findings.consequence: Code grammar is `ERR-<AREA>-<NNN>` where AREA is 2–4 upper-case letters (`WO` is two, `TECH` is four) and NNN is zero-padded per area from 001. Any new P1-22 code must also pick an existing `owner` from the closed union — `'transition'` is the precedent for domain-refusal codes (`ERR-TRN-001`, `ERR-WO-001`, `ERR-DIA-001`, `ERR-QMS-001`).

findings.fact: `SafeDetails` is the ONLY structure that can reach a caller, and it has exactly four optional fields. No domain-specific number, amount, id, or state name can be returned in a problem document.
findings.evidence: `export interface SafeDetails { readonly violations?: readonly FieldViolation[]; readonly retryAfterSeconds?: number; readonly contract?: string; readonly requiredPermissions?: readonly string[]; }` and `problemFor()` spreads only `details.violations`, `details.retryAfterSeconds`, `details.contract`, `details.requiredPermissions`. `message` is documented "developer-facing and goes to logs and error monitoring".
findings.consequence: A P1-22 refusal such as "allocation of 500.0000 exceeds the invoice open receivable of 120.0000" can only appear in the log `message`, never in the response body. If P1-22 wants the caller to see the bound, it needs a read endpoint over `sal.invoice_open_receivable`, not a richer error.

findings.fact: P1-20 and P1-21 added ZERO error codes between them; P1-19 added five. Adding a code is optional, and the precedent is to add one only when an existing code would mislead about the caller's remedy.
findings.evidence: `ERR-WO-001` description: "Deliberately NOT ERR-TRN-001: the ready_to_close→closed edge exists in the graph and the aggregate is in a legal starting state, so this is not a graph refusal. The caller must clear a condition, not re-read a version or pick a different target." P1-21's inventory refusals reuse `ERR-TRN-001` — the stock-reservation route comment reads "the loser sees `ERR-TRN-001` rather than a partially applied reservation".
findings.consequence: P1-22 should first try to express each refusal with `ERR-TRN-001`, `ERR-CON-001`/`ERR-CON-002`, `ERR-INT-001`/`ERR-INT-002`, `ERR-RES-001`, `ERR-IAM-001`, `ERR-VAL-001`. A new code is justified only where the remedy differs — e.g. a bounds refusal (allocation > open receivable) versus a state refusal (invoice not issued).

findings.fact: The operation registry declaration is a single frozen shape whose sixteen fields carry all the security metadata. It rejects an unguarded, mis-classified, duplicate-id or duplicate-route declaration at MODULE LOAD.
findings.evidence: Fields: `id, module, method, path, summary, permissions?, public?, publicReason?, scope?, auditClass?, auditAction?, featureFlag?, idempotent?, versionGuarded?, rateLimitPolicy?, cacheCategory?`. `const ID_PATTERN = /^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9-]*)+$/;` Defaults on registration: `scope: declaration.scope ?? 'tenant'`, `auditClass: declaration.auditClass ?? 'none'`. Guards: "declares no permission codes", "is public and also declares permissions. Choose one.", "is audit class \"${auditClass}\" but declares no auditAction (FR-AUD-001)", "declares an auditAction but audit class \"none\"", "Route ${routeKey} is already claimed by operation \"${existing}\"."
findings.consequence: Every P1-22 route declares: dotted lower-case-kebab id, long-form module name, method, path, summary, the full permission conjunction, `scope: 'branch'` (all `sal`/`wty` business tables are branch-scoped), `auditClass` + `auditAction`, `idempotent: true` on commands, `rateLimitPolicy`, `cacheCategory`.

findings.fact: THE ROUTE GRAMMAR FACT: colon-style action routes are structurally impossible. `PATH_PATTERN` accepts only lower-case-kebab literal segments and `{camelCase}` parameter segments, so a segment containing `:` matches neither alternative.
findings.evidence: Registration failure message: "has a path that is not a lower-case API path: ${declaration.path}". Directory mapping: `return `src/app/api/v1${declaredPath.replace(/\{([a-zA-Z0-9_]+)\}/g, '[$1]')}`;` — an OpenAPI `{param}` becomes a Next.js `[param]` directory and a `:` has no directory spelling. P1-21 states the decision explicitly in its own coverage-manifest note for `inv.stock-reservation-release`: "a subresource and not a colon-action, because the registry PATH_PATTERN accepts only lower-case literals and {camelCase} parameters".
findings.consequence: `POST /invoices/{id}:issue` cannot be registered. P1-22 uses sub-resource routes. The 169 committed templates give the exact idiom per verb class: imperative (`/quotations/{quotationId}/issue`, `/receptions/{receptionId}/approve`, `/stock-reservations/{reservationId}/release`, `/rework-links/{reworkLinkId}/sign-off`) and nominalised (`/opening-inventory-batches/{batchId}/approval`, `/work-orders/{workOrderId}/closure`, `/price-lists/{priceListId}/versions/{versionId}/publication`, `/template-versions/{versionId}/retirement`). The nominalised form is the newer P1-20/P1-21 preference.

findings.fact: Every route template is duplicated as a compile-time literal in a frozen 169-entry array, because the idempotency fingerprint may only hash a template this platform actually serves. A route added without updating the array fails the build.
findings.evidence: "`find` returns an element of THIS array — a compile-time constant with no relationship to any route module — so the hashed value provably stops deriving from the caller's input." and "`tests/foundation/route-templates.test.ts` reconciles this list against the route modules on disk and fails on any difference in either direction. A template added without updating this file fails the build rather than failing a request." `export function internRouteTemplate(path: string): string | null { return ROUTE_TEMPLATES.find((template) => template === path) ?? null; }`
findings.consequence: Each new P1-22 path must be appended to `ROUTE_TEMPLATES` in sorted position in the same commit. Omitting it makes every idempotent P1-22 command refuse to fingerprint.

findings.fact: Idempotency is header-driven with a fixed 8–200 character key, and the operation id must survive translation into the database's underscored operation code.
findings.evidence: `export function toOperationCode(operationId: string): string { const code = operationId.replace(/[.-]/g, '_').toLowerCase(); if (!OPERATION_PATTERN.test(code)) { throw new Error(...); } return code; }` backed by `shared.idempotency_keys` `operation ~ '^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,62}$'` and `char_length(idempotency_key) BETWEEN 8 AND 200`. The fingerprint binds method + registered template + resolved params + body + principal.
findings.consequence: A P1-22 operation id must be at most 63 characters after `.`/`-` → `_` translation (`sal.invoice-issue` → `sal_invoice_issue`). `idempotent: true` also creates a mandatory `idempotency` test-evidence obligation via `derivedRequirements()`, which applies to EVERY namespace, derived or not.

findings.fact: Module layout, import path, and layering are fixed and mechanically enforced: one public entry point per module, three layers, a memoised composition root.
findings.identifier: src/server/layering.ts — `ApplicationService`, `DomainService`, `composeModule()`; scripts/check-module-boundaries.mjs (`npm run validate:module-boundaries`); src/modules/inventory/index.ts as the P1-21 exemplar
findings.evidence: `export const inventoryModule = composeModule({ module: 'inventory', create: () => { const repository = new InventoryRepository(); return { reads: new InventoryReadService(repository), stock: new InventoryStockService(repository), intake: new InventoryIntakeService(repository) }; } });` with the header "The ONLY legal import path for this module (ADR-001): `@/modules/inventory`. The boundary checker and the ESLint rule both reject `@/modules/inventory/<anything>`." Layering: "Application service … receives the transaction handle, calls domain services and repositories in order, publishes events, emits audit … Domain service — the rules. Pure decision-making over values it is given. It must not touch the database … Repository — the SQL, behind the context guard". Directory shape: `src/modules/<module>/{domain/,application/,data/,index.ts}`.
findings.consequence: P1-22 creates `src/modules/<module>/` with `domain/` (vocabularies, rule assertions, no DB), `application/` (services that call the `sal.*`/`wty.*` primitives, append audit, publish events), `data/` (one repository per schema), and `index.ts` (sole export surface + `composeModule`). Route handlers parse, call one application service, and return.

findings.fact: The operation `module` field and the operation `id` prefix are DIFFERENT vocabularies and are allowed to differ. 199 operations are registered across 14 module names.
findings.evidence: Live pairings: `module: 'inventory'` with `id: 'inv.…'`; `module: 'work-order'` with `id: 'wo.…'`; `module: 'shared-services'` with `id: 'shared.…'`; `module: 'service-catalog'` AND `module: 'pricing'` both with `id: 'svc.…'`; `module: 'vehicle'`/`veh.`; `module: 'quality'`/`qms.`; `module: 'diagnostics'`/`dia.`. Counts: iam 38, work-order 26, shared-services 21, vehicle 20, crm 18, inventory 14, quality 13, diagnostics 13, reception 12, technician 6, quotation 6, pricing 6, service-catalog 5, meta 1 = 199.
findings.consequence: P1-22 operation ids use the DB schema short codes `sal.` and `wty.` (matching the permission and audit-action catalogues), while `module` uses long-form kebab names. A single `sal` schema may legitimately be served by more than one module name, exactly as `svc` is served by both `service-catalog` and `pricing`.

findings.fact: The OpenAPI document is generated from the registry and re-checked by count, but the registry is only filled by a HAND-MAINTAINED import list in a test file — the documented trap that hid all twelve P1-18 operations.
findings.identifier: src/server/openapi/document.ts — `buildOpenApiDocument()`, `API_VERSION_PREFIX = '/api/v1'`; tests/openapi-contract.test.ts import block; scripts/check-openapi.mjs; docs/api/openapi.v1.json
findings.evidence: tests/openapi-contract.test.ts: "THIS LIST IS HAND-MAINTAINED, AND THAT IS ITS TRAP … a route missing here is missing from the published contract AND the test still passes, because both sides agree on the same incomplete registry. That is exactly how all twelve Phase 1-18 operations came to be absent from `docs/api/openapi.v1.json` while every gate read green. The arithmetic that catches it is external: `check-authorization-coverage.mjs` counts registered operations, `check-openapi.mjs` counts published ones, and the two numbers must be equal." Per-operation extensions emitted: `'x-required-permissions'`, `'x-scope'`, `'x-audit-class'`, optional `'x-feature-flag'`, `'x-rate-limit-policy'`, `'x-cache-category'`.
findings.consequence: Every P1-22 route needs an `import '@/app/api/v1/…/route';` line in tests/openapi-contract.test.ts and a regenerated `docs/api/openapi.v1.json` via `UPDATE_OPENAPI=1 npx vitest run tests/openapi-contract.test.ts`.

findings.fact: Three exhaustive expected-value lists in one unit test pin the whole error catalogue, the whole audit-action catalogue, and the whole event catalogue by exact equality in both directions.
findings.evidence: `expect(ascending(ERROR_CODES)).toEqual(EXPECTED_ERROR_CODES);`, `expect(ascending(AUDIT_ACTIONS.map((action) => action.code))).toEqual(EXPECTED_AUDIT_ACTIONS);`, `expect(ascending(EVENT_CATALOG.map((entry) => entry.eventType))).toEqual(EXPECTED_EVENT_TYPES);` plus `it('allocates every wire name and every EVT- code exactly once')` and `it('never registers a code twice')`.
findings.consequence: Adding one P1-22 audit action or event without extending the matching expected list fails the unit suite immediately — a good failure, but it must be planned into the same commit.

findings.fact: The rate-limit and cache vocabularies are closed catalogues; a declaration referencing an unknown policy throws at request time.
findings.identifier: src/server/http/rate-limit.ts — `RATE_LIMIT_POLICIES` (`auth-adjacent` 10 keyBy op+ip securityRelevant, `expensive-read` 30 op+tenant+user, `standard-command` 120 op+tenant+user, `public-probe` 120 op+ip, `low-risk-metadata` 600 op+tenant); src/server/cache/eligibility.ts — `CACHE_CATEGORIES` incl. `'never'`; `policyFor()` in route-handler.ts
findings.evidence: `if (name && !declared) { throw new Error(`Operation ${operation.id} references unknown rate-limit policy "${name}"`); }`. P1-21 exemplar declaration: `rateLimitPolicy: 'standard-command', cacheCategory: 'never'`.
findings.consequence: P1-22 commands use `rateLimitPolicy: 'standard-command'`, reads `'expensive-read'` or `'low-risk-metadata'`, and every financial route uses `cacheCategory: 'never'` — a receivable balance must never be served from cache.

findings.fact: Authorization is re-evaluated against the row's own scope INSIDE the transaction for id-addressed operations. The `sal` RLS policies use the scope-blind `iam.has_permission`, so the application-level scoped check is the only one that consults grant scope.
findings.evidence: `function requiresScopedEvaluation(scope, target) { if (scope === 'tenant') return false; return target.companyId !== undefined || target.branchId !== undefined; }`; the evaluation branch is `scoped ? 'SELECT iam.has_permission_in_scope($1, $2, $3, $4)' : 'SELECT iam.has_permission($1)'`. Route-handler comment: "With an empty target `requiresScopedEvaluation` returns false whatever the declared scope is, and the check falls back to `iam.has_permission`, which does not consult grant scope at all. RLS cannot make up the difference: `app.branch_ids` is the union of every active grant regardless of which permission it carries." The sal policies call `iam.has_permission('sal.finance.view')`, never `iam.has_permission_in_scope`.
findings.consequence: Every P1-22 operation addressed by `{invoiceId}`, `{receiptId}`, `{deliveryId}` or `{warrantyId}` must call `authorizeScope({ companyId, branchId })` with the LOCKED row's own company and branch before writing, and must declare the `isolation` evidence kind. Declaring `scope: 'branch'` alone is not enough.

findings.fact: Security-event candidates are emitted separately from audit records and never fail the request; the DB accepts any non-blank event type with one of three severities.
findings.evidence: `await recordSecurityEvent(db, { eventType: 'authorization.denied', severity: 'warning', detail: `Operation ${operation.id} denied` });` and "an audit record is evidence of a state change that is happening, and losing it corrupts the record; a security event describes an action that was refused, and the refusal already happened." `SecurityEventInput.detail` is documented "Operator-facing detail. Must not contain caller-supplied free text."
findings.consequence: A P1-22 dual-control violation (maker == approver, refused by `sal.guard_dual_control_approval`) or an out-of-scope approval attempt is a security-event candidate alongside the returned error, using the established dotted `authorization.denied` spelling, with no caller-supplied text in `detail`.

findings.fact: Both DB numbering runs P1-22 needs are already recognised by the application sequence allow-list; no other sal/wty document carries a number at all.
findings.identifier: src/modules/shared-services/domain/sequence-registry.ts — `SEQUENCE_DEFINITIONS` (codes `appointment, business_partner, invoice, quotation, receipt, reception_visit, vehicle, work_order`), `findSequenceDefinition()`; `sal.invoices.invoice_number`, `sal.receipts.receipt_number`
findings.evidence: `{ code: 'invoice', targetTable: 'sal.invoices', targetColumn: 'invoice_number', introducedIn: 'P1-11', description: 'Invoice number as printed on the issued document.' }` and `{ code: 'receipt', targetTable: 'sal.receipts', targetColumn: 'receipt_number', introducedIn: 'P1-11' }`. DB: `SELECT display_number INTO v_number FROM shared.next_display_number(v_seq_code, v_inv.company_id, v_inv.branch_id);` in `sal.issue_invoice`; `shared.next_display_number('receipt', p_company_id, p_branch_id)` in `sal.record_receipt`. Invoice uniqueness: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_invoices_number ON sal.invoices (tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, invoice_number) WHERE invoice_number IS NOT NULL;` and `CONSTRAINT ck_invoices_number_iff_issued CHECK ((invoice_number IS NULL AND issued_at IS NULL) = (status IN ('draft', 'void_before_issue')))`.
findings.consequence: P1-22 invents no numbering scheme. Numbers come from the DB primitives; the backend never allocates one itself.

gaps.assumed: A billing-specific error code such as `ERR-SAL-001` is available for financial refusals, and the response can tell the caller what bound was exceeded.
gaps.reality: ABSENT. `ERROR_CODES` has 28 entries and no `ERR-SAL-*`, `ERR-WTY-*`, `ERR-BIL-*` or `ERR-DLV-*`. `ErrorDefinition.owner` is a CLOSED union with no financial/billing member. `SafeDetails` has exactly four fields (`violations`, `retryAfterSeconds`, `contract`, `requiredPermissions`) — none can carry an amount, an invoice id, or an open-receivable bound. Note also that P1-20 and P1-21 each shipped zero new codes, so adding none is an acceptable outcome.
gaps.mitigation: Prefer existing codes: `ERR-TRN-001` for "invoice is not in a state that may be issued / receipt already reversed", `ERR-INT-001/002` for idempotency, `ERR-CON-001/002` for version, `ERR-RES-001` for not-found-or-out-of-scope, `ERR-IAM-001` for denial. If a bounds refusal genuinely needs its own code because the caller's remedy differs from a state refusal, add e.g. `ERR-SAL-001` with `owner: 'transition'` or `'validation'`, extend `EXPECTED_ERROR_CODES`, and accept that the response can carry no figure.

gaps.assumed: Reading an invoice, a receipt, a delivery or a warranty has its own read permission, and credit-note approval has its own approval permission.
gaps.reality: Partially ABSENT. The catalogue has exactly 10 `sal` and 2 `wty` codes: `sal.invoice.manage`, `sal.invoice.issue`, `sal.payment.record`, `sal.payment.allocate`, `sal.credit.manage`, `sal.reversal.approve`, `sal.finance.view`, `sal.delivery.manage`, `sal.delivery.complete`, `sal.delivery.view`, `wty.policy.manage`, `wty.warranty.issue` (100 permissions platform-wide). There is NO `sal.invoice.read`, no `sal.payment.read`, no `wty.warranty.read`, and no `sal.credit.approve` — credit-note creation and approval share `sal.credit.manage`, asymmetric with `sal.reversal.approve`.
gaps.mitigation: Reuse rather than invent: `sal.finance.view` is the read gate for anything carrying an amount (it is the gate inside the RLS policy on `sal.financial_events` and the restricted amount tables), `sal.delivery.view` for signature/receiver evidence, `sal.invoice.manage` for draft-invoice reads. For credit-note approval declare the conjunction `['sal.credit.manage','sal.finance.view']` and rely on `sal.guard_dual_control_approval` for maker≠approver; record the asymmetry with `sal.reversal.approve` as an observation rather than minting a code.

gaps.assumed: Credit notes, deliveries and warranties carry human-facing numbers the backend allocates.
gaps.reality: ABSENT. Only `sal.invoices.invoice_number` and `sal.receipts.receipt_number` exist. `sal.credit_notes`, `sal.receipt_reversals`, `sal.delivery_records` and `wty.warranty_records` have NO number column, and `SEQUENCE_DEFINITIONS` registers only `invoice` and `receipt` for `sal`. Adding a column would require a migration P1-22 may not create.
gaps.mitigation: Expose the UUID `id` for these entities and no number. Do NOT synthesise a display number in the application — it would be a business fact the schema cannot store, and the standing no-fake-data policy forbids shipping one.

gaps.assumed: The application's reviewed sequence-code allow-list governs which numbering run an issued invoice draws from.
gaps.reality: It does not, on the issuing path. `sal.issue_invoice` reads the config itself — `SELECT sequence_code INTO v_seq_code FROM sal.invoice_numbering_configs WHERE tenant_id = ... AND status = 'active' AND deleted_at IS NULL; v_seq_code := COALESCE(v_seq_code, 'invoice'); SELECT display_number INTO v_number FROM shared.next_display_number(v_seq_code, ...)` — and `ck_invoice_numbering_configs_sequence_code CHECK (sequence_code ~ '^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,62}$')` constrains only the spelling. A config row naming an unregistered code allocates from a sequence the application registry never reviewed, which is exactly the failure `sequence-registry.ts` says it exists to prevent ("a caller that invents `invoice_2` would create a second numbering run for the same document type").
gaps.mitigation: Whatever P1-22 route creates or activates an `sal.invoice_numbering_configs` row must validate `sequence_code` against `findSequenceDefinition()` before writing and should refuse anything but `invoice`. The issuing path itself cannot be changed without a migration; record the residual.

gaps.assumed: An audited invoice lifecycle can name the states `partially_paid` and `paid`.
gaps.reality: Divergent between two protected tables. `ck_invoices_status CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'issued', 'credited', 'void_before_issue'))` — four values — but `ck_invoice_status_history_to_status CHECK (to_status IN ('draft', 'issued', 'partially_paid', 'paid', 'credited', 'void_before_issue'))` — six. `partially_paid` and `paid` can be written to the HISTORY but the invoice row can never hold them, so a history row claiming `paid` describes a state the aggregate cannot be in. `sal.allocate_receipt` writes no invoice history row at all; it updates only `sal.receipts.status` to `partially_allocated`/`allocated`.
gaps.mitigation: Treat `sal.invoices.status` as authoritative (DDL wins over prose) and derive paid-ness from `sal.invoice_open_receivable(invoice_id)` rather than from a status. Do not mint an audit action or event name for `paid` while the invoice table cannot express it, and raise the divergence as a finding either way.

gaps.assumed: An audit record can be attributed to a non-human actor kind of `service`, and a scheduled/worker billing producer can publish events.
gaps.reality: Both half-absent. The database allows three actor kinds — `ck_audit_records_actor_kind CHECK (actor_kind IN ('user', 'system', 'service'))` — but the TypeScript helper exposes only two: `readonly actorKind?: 'user' | 'system';`, defaulting via `input.actorKind ?? 'user'`. Separately, `publishEvent()` cannot be called without a `RequestContext` (it reads `db.context.correlationId`, `db.context.principal.tenantId`), which is the documented reason `EVT-NTF-001` is still `implementedIn: null` after P1-15.
gaps.mitigation: P1-22 uses `'user'` for request-driven commands. Any scheduled billing action (dunning, warranty expiry sweep) is a carried-forward obligation, not a build — there is no worker-side publication path and reserving an event name for a producer that does not exist is what the catalogue's own P1-21 comment calls "how a catalog fills with fiction".

gaps.assumed: Adding the routes is enough for them to appear in the published API contract.
gaps.reality: It is not. `tests/openapi-contract.test.ts` fills the registry from a hand-maintained `import '@/app/api/v1/…/route';` list and regenerates the document from that SAME incomplete registry — so a missing import passes the test while silently omitting the operation from `docs/api/openapi.v1.json`. The file documents this as the exact mechanism by which all twelve P1-18 operations went missing with every gate green.
gaps.mitigation: Add one import line per P1-22 route in the same commit, regenerate `docs/api/openapi.v1.json`, and verify the external arithmetic: registered-operation count from `npm run validate:authorization-coverage` must equal published-operation count from `npm run validate:openapi`.

gaps.assumed: Declaring `scope: 'branch'` is sufficient for branch isolation on id-addressed billing commands.
gaps.reality: It is not, and the `sal` RLS policies make it worse rather than better: they call the SCOPE-BLIND `iam.has_permission('sal.finance.view')`, and per P1-18-A-01 `iam.allowed_branch_ids()` is the union of every active grant regardless of which permission carries it. `requiresScopedEvaluation()` returns false for an empty `AuthorizationTarget` whatever the declared scope, so the pre-handler check degrades to `iam.has_permission`.
gaps.mitigation: Every id-addressed P1-22 command must call `authorizeScope({ companyId, branchId })` with the LOCKED row's own company and branch inside the transaction, so the evaluation becomes `iam.has_permission_in_scope`, and must carry the `isolation` evidence kind. The P1-21 route comment is the template: "the location is the scope anchor and its company/branch are the authorizationTarget".

gaps.assumed: The P1-22 plan's event names carry a version suffix — `billing.invoice-issued.v1`, and per the P1-11 handoff `invoice.issued.v1`, `payment.recorded.v1`, `payment.allocated.v1`, `credit-note.issued.v1`, `receipt.reversed.v1`, `delivery.completed.v1`, `warranty.issued.v1`, `warranty-claim.status.changed.v1`.
gaps.reality: Not expressible. `schemaVersion` is a separate envelope field and `shared.event_outbox.schema_version` a separate `integer NOT NULL` column; `tests/foundation/p1-15-catalogs.test.ts` asserts `expect(entry.eventType).not.toMatch(/\.v\d+$/)` over the WHOLE catalogue, so a single suffixed entry fails the unit suite. All 42 registered names are unsuffixed. Additionally none of the eight names exists in `EVENT_CATALOG`, and `buildEventEnvelope()` throws `Event type "X" is not in the event catalog. Register it before publishing.` for an unregistered name.
gaps.mitigation: Register unsuffixed names with `schemaVersion: 1` under new `EVT-SAL-*` / `EVT-WTY-*` codes (the P1-11 handoff already reserves `EVT-SAL-001` and `EVT-WTY-001`), extend `EXPECTED_EVENT_TYPES`, and record the planned→shipped mapping in the P1-22 archaeology doc exactly as P1-20 (`service.published.v1` → `service.published`) and P1-21 (`inventory.stock-reserved.v1` → `stock.reserved`) did.

verdict.reasoning:
REFUTED as a BLOCKER — the observations are accurate but the severity is wrong: an application-level composition is clearly sufficient and no migration is required.

WHAT IS TRUE (verified, quoted):
1. `schemaVersion` is a separate envelope field (`EventCatalogEntry.schemaVersion: number`, `src/server/events/envelope.ts:28`) and `shared.event_outbox.schema_version integer NOT NULL` is a separate column with `CONSTRAINT ck_event_outbox_schema_version CHECK (schema_version >= 1)` (supabase/migrations/20260718106000_shared_event_outbox.sql:90, 126).
2. `tests/foundation/p1-15-catalogs.test.ts:648-653` iterates the WHOLE catalogue: `expect(entry.eventType, `${entry.code} carries a version suffix`).not.toMatch(/\.v\d+$/);` plus `expect(entry.eventType).not.toContain('.v1');` — one suffixed entry fails the unit suite. Confirmed.
3. `EVENT_CATALOG` holds exactly 42 entries (`grep -c "^    code: 'EVT-"` = 42; `EXPECTED_EVENT_TYPES` at line 570 lists 42 names). All unsuffixed. Confirmed.
4. None of the eight names (`invoice.issued`, `payment.recorded`, `payment.allocated`, `credit-note.issued`, `receipt.reversed`, `delivery.completed`, `warranty.issued`, `warranty-claim.status.changed`) exists in EVENT_CATALOG in any spelling. The 42 registered names contain no sal/wty/billing/delivery/warranty entry at all. Confirmed ABSENT.
5. `buildEventEnvelope()` (envelope.ts:585-590) throws verbatim: `Event type "${input.eventType}" is not in the event catalog. Register it before publishing.` Confirmed.
6. The P1-11 handoff really does reserve them: `docs/phase-1/phase-1-11/phase-1-11-p1-22-backend-contract.md:43-46` — "P1-22 will publish via the existing `shared.event_outbox` (Phase 1-5). Anticipated contracts: `invoice.issued.v1` (EVT-SAL-001), `payment.recorded.v1`, `payment.allocated.v1`, `credit-note.issued.v1`, `receipt.reversed.v1`, `delivery.completed.v1`, `warranty.issued.v1`, and `warranty-claim.status.changed.v1` (EVT-WTY-001, if claims activate)." That file is the ONLY place in the repo where `EVT-SAL`/`EVT-WTY` appear.
7. Precedent is exactly as described. P1-20 block comment (envelope.ts:400-409): "The P1-10 backend contract anticipated these as `service.published.v1` ... The `.v1` suffix is NOT used ... The mapping from the planned names to these is recorded in docs/phase-1/phase-1-20/evidence/wave-1-contract-archaeology.md." P1-21 block comment (envelope.ts:~500): "The phase plan proposed `inventory.stock-reserved.v1` ... The mapping is recorded in docs/phase-1/phase-1-21/wave-1-contract-archaeology.md."

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE CLAIM:
A. "Not expressible" is OVERSTATED at the DB level. `CONSTRAINT ck_event_outbox_event_type_format CHECK (event_type ~ '^[a-z][a-z0-9_.-]{1,62}$')` (line 122-123) PERMITS a `.v1` suffix — `.` and digits are both inside the character class, and `invoice.issued.v1` (16 chars) matches. Nothing in the protected schema forbids the suffix. The only barrier is the repository's own unit-test convention, which is application-level and authored in this repo. The convention is still the right one to follow (it is uniform across P1-15/19/20/21), but it is a convention, not a schema constraint, and the archaeology doc must not claim the database forbids it.
B. The mitigation surface is wider than the claim states. Beyond `EXPECTED_EVENT_TYPES` in p1-15-catalogs.test.ts, `tests/foundation/event-envelope.test.ts` also needs work: line ~185 has a hard-coded `expect(implemented.sort()).toEqual([...])` list of every event with a non-null `implementedIn`, and lines ~290-305 have an `OWNERS_BY_PHASE` map keyed by phase (`'P1-20': ['pricing','quotation','service-catalog']`, `'P1-21': ['inventory']`) that must gain a `'P1-22'` key naming the owning modules. Also `expect(entry.code).toMatch(/^EVT-[A-Z]{3}-\d{3}$/)` — `EVT-SAL-001`, `EVT-WTY-001`, `EVT-DLV-001` all satisfy it. And `buildEventEnvelope` enforces `producer.split('.')[0] === entry.owner`, so the owner string chosen for each new entry constrains the producer id the module may use.

WHY NOT A BLOCKER: every remedial edit is a TypeScript source/test edit — appending frozen entries to the `EVENT_CATALOG` array with `schemaVersion: 1`, extending three test arrays/maps. No DDL changes, no migration 120, no modification of migrations 1-119. The outbox already accepts any regex-conformant name and already stores the version in its own column. This is a naming-convention MAPPING obligation identical to the ones P1-20 and P1-21 already discharged, and it belongs in the P1-22 archaeology doc as a documented planned-to-shipped mapping, not as a blocking contract gap.

SEPARATE FINDING THE CLAIM DOES NOT MENTION AND MUST NOT BE CONFLATED WITH IT: there IS a genuinely frozen, DB-level event vocabulary in this domain — `sal.financial_events` in supabase/migrations/20260724093000_sal_financial_events.sql carries `CONSTRAINT ck_financial_events_event_type CHECK (event_type IN ('invoice_issued', 'receipt_recorded', 'payment_allocated', 'credit_note_issued', 'receipt_reversed', 'warranty_split_recorded'))` with companion `CONSTRAINT ck_financial_events_source_type CHECK (source_type IN ('invoice','receipt','payment_allocation','credit_note','receipt_reversal'))`, `CONSTRAINT uq_financial_events_source UNIQUE (tenant_id, source_type, source_id, event_type)`, `amount numeric(18,4)`, and the provenance trigger function `sal.guard_financial_event_provenance()` which raises `sal.financial_events: no authorized % source % for event %` with `ERRCODE = 'check_violation'`. Those six snake_case values are ledger event types, are enum-locked, and WOULD require a migration to extend. They are a different concept from the outbox wire names and the P1-22 archaeology must document both separately. Note the ledger has no delivery or warranty-issuance event type at all — only `warranty_split_recorded`, which is an invoice-side payer split.
verdict.searched:
Files read in full or in part: src/server/events/envelope.ts (all 651 lines — EVENT_CATALOG, EventCatalogEntry, findEvent, buildEventEnvelope, EVENT_TYPE/AGGREGATE_TYPE/PRODUCER regexes); src/server/events/publisher.ts (publishEvent INSERT into shared.event_outbox); tests/foundation/p1-15-catalogs.test.ts lines 560-700 (EXPECTED_EVENT_TYPES, the four `describe('event catalog')` its, the no-version-suffix assertion); tests/foundation/event-envelope.test.ts lines 140-200 and 290-320 (reserved-name registry invariants, implemented list, OWNERS_BY_PHASE, producer-owner refusal, findEvent); supabase/migrations/20260718106000_shared_event_outbox.sql lines 85-130 (full column list and every CHECK/UNIQUE/FK constraint); supabase/migrations/20260724093000_sal_financial_events.sql lines 30-100 (ck_financial_events_event_type, ck_financial_events_source_type, uq_financial_events_source, guard_financial_event_provenance); docs/phase-1/phase-1-11/phase-1-11-p1-22-backend-contract.md lines 43-46.

Greps run: `grep -rl "EVENT_CATALOG" --include=*.ts .` (5 files, all inspected); `grep -rn "EXPECTED_EVENT_TYPES" --include=*.ts .` (only p1-15-catalogs.test.ts); `grep -rn "invoice.issued|payment.recorded|payment.allocated|credit-note.issued|receipt.reversed|delivery.completed|warranty.issued|warranty-claim" over src/ tests/ supabase/` (only snake_case sal.financial_events ledger hits, zero dotted outbox-style hits); `grep -rln "EVT-SAL|EVT-WTY|EVT-DLV|EVT-BIL" .` (single hit: the P1-11 handoff doc); `grep -rln "event_outbox" supabase/migrations/` (2 files); `grep -c "^    code: 'EVT-" src/server/events/envelope.ts` = 42.

Alternate hiding places checked and ruled out: a second/different catalog module under src/server/events (only envelope.ts and publisher.ts exist); a seed or SQL-side event-name registry (none — no table of registered outbox event names exists; the outbox only has the format CHECK); a generated column or DB enum type carrying versioned names (none — event_type is plain `text` with a regex CHECK); a different schema or namespace spelling of the eight names (searched free-form across src/, tests/, supabase/); a function rather than a table (checked publisher.ts and the sal.* functions in migration 20260724093000). Also verified the DB regex mathematically admits `.v1`, which is the basis for correction A. Did not run the database, migrations, or tests; repo untouched (git status shows only the pre-existing untracked docs/phase-1/phase-1-22/).

gaps.assumed: A `billing` namespace can own the invoice events.
gaps.reality: `EventCatalogEntry.owner` is enforced: `const producerModule = input.producer.split('.')[0]; if (producerModule !== entry.owner) throw new EventEnvelopeError(...)`. Whatever P1-22 writes as `owner` becomes the mandatory leading segment of every producer id. The catalogue is already inconsistent about this — some owners are DB schema short codes (`wo`, `tech`, `qms`, `veh`), others long module names (`inventory`, `quotation`, `pricing`, `service-catalog`) — so there is no single precedent to inherit, and choosing `billing` while naming the producer `sal.…` (or vice versa) makes the first publish throw at runtime rather than at build time.

gaps.assumed: Warranty claim adjudication can be built (the P1-11 handoff names `warranty-claim.status.changed.v1` and `EVT-WTY-001`, "if claims activate").
gaps.reality: ABSENT at every layer. There is NO `wty.warranty_claims` table, no claim status vocabulary, and no claim permission. The only warranty vocabulary is `ck_warranty_records_status CHECK (status IN ('issued', 'active', 'expired', 'voided', 'claimed_against'))` and the identical `ck_warranty_status_history_to_status`. The migration says so twice: "Full claim adjudication is deferred to Phase 1-22" and, in the `wty.warranty_records` table comment, "Full claim adjudication deferred to Phase 1-22." The permission catalogue holds exactly two `wty` codes — `wty.policy.manage`, `wty.warranty.issue` — and no `wty.claim.*`.
gaps.mitigation: Claim adjudication cannot be built at the application layer without a claims table, and P1-22 may create no migration. The only representable claim-adjacent act is moving a warranty record to `claimed_against` and appending the `wty.warranty_status_history` row. Record full claim adjudication (P1-OD-024) as a carried-forward obligation in the accepted limitations — as P1-21 carried D-04 — rather than half-building it or reserving an event name for a producer that cannot exist.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED — the gap is real, and a migration would genuinely be required. Every refutation avenue was closed by the DDL.

**1. No claims table under any name, in any schema.** Sweeping every `CREATE TABLE` across all 119 migrations for `claim|case|ticket|request|dispute|reimburs|adjud` returns only `wo.additional_work_requests` / `wo.additional_work_request_details` — which is `'Phase 1-9 additional-work request (P1-09-DB-042). state pending→approved|rejected|withdrawn; … A required pending or approved-unfulfilled request blocks work-order closure (B3)'`, a customer approval for extra work on an open WO, not a warranty claim entity (no warranty_record_id, no policy/coverage link). The `wty` schema contains **exactly five tables**: `wty.warranty_policies`, `wty.warranty_coverage`, `wty.warranty_records`, `wty.warranty_record_items`, `wty.warranty_status_history`. The P1-11 DB test fixture teardown (`tests/db/p1-11-helpers.ts:188-192`) deletes exactly those five and no others — independent corroboration that no sixth table exists.

**2. Not a function either.** The `wty` schema declares exactly three functions: `wty.guard_warranty_record_freeze()`, `wty.guard_warranty_record_coherence()`, and `wty.issue_warranty(p_delivery_id uuid, p_policy_id uuid, p_correlation_id uuid DEFAULT NULL, p_idempotency_key text DEFAULT NULL) RETURNS uuid`. There is no `wty.file_claim`, no `wty.adjudicate_claim`, no `wty.change_warranty_status`.

**3. Not a seed.** `supabase/seeds/` holds six files; the only `claim` token in any of them is prose in a permission comment at `04_iam_permission_catalog.sql:198` ("a payroll or warranty claim may…"). The catalogue has 100 permissions and exactly two `wty` codes — `('wty.policy.manage','wty','Manage warranty policies and coverage','medium',…)` and `('wty.warranty.issue','wty','Issue warranty records','medium',…)`. `docs/database/permission-catalog-reference.md:63-64` agrees. No `wty.claim.*` anywhere.

**4. Not a generated column or a repurposable vocabulary.** The only warranty vocabulary is `ck_warranty_records_status CHECK (status IN ('issued','active','expired','voided','claimed_against'))` (line 150) and the identical `ck_warranty_status_history_to_status` (line 306). The migration header (line 5) says "Full claim adjudication is deferred to Phase 1-22", and the table comment (line 159) repeats it verbatim — exactly as the archaeologist reports.

**5. The work-order composition escape hatch is explicitly nailed shut.** `ck_work_orders_kind CHECK (kind IN ('ordinary','rework'))`, and `src/modules/work-order/domain/work-order.ts:30` states in the frozen-vocabulary comment: "There is no `warranty` and no `internal` kind. Warranty is modelled by the `wty` schema against the closed order, not by a work-order kind". A claim cannot be smuggled in as a WO kind.

**6. The event name has no producer and no consumer.** `warranty-claim.status.changed.v1` / `EVT-WTY-001` appears in exactly one file in the repository — `docs/phase-1/phase-1-11/phase-1-11-p1-22-backend-contract.md:46` — hedged in the source itself with "(EVT-WTY-001, **if claims activate**)". The same document's own "What P1-22 owns (not built here)" section already concedes: "Full warranty **claim adjudication** (P1-OD-024) — only records + status history exist now." `src/server/events/envelope.ts` contains no warranty event type. So P1-11 did not promise claims; it reserved a name conditionally. `docs/phase-1/phase-1-11/phase-1-11-od-linkage.md:16` files P1-OD-024 as "Held / deferred", and `docs/phase-1/phase-1-12/phase-1-12-owner-gate.md:229` (WVR-P1-12-001) assigns its remediation to "warranty-claim adjudication scope (post-Release-2)" — i.e. a later phase, not P1-22.

**The one nuance the archaeologist understates (refinement, not refutation):** claim-adjacent representable acts are slightly broader than "only `claimed_against` + history". `sal.invoice_line_amounts.warranty_pay_amount numeric(18,4)` with `ck_invoice_line_amounts_payer_split CHECK (customer_pay_amount + warranty_pay_amount = gross_amount)` (FR-WTY-004) and the `sal.financial_events` event type `'warranty_split_recorded'` let the backend record who *pays*. That is warranty-payer billing, not adjudication — no claim identity, no submitted/under-review/approved/rejected states, no decision actor, no dual control.

**Two gaps the archaeologist did NOT name, which strengthen the finding:**
- **No permission covers the one act that IS representable.** `wty.warranty.issue` covers issuing. There is no `wty.warranty.void`, `wty.warranty.status.manage`, or equivalent, so moving a record to `claimed_against`/`voided`/`expired` has no permission code to authorize it. P1-22 must either overload `wty.warranty.issue` or leave the transition unauthorized at the catalogue layer — and adding a permission is a seed/migration change.
- **There is no status-transition guard at all.** `tg_warranty_records_freeze` (line 181) freezes identity and terms only — its own comment says "status may advance" — and the CHECK is a flat unordered five-value set. There is no state machine, so `expired → issued` or `voided → active` is DB-legal. The backend owns transition legality entirely, with no protected floor beneath it. Grants permit the composition (`GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON wty.warranty_records TO app_runtime`; `GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON wty.warranty_status_history TO app_runtime`), which is precisely why half-building claims here would be dangerous.

The mitigation is correct and matches the established precedent: record P1-OD-024 as a carried-forward obligation in accepted limitations, exactly as `docs/phase-1/phase-1-21/wave-1-contract-archaeology.md:223` records D-04 ("Extending the **database** guard … would require a new migration, which P1-21 is not authorized to add … Both are recorded as carried-forward obligations in the accepted limitations rather than silently dropped or silently half-built"). Do not reserve `warranty-claim.status.changed.v1` for a producer that cannot exist.

reports.lens: Upstream cross-phase ports P1-22 must consume: work-order completion/closure state and the closure-eligibility contract (wo), quotation acceptance and pricing outputs (quo/svc), inventory issue/return state for invoiceable parts (inv), and the file/evidence module for delivery signatures (shared-services). Read at feature/p1-22-billing-payment-delivery-warranty-backend = d9a2c1dc8d09e8fe2b3cf9ca8a2d4a6c905756de; 119 migrations, no migration 120, none modified.
reports.summary: Every upstream fact P1-22 needs has a legal public port, and no private import (`@/modules/<x>/<internals>`, boundary rule B1-module-internals-are-private) is forced on the critical path — but four of those ports return less than the phase plan assumes. Work-order closure is fully served: `workOrderModule().workOrders.closureEligibility()` reports B1-B6 plus the P1-21 inventory commitments, and the state graph is DATA (`wo.work_order_states`, seeded in `supabase/seeds/06_wo_job_state_graph.sql`) that must be read through `workOrderCatalog.workOrderStates()` rather than mirrored — with the trap that `is_closed` is TRUE for `cancelled` as well as `closed`, so the only honest "billable/deliverable" predicate is `isTerminal && !isCancellation`. The protected `sal`/`wty` schema enforces NOTHING about upstream state: `sal.issue_invoice`, `sal.complete_delivery` and the `sal.invoices` triggers never read `wo.work_orders.state`, `quo.quotation_revisions.status`, or any `inv` table, and `sal.invoices.quotation_revision_id` is an unguarded nullable FK — so acceptance, closure and billability are 100% application-level and must be composed from `commercialApproval()`, `closureEligibility()` and `openCommitmentsFor()`. Quotation acceptance is DERIVED per item (`quo.approval_decisions`, `rollUpDecisions`); there is no `accepted` revision status, and `commercialApproval(db, revisionId, { lock: true })` is the only acceptance truth. The largest real gaps are pricing and evidence: `svc.price_rules.service_id` is `NOT NULL` and `PriceQuery` is keyed on `serviceId` alone, so NO port anywhere prices an `inv.item_master` part; `LINKABLE_ENTITY_TYPES` has no `sal.delivery_records` entry, so a delivery-signature document cannot be linked to the delivery it evidences; and no application role can move a `shared.document_versions` row to `accepted`, so a bound signature can never be downloaded. Two P1-11 handoff claims are contradicted by the deployed DDL — the authorized-receiver "or a valid CRM authorized-person relationship" branch does not exist in `sal.guard_authorized_receiver`, and the `ready → receiver_verified → signed → delivered` ordering has no transition guard at all. Finally, `wty` has five tables and none of them is a warranty claim, while P1-11 promised "claim structures activate with the P1-22 backend" — that promise cannot be kept without a migration this phase may not create.
