NOT REFUTED. Every object the archaeologist says is missing is genuinely missing from the deployed DDL, and the decisive evidence is stronger than what they cited.

CONFIRMED, WITH THE EXACT DDL:

1. No refund anywhere. The only occurrence of the string "refund" in the entire repository is a test fixture at tests/db/iam-approvals.test.ts:156,162,169 supplying it as iam.approval_limits.limit_type, a column whose vocabulary is OPEN, not closed: `CONSTRAINT ck_approval_limits_type_format CHECK (limit_type ~ '^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,62}$')`. So a tenant can configure a monetary approval CEILING named 'refund' while no refund fact is persistable. That is a trap worth recording: seeing 'refund' in the codebase does not mean a refund object exists.

2. Partial reversal: `CONSTRAINT uq_receipt_reversals_receipt UNIQUE (tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, original_receipt_id)` and `sal.approve_receipt_reversal` lines 341-343 `IF v_rev.amount <> v_rcpt.amount THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'sal.approve_receipt_reversal: full-receipt reversal amount % must equal receipt amount %'`. But the DECISIVE point the archaeologist missed is that the BALANCE MATH IS BINARY, not the constraint: `sal.invoice_open_receivable` filters `AND r.status <> 'reversed'` and `sal.receipt_unallocated` does `IF v_amount IS NULL OR v_status = 'reversed' THEN RETURN 0`. A partial reversal has nowhere to land even if a row for it existed. That is why a migration is genuinely required and no application composition can substitute.

3. Cross-invoice credit note: `sal.credit_notes.invoice_id uuid NOT NULL` with `fk_credit_notes_invoice FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, invoice_id)`, frozen by `tg_credit_notes_immutable` (invoice_id is in the org.guard_immutable_columns allowlist). Stronger still: `sal.approve_credit_note` rejects `v_cn.amount > sal.invoice_open_receivable(v_cn.invoice_id)`, so a credit can never EXCEED one invoice's open receivable and therefore no carryable credit balance can be created in the first place.

4. Staged/progress billing: `work_order_id uuid NOT NULL` plus `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_invoices_work_order_active ON sal.invoices (tenant_id, company_id, branch_id, work_order_id) WHERE status <> 'void_before_issue' AND deleted_at IS NULL`, and `sal.guard_invoice_freeze` makes `credited` and `void_before_issue` terminal and permits only `issued -> credited`.

5. No ledger: no journal/journal-line/chart-of-accounts/period/posting-rule table exists in any of the 18 schemas. `COMMENT ON TABLE sal.financial_events` says "NOT a general ledger: no debit/credit/account columns", `ck_financial_events_event_type CHECK (event_type IN ('invoice_issued','receipt_recorded','payment_allocated','credit_note_issued','receipt_reversed','warranty_split_recorded'))` and `ck_financial_events_source_type CHECK (source_type IN ('invoice','receipt','payment_allocation','credit_note','receipt_reversal'))` are closed, and `ck_financial_events_amount CHECK (amount >= 0)` means no outflow can be expressed.

6. Payment methods: `ck_payment_methods_kind CHECK (kind IN ('cash','card_terminal','bank_transfer'))`, comment "No online payment gateway/settlement types (ASM-14, CON-04)", seeded exactly as the three platform rows in supabase/seeds/08_sal_payment_methods.sql. The complete sal permission catalogue is 10 codes (seeds/04 lines 60-70): sal.invoice.manage, sal.invoice.issue, sal.payment.record, sal.payment.allocate, sal.credit.manage, sal.reversal.approve, sal.finance.view, sal.delivery.manage, sal.delivery.complete, sal.delivery.view. No refund permission ABSENT-by-design.

THREE CORRECTIONS THE ARCHAEOLOGIST SHOULD MAKE:

A. "cross-invoice credit" is imprecise and, read broadly, is FALSE. CASH can be applied across invoices: sal.payment_allocations has NO unique constraint per receipt, and sal.allocate_receipt is bounded only by sal.receipt_unallocated and sal.invoice_open_receivable. One receipt legitimately funds many invoices, so an overpayment carried as unallocated receipt balance IS a working cross-invoice customer credit. The limits are same-branch (`AND company_id = v_rcpt.company_id AND branch_id = v_rcpt.branch_id`), same-currency (`IF v_inv.currency_code <> v_rcpt.currency_code THEN RAISE`), and invoice status IN ('issued','credited'). What is impossible is applying a CREDIT NOTE across invoices. Reword to "no cross-invoice credit-NOTE application".

B. "MITIGATION: None of these can be built" is too absolute in exactly one case. The NET RECEIVABLE POSITION after a partial refund IS composable: approve a full reversal, then sal.record_receipt for the retained amount. What is genuinely unbuildable is the refund as a recorded fact: `ck_receipts_amount CHECK (amount > 0)` forbids a negative receipt, there is no disbursement table, and no outflow event_type exists, so the cash actually leaving the till is never persisted. Two fidelity losses to state: sal.record_receipt has NO received_at parameter (the column defaults to now()) and sal.guard_receipt_freeze then freezes received_at, so the rebooked receipt permanently carries the wrong payment date; and the original allocations survive forever as append-only rows (no DELETE is granted on any sal table) merely excluded from the derivation.

C. Doc-vs-DDL divergence, DDL authoritative. docs/phase-1/phase-1-11/phase-1-11-receipt-reversal-contract.md asserts "CHECK receipt_reversals.amount = original receipt amount". THERE IS NO SUCH CHECK CONSTRAINT. The only amount check is `ck_receipt_reversals_amount CHECK (amount > 0)`. Equality lives solely in the plpgsql IF at 20260724093000_sal_financial_events.sql:341-343. Because `GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON sal.receipt_reversals TO app_runtime` includes raw UPDATE and `sal.guard_dual_control_approval` never compares amounts, a reversal row with amount <> receipt amount can be raw-approved outside the primitive. It yields no partial effect (the derivation is binary) but does emit a truthful-looking `receipt_reversed` financial event carrying a false amount, since `sal.guard_financial_event_provenance` binds the event amount to the REVERSAL row, not to the receipt. P1-22 must therefore route reversals exclusively through sal.approve_receipt_reversal and must never issue raw UPDATE on sal.receipt_reversals.approval_state.

TWO ADDITIONAL FINDINGS THAT REINFORCE THE BLOCKER:

D. The one-invoice-per-work-order guarantee has a soft-delete hole. uq_invoices_work_order_active carries `AND deleted_at IS NULL`, deleted_at is NOT in the tg_invoices_immutable allowlist ('tenant_id','company_id','branch_id','created_at','created_by' - org.guard_immutable_columns is a per-column allowlist, verified in 20260717101000_org_tenants.sql:57-74), and sal.guard_invoice_freeze never inspects deleted_at. app_runtime holds raw UPDATE on sal.invoices, so an ISSUED invoice can be soft-deleted, freeing the work-order slot for a second invoice. This is an abuse path, not a sanctioned staged-billing mechanism - using it would erase a numbered financial document. P1-22 must never write sal.invoices.deleted_at after issue, and this should be recorded as an open defect against the protected schema.

E. The warranty split has no counterparty billing document, which independently confirms that the missing second-invoice path is a real gap and not merely stylistic. `ck_invoice_line_amounts_payer_split CHECK (customer_pay_amount + warranty_pay_amount = gross_amount)` records what the warranty payer owes, and sal.issue_invoice emits `warranty_split_recorded` when the sum is positive - yet sal.invoice_open_receivable returns `round(v_gross - v_alloc - v_credit, 4)` against the FULL gross_total charged to the single `sal.invoices.payer_partner_id`, there is no warranty claim or reimbursement table in wty (only warranty_policies, warranty_coverage, warranty_records, warranty_record_items, warranty_status_history; the migration header says "Full claim adjudication is deferred to Phase 1-22" but no table was created for it), and uq_invoices_work_order_active forbids raising a separate invoice to the warranty provider. So the warranty portion is currently receivable from the customer. P1-22 must not build a warranty-reimbursement or claim-billing API, and should record this as a named contract gap.

BOTTOM LINE: refuted=false. Refund, partial reversal, cross-invoice credit-note application, staged/progress billing, gateway settlement and ledger posting each genuinely require a migration. Since P1-22 is backend-only with migrations 1-119 frozen and no migration 120 permitted, every one of them must be refused at design time and recorded as out of scope.

NOT REFUTED. The gap is real and a migration would genuinely be required.

CORE FACTS CONFIRMED, twice over (migration DDL text AND the deployed pgdelta catalog):

`wty` is exactly five tables. No claim table, view, materialized view, enum, sequence, or function exists in ANY schema across all 119 migrations. The only /claim/ relation in the deployed catalog is `auth.mfa_amr_claims`, a Supabase-managed auth artefact with no relation to warranty; the only /claim/ routine is `shared.claim_outbox_events(text, integer, interval)`, the outbox worker lease.

The entire trace of a claim is the string `'claimed_against'` in exactly two constraints:
  CONSTRAINT ck_warranty_records_status CHECK (status IN ('issued', 'active', 'expired', 'voided', 'claimed_against'))
  CONSTRAINT ck_warranty_status_history_to_status CHECK (to_status IN ('issued', 'active', 'expired', 'voided', 'claimed_against'))

`wty.warranty_status_history` is the whole available persistence surface, and its full column list is: id uuid, tenant_id uuid, company_id uuid, branch_id uuid, warranty_record_id uuid, from_status text NULL, to_status text NOT NULL, reason text NULL, correlation_id uuid NULL, actor_id uuid NOT NULL, occurred_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), seq bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY. There is no claimant, no claim amount, no decision, no approver, no claim number, no claim date distinct from occurred_at. Note `reason` is NULLABLE here (unlike `shared.status_history.reason`, which is NOT NULL) — so the schema does not even force a textual justification.

The transition itself IS mechanically possible: `GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON wty.warranty_records TO app_runtime` with `upd_warranty_records_scope`, and `wty.guard_warranty_record_freeze()` freezes only vehicle_id/work_order_id/delivery_record_id/policy_id/coverage_id/start_date/expiry_date/odometer_at_issue/odometer_limit — its comment says "identity + terms immutable; status may advance". `GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON wty.warranty_status_history TO app_runtime` with `tg_warranty_status_history_stamp` server-stamping actor_id/occurred_at. So "record that a warranty was claimed against" is buildable; "adjudicate a claim" is not.

EVERY GENERIC COMPOSITION SURFACE IS CLOSED — I checked each one specifically because that was the strongest refutation path:
  - `shared.status_history` + `shared.status_evidence` (which carries evidence_type/evidence_ref/note and would have been a natural claim-evidence home): app_runtime has SELECT only. The migration states it outright — "Deliberately ABSENT: INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE for both roles on both tables." UNUSABLE.
  - `shared.notes` (entity_type/entity_id polymorphic, body text): the only runtime INSERT path is `ins_notes_crm_customer`, whose WITH CHECK pins `entity_type = 'crm.business_partners'` AND requires an EXISTS against `crm.business_partners`. A note CANNOT be authored against a warranty record. UNUSABLE.
  - `iam.approval_limits`: an effective-dated limit table (limit_type/amount, gist no-overlap). There is no approval-REQUEST table anywhere; every approval object in the schema (`wo.customer_approvals`, `quo.approval_decisions`, `svc.pricing_approval_policies`) is FK-pinned to its own domain. UNUSABLE.
  - `sal.financial_events`: doubly closed. `ck_financial_events_event_type CHECK (event_type IN ('invoice_issued','receipt_recorded','payment_allocated','credit_note_issued','receipt_reversed','warranty_split_recorded'))` AND `ck_financial_events_source_type CHECK (source_type IN ('invoice','receipt','payment_allocation','credit_note','receipt_reversal'))`, plus `sal.guard_financial_event_provenance()` which has an IF/ELSIF branch per event_type and RAISEs 'no authorized % source % for event %' when none matches. Even if a claim row existed, no source_type value could name it. The archaeologist understated this — source_type is closed too.
  - `shared.document_links` is the ONE partial surface they missed: `ins_document_links_scoped` allows app_runtime INSERT under `iam.has_permission_in_scope('shared.document.manage', d.company_id, d.branch_id)` with `entity_type` constrained only by format `'^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$'`, so a claim FORM could legitimately be attached as a document to `entity_type = 'wty.warranty_records'`. That is an opaque file reference with no queryable claim state, no amount, no decision. It mitigates evidence capture, not adjudication.

THREE CORRECTIONS to the archaeologist's supporting reasoning (none change the verdict, but the write-up should not assert them as schema blocks):
  1. "no claim audit action" — `iam.audit_records.action` is constrained ONLY by `ck_audit_records_action_not_blank CHECK (btrim(action) <> '')`. Audit actions are free text, application-defined throughout this codebase. This is not a closed vocabulary and is not evidence of a gap.
  2. Outbox event types are NOT schema-constrained either: `ck_event_outbox_event_type_format CHECK (event_type ~ '^[a-z][a-z0-9_.-]{1,62}$')`. `warranty-claim.status.changed` (29 chars) is publishable today — app_runtime holds `GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON shared.event_outbox` with `ins_event_outbox_producer` since migration 20260725090000. The registry in `src/server/events/envelope.ts` is a TypeScript array, not DDL.
  3. A permission code is NOT migration-gated: codes live in `supabase/seeds/04_iam_permission_catalog.sql`, and backend phases have added them there — `69d749e feat(p1-20): seed the commercial read permissions`, `08544ca feat(p1-21): expose the inventory API surface and register its catalogs`. So "`wty.claim.*` does not exist" is true today but is a seed edit, not a schema change. (It is also worth noting there is no `wty.warranty.read` or `wty.warranty.view` code at all — wty RLS is scope-only, with no permission predicate on any of the five tables.)

But `sal.invoice_line_amounts` has NO foreign key to `wty.warranty_records`, `wty.warranty_policies`, or `wty.warranty_coverage`. The schema can say "the warranty pays 300.0000 of this line" and CANNOT say WHICH warranty. So even the money side cannot be reconciled to a claim without new DDL.

ALSO WORTH CARRYING FORWARD (adjacent, not part of this claim): there is no status-transition-legality guard on `wty.warranty_records` at all — no `wty.transition_warranty_status` function exists, and nothing prevents `'voided' -> 'claimed_against'` or `'expired' -> 'active'`. Transition legality is entirely a P1-22 backend responsibility, unlike the DB-enforced graphs in `wo`/`apt`.

FINALLY, THE DDL-VS-PROSE DIVERGENCE, which should be raised as a finding in the archaeology record: `docs/phase-1/phase-1-11/phase-1-11-warranty-record-contract.md` lines 37-38 assert "the `…claimed_against` status is prepared so a later claim links to the record without schema change." Per the P1-21 wave-1 rule, the DDL is authoritative and the handoff prose is wrong. VERDICT: submit/adjudicate/approve/reject-a-warranty-claim must be declared OUT OF SCOPE for P1-22 and carried as an accepted limitation in the manner of P1-21 D-04. What P1-22 CAN legitimately build without a migration: (a) transition `wty.warranty_records.status` to `'claimed_against'` with a `wty.warranty_status_history` row carrying `reason` and `correlation_id`, under a new seed-added permission code, with transition legality enforced in application code; (b) attach a claim form via `shared.document_links` with `entity_type = 'wty.warranty_records'` under `shared.document.manage`; (c) publish a `warranty-claim.status.changed` outbox event. The `wty` schema contains **exactly five tables**: `wty.warranty_policies`, `wty.warranty_coverage`, `wty.warranty_records`, `wty.warranty_record_items`, `wty.warranty_status_history`. The P1-11 DB test fixture teardown (`tests/db/p1-11-helpers.ts:188-192`) deletes exactly those five and no others — independent corroboration that no sixth table exists.

**2. Not a function either.** The `wty` schema declares exactly three functions: `wty.guard_warranty_record_freeze()`, `wty.guard_warranty_record_coherence()`, and `wty.issue_warranty(p_delivery_id uuid, p_policy_id uuid, p_correlation_id uuid DEFAULT NULL, p_idempotency_key text DEFAULT NULL) RETURNS uuid`. There is no `wty.file_claim`, no `wty.adjudicate_claim`, no `wty.change_warranty_status`.

**3. Not a seed.** `supabase/seeds/` holds six files; the only `claim` token in any of them is prose in a permission comment at `04_iam_permission_catalog.sql:198` ("a payroll or warranty claim may…"). The catalogue has 100 permissions and exactly two `wty` codes — `('wty.policy.manage','wty','Manage warranty policies and coverage','medium',…)` and `('wty.warranty.issue','wty','Issue warranty records','medium',…)`. `docs/database/permission-catalog-reference.md:63-64` agrees. No `wty.claim.*` anywhere.

**4. Not a generated column or a repurposable vocabulary.** The only warranty vocabulary is `ck_warranty_records_status CHECK (status IN ('issued','active','expired','voided','claimed_against'))` (line 150) and the identical `ck_warranty_status_history_to_status` (line 306). The migration header (line 5) says "Full claim adjudication is deferred to Phase 1-22", and the table comment (line 159) repeats it verbatim — exactly as the archaeologist reports.

**5. The work-order composition escape hatch is explicitly nailed shut.** `ck_work_orders_kind CHECK (kind IN ('ordinary','rework'))`, and `src/modules/work-order/domain/work-order.ts:30` states in the frozen-vocabulary comment: "There is no `warranty` and no `internal` kind. Warranty is modelled by the `wty` schema against the closed order, not by a work-order kind". A claim cannot be smuggled in as a WO kind.

**6. The event name has no producer and no consumer.** `warranty-claim.status.changed.v1` / `EVT-WTY-001` appears in exactly one file in the repository — `docs/phase-1/phase-1-11/phase-1-11-p1-22-backend-contract.md:46` — hedged in the source itself with "(EVT-WTY-001, **if claims activate**)". The same document's own "What P1-22 owns (not built here)" section already concedes: "Full warranty **claim adjudication** (P1-OD-024) — only records + status history exist now." `src/server/events/envelope.ts` contains no warranty event type. So P1-11 did not promise claims; it reserved a name conditionally. `docs/phase-1/phase-1-11/phase-1-11-od-linkage.md:16` files P1-OD-024 as "Held / deferred", and `docs/phase-1/phase-1-12/phase-1-12-owner-gate.md:229` (WVR-P1-12-001) assigns its remediation to "warranty-claim adjudication scope (post-Release-2)" — i.e. a later phase, not P1-22.

**The one nuance the archaeologist understates (refinement, not refutation):** claim-adjacent representable acts are slightly broader than "only `claimed_against` + history". `sal.invoice_line_amounts.warranty_pay_amount numeric(18,4)` with `ck_invoice_line_amounts_payer_split CHECK (customer_pay_amount + warranty_pay_amount = gross_amount)` (FR-WTY-004) and the `sal.financial_events` event type `'warranty_split_recorded'` let the backend record who *pays*. That is warranty-payer billing, not adjudication — no claim identity, no submitted/under-review/approved/rejected states, no decision actor, no dual control.

**Two gaps the archaeologist did NOT name, which strengthen the finding:**
- **No permission covers the one act that IS representable.** `wty.warranty.issue` covers issuing. There is no `wty.warranty.void`, `wty.warranty.status.manage`, or equivalent, so moving a record to `claimed_against`/`voided`/`expired` has no permission code to authorize it. P1-22 must either overload `wty.warranty.issue` or leave the transition unauthorized at the catalogue layer — and adding a permission is a seed/migration change.
- **There is no status-transition guard at all.** `tg_warranty_records_freeze` (line 181) freezes identity and terms only — its own comment says "status may advance" — and the CHECK is a flat unordered five-value set. There is no state machine, so `expired → issued` or `voided → active` is DB-legal. The backend owns transition legality entirely, with no protected floor beneath it. Grants permit the composition (`GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON wty.warranty_records TO app_runtime`; `GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON wty.warranty_status_history TO app_runtime`), which is precisely why half-building claims here would be dangerous.

The mitigation is correct and matches the established precedent: record P1-OD-024 as a carried-forward obligation in accepted limitations, exactly as `docs/phase-1/phase-1-21/wave-1-contract-archaeology.md:223` records D-04 ("Extending the **database** guard … would require a new migration, which P1-21 is not authorized to add … Both are recorded as carried-forward obligations in the accepted limitations rather than silently dropped or silently half-built"). Do not reserve `warranty-claim.status.changed.v1` for a producer that cannot exist.

verdict.reasoning:
NOT REFUTED — the gap is real. A warranty claim cannot be persisted without a new table, and P1-22 may create no migration. Two refinements to the claim are warranted (one mitigation the archaeologist missed, plus four additional gaps that make the finding stronger).

=== 1. The five-table inventory is exact ===
`supabase/migrations/20260724095000_wty_warranty.sql` (361 lines) is the ONLY file in the repo that creates anything in the `wty` schema (`grep -rn "CREATE TABLE wty\." supabase/` returns 5 hits, all in this file, at lines 20, 63, 117, 236, 288): `wty.warranty_policies`, `wty.warranty_coverage`, `wty.warranty_records`, `wty.warranty_record_items`, `wty.warranty_status_history`. `docs/phase-1/phase-1-11/phase-1-11-data-dictionary-wty.md` lists exactly the same five headings.

The only three `wty` functions are `wty.guard_warranty_record_freeze()` (line 169), `wty.guard_warranty_record_coherence()` (line 193), and `wty.issue_warranty(p_delivery_id uuid, p_policy_id uuid, p_correlation_id uuid DEFAULT NULL, p_idempotency_key text DEFAULT NULL) RETURNS uuid` (line 327). There is no claim-shaped function, no view, no materialized view anywhere in `supabase/migrations/`, and no generated column other than `seq bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY` on the history table.

Cross-checked against the DEPLOYED catalog snapshot `supabase/.temp/pgdelta/catalog-local-migrations-2d15e803…-1785261654495.json`: `grep -o "warranty_[a-z_]*"` yields exactly five relation names (warranty_policies, warranty_coverage, warranty_records, warranty_record_items, warranty_status_history) plus their constraints/indexes/triggers. The only other hits are `warranty_pay_amount` (a `sal.invoice_line_amounts` column) and `warranty_split_recorded` (a `sal.financial_events` event type) — neither is a claim.

=== 2. The quoted vocabularies are correct ===
Line 150: `CONSTRAINT ck_warranty_records_status CHECK (status IN ('issued', 'active', 'expired', 'voided', 'claimed_against'))`.
Line 306: `CONSTRAINT ck_warranty_status_history_to_status CHECK (to_status IN ('issued', 'active', 'expired', 'voided', 'claimed_against'))`.
`wty.warranty_status_history` columns: `id uuid`, `tenant_id uuid`, `company_id uuid`, `branch_id uuid`, `warranty_record_id uuid`, `from_status text NULL`, `to_status text NOT NULL`, `reason text NULL`, `correlation_id uuid NULL`, `actor_id uuid NOT NULL`, `occurred_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()`, `seq bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY`. Grants: `GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON wty.warranty_status_history TO app_runtime` — append-only, no UPDATE/DELETE. The archaeologist is right that `reason text NULL` is the only free-text surface.

=== 3. Every generic-composition escape route is CLOSED — this is the decisive test ===
The strongest refutation candidates are the polymorphic `shared.*` tables, whose `entity_type` is only format-checked (`ck_notes_entity_type_format CHECK (entity_type ~ '^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$')`), so `'wty.warranty_records'` would pass the CHECK. They fail on PRIVILEGE and POLICY, not on the CHECK:

- `shared.notes` — `GRANT SELECT ON shared.notes TO app_runtime, app_readonly` (20260718110000 line 410). Migration 20260730090000 (the newest, 119th) DOES add `GRANT INSERT (id, tenant_id, entity_type, entity_id, author_id, body, classification, visibility, created_by) ON shared.notes TO app_runtime` — but its only INSERT policy `ins_notes_crm_customer` contains `AND entity_type = 'crm.business_partners'`. RLS is ENABLEd and FORCEd, and no other INSERT policy exists, so a note with `entity_type = 'wty.warranty_records'` is rejected. That migration's own header says it out loud: "A future module that needs to annotate its own entities adds its own scoped policy" — i.e. a migration.
- `shared.comments` — `GRANT SELECT ... TO app_runtime, app_readonly` only (line 411). No INSERT grant, no INSERT policy, anywhere.
- `shared.status_history` / `shared.status_evidence` — `GRANT SELECT ... TO app_runtime, app_readonly` only (20260718096000 lines 136-137). Migration 20260728090000 lines 61-68 withholds them DELIBERATELY and explains why: "NOT granted to any application role… Granting INSERT would create a transition log forgeable inside a tenant." So the generic status ledger cannot carry a claim lifecycle either.
- `rec.complaints` / `rec.complaint_details` — real tables, but `reception_visit_id uuid NOT NULL` with `fk_complaints_visit` to `rec.reception_visits`, `ck_complaints_category CHECK (category IN ('mechanical','electrical','body','noise','performance','other'))`, and NO column referencing a warranty record. A claim forced through here would require inventing a reception visit and would be unlinkable to the warranty except by an un-FK'd shared `correlation_id`.
- `wo.work_orders` — `ck_work_orders_kind CHECK (kind IN ('ordinary', 'rework'))`. There is no warranty kind, and the existing backend already documents this at `src/modules/work-order/domain/work-order.ts:30`: "There is no `warranty` and no `internal` kind. Warranty is modelled by the `wty` schema against the closed order, not by a work-order kind."
- No claim numbering: `supabase/seeds/` seeds ZERO `shared.number_sequences` rows, so no claim sequence code exists (nor could be invented without seeding).

=== 4. CORRECTION to the claim: "MITIGATION: None" is overstated in exactly one respect ===
`shared.document_links` IS usable. Migration 20260728090000 lines 130-134 grants `INSERT (id, tenant_id, document_id, entity_type, entity_id, link_purpose, linked_by, created_by)` and `UPDATE (deleted_at)` to `app_runtime`, and policy `ins_document_links_scoped` (line 263) does NOT constrain `entity_type` — it gates only on `tenant_id = iam.current_tenant_id() AND linked_by = iam.current_user_id() AND created_by = iam.current_user_id()` plus `iam.has_permission_in_scope('shared.document.manage', d.company_id, d.branch_id)`. `ck_document_links_entity_type_format` admits `'wty.warranty_records'` and `ck_document_links_purpose_format CHECK (link_purpose ~ '^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,62}$')` admits an arbitrary purpose token. So CLAIM EVIDENCE (a document) CAN be attached to a warranty record with no migration. Caveat: `shared.file_scan_results` is granted to NO role, and that migration records the consequence honestly — "no scanner exists in this phase, so a document version cannot reach `accepted`" — so evidence stays pre-acceptance. This mitigation covers evidence only; it provides no claim identity, no claimant, no decision, and no lifecycle.

=== 5. Four ADDITIONAL gaps found that make the finding worse, not better ===
(a) NO CLAIM PERMISSION EXISTS. `supabase/seeds/04_iam_permission_catalog.sql` lines 72-73 contain the ONLY two `wty.*` codes in the system: `('wty.policy.manage', 'wty', 'Manage warranty policies and coverage', 'medium', …)` and `('wty.warranty.issue', 'wty', 'Issue warranty records', 'medium', …)`. There is no `wty.claim.*`, no adjudication code, and not even a status-change code. Worse: `upd_warranty_records_scope` (line 223) carries NO `iam.has_permission` predicate at all — only tenant/company/branch scope — so at the DB layer a move to `'claimed_against'` is authorized by nothing but scope. P1-22 must gate it in application code against a permission that does not exist in the catalog.
(b) NO STATUS-TRANSITION GUARD. The only triggers on `wty.warranty_records` are `tg_warranty_records_freeze` (BEFORE UPDATE, terms only), `tg_warranty_records_touch_metadata`, `tg_warranty_records_immutable` ('tenant_id','company_id','branch_id','created_at','created_by'), and `tg_warranty_records_coherence` (BEFORE INSERT). Nothing constrains status→status: `'voided'` → `'active'` or `'expired'` → `'issued'` are both accepted by the database. The entire warranty state machine is an unenforced P1-22 responsibility.
(c) THE DOCUMENTED CORRECTION PATH IS UNIMPLEMENTABLE. `wty.guard_warranty_record_freeze` raises `'wty.warranty_records: an issued warranty record''s terms are frozen (corrections via a linked record)'` — but `wty.warranty_records` has NO self-referencing column (contrast `rec.complaints.correction_of` with `fk_complaints_correction_of`). There is nothing to link a corrective record by.
(d) HANDOFF PROSE CONTRADICTS THE DDL (DDL authoritative). `docs/phase-1/phase-1-11/phase-1-11-warranty-record-contract.md:37-38`: "Claim structures activate with the P1-22 backend; the `…claimed_against` status is prepared so a later claim links to the record without schema change." The DDL refutes "without schema change" — there is no claim entity to link FROM, and creating one is precisely a schema change. Same optimism at `phase-1-11-design.md:213-214` and `phase-1-11-od-linkage.md:16`. By contrast `phase-1-11-p1-22-backend-contract.md:39` is accurate ("Full warranty **claim adjudication** (P1-OD-024) — only records + status history exist now") and line 46 hedges correctly: `warranty-claim.status.changed.v1` (EVT-WTY-001) is listed only "if claims activate".

=== VERDICT ===
refuted = false. Recording, adjudicating and tracking a warranty claim requires a new table; there is no table, function, view, generated column, seed, or writable generic surface that can hold a claim number, claimant, defect description, adjudication decision, or claim-to-work-order link. P1-22's accepted limitation should be stated as: the phase can move a `wty.warranty_records` row to `'claimed_against'` and append one `wty.warranty_status_history` row carrying `reason`/`correlation_id`, and may attach evidence documents via `shared.document_links`; it must NOT ship any endpoint whose name implies claim storage or adjudication. The P1-11 "without schema change" prose should be raised as a divergence finding.
